## Introduction

[Our shaykh, the imam, Shaykh al-Islām, sovereign of the eminent scholars, hadith master of the age and its dictating scholar, bearer of the banner of the Sunna therein, imam of those who assess transmitters and those who compile hadith: Abū al-Faḍl Shihāb al-Dīn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī al-Shāfiʿī—may God preserve him in goodness and well-being—said:]

Praise be to God, who has numbered everything, who raised some of His creatures above others so that they became groups following diverse ways. I bear witness that there is no deity but God alone, without partner. He has taken neither consort nor child; He has never had a partner in dominion, nor ever shall. And I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and messenger, His chosen one and intimate friend. How noble a servant and master he is, and how great a beloved one, divinely aided! How pure his root and ancestry, how pure his resting place and birthplace, and how noble his Companions, who were stars of guidance and imams to be followed. May God bless him and them with an everlasting blessing and grant them perpetual peace [and fullest peace].

To proceed: among the noblest of the religious sciences is the science of Prophetic hadith, and among its most eminent branches of knowledge is distinguishing the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ from those who came after them.

A number of hadith masters compiled works on that subject, each according to the extent of the material that came within his knowledge. The earliest person I know to have composed on it was Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Bukhārī, who devoted an independent work to it, from which Abū al-Qāsim al-Baghawī and others transmit. A group from the generation of al-Bukhārī's teachers assembled the names of the Companions together with those who came after them, including Khalīfa ibn Khayyāṭ and Muḥammad ibn Saʿd; among his contemporaries were Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān and Abū Bakr ibn [Abī] Khaythama. After them, a number composed works on the subject, including Abū al-Qāsim al-Baghawī, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Dāwūd, and ʿAbdān; a little before them there was Muṭayyan; then came Abū ʿAlī ibn al-Sakan, Abū Ḥafṣ ibn Shāhīn, Abū Manṣūr al-Māwardī, Abū Ḥātim Ibn Ḥibbān, and al-Ṭabarānī in his Great Lexicon; then Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Manda and Abū Nuʿaym; then Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, who called his book al-Istīʿāb because he believed he had encompassed the contents of the books before his. Despite that, much escaped him. Abū Bakr ibn Fatḥūn therefore appended to it a substantial supplement, while a number of others appended smaller works. Abū Mūsā al-Madīnī also wrote a large supplement to Ibn Manda.

In the eras of these scholars there were innumerable other people who also wrote on the subject. Then, in the early seventh century, ʿIzz al-Dīn ibn al-Athīr compiled a substantial book that he called Usd al-Ghāba, bringing together in it much of the earlier literature. Yet he followed his predecessors: he mingled persons who were not Companions among the Companions and often failed to call attention to the many errors in their books. The hadith master Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Dhahabī then extracted the names in Ibn al-Athīr's book, adding others, and marked those who had been included in error and those whose Companionship was unsound; but he did not make this exhaustive, or nearly so.

Through continued investigation I encountered many names that were in neither his book nor its source, according to the criteria of both. I therefore compiled a large book on the subject, in which I distinguished the Companions from others. Yet all of that has not enabled us to identify even a tenth of the Companions' names in comparison with what is reported from Abū Zurʿa al-Rāzī. He said: When the Prophet ﷺ died, the men and women who had seen him and heard from him numbered more than one hundred thousand; every one of them had transmitted from him by hearing or sight.

After citing that, Ibn Fatḥūn said in his supplement to al-Istīʿāb: Abū Zurʿa gave this answer to someone who had asked him specifically about transmitters, so what of those who did not transmit? Even so, everyone in al-Istīʿāb—that is, everyone mentioned in it by name or by kunya—numbers three thousand five hundred. He stated that he had added, according to Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's criteria, nearly as many as Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr himself had mentioned.

I say: in the hand of the hadith master al-Dhahabī, on the back of his book al-Tajrīd, I read: 'Perhaps the total is eight thousand—no fewer, if not more.' I later saw in his hand that the total number in Usd al-Ghāba is seven thousand five hundred [and fifty-four persons].

Further support for Abū Zurʿa's statement is what is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from Kaʿb ibn Mālik in the account of Tabūk: 'The people were so numerous that no register could enumerate them.'

It is also established from al-Thawrī, in a report transmitted by al-Khaṭīb with a sound chain to him, that he said: 'Whoever gives ʿAlī precedence over ʿUthmān has disparaged twelve thousand men when the Messenger of God ﷺ died while pleased with them.' Al-Nawawī said: This was twelve years after the Prophet ﷺ, after many whose names were never recorded had died during the caliphate of Abū Bakr in the wars of apostasy and the conquests; and then, during the caliphate of ʿUmar, uncountably many died in the conquests, the general plague, the plague of ʿAmwās, and otherwise.

The reason their names remained obscure is that most of them were Bedouins, and most attended the Farewell Pilgrimage. والله أعلم.

A group of brethren repeatedly asked me to prepare a fair copy of the book. I therefore sought God's guidance in the matter and arranged it in four divisions under each letter:

The first division contains anyone whose Companionship is reported through a transmission from him or from another, whether its chain is sound, fair, or weak, as well as anyone mentioned in any manner that indicates Companionship.

At first I arranged this one division as three divisions. I later decided to make it a single division and to distinguish the relevant status within each biography.

The second division contains those listed among the Companions who were children born during the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime to male or female Companions and who were below the age of discernment when he ﷺ died. Their inclusion among the Companions is only by way of affiliation, because it is overwhelmingly likely that he ﷺ saw them: his Companions had every reason to bring their newborn children to him so that he might perform taḥnīk for them, name them, and invoke blessing upon them. Reports of this are numerous and well known. In the Ṣaḥīḥ of Muslim, through Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, it is related that children used to be brought to the Prophet ﷺ and he would invoke blessing upon them.

Al-Ḥākim transmitted in the Book of Tribulations in al-Mustadrak, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who said: 'Whenever a child was born to anyone, the child was brought to the Prophet ﵌ and he prayed for the child'—to the end of the hadith. Ibn Shāhīn transmitted in the Book of the Companions, in the biography of Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa ibn ʿAbd Allāh, through Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the client of Abū Ṭalḥa, from the wet nurse of Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa, who said: 'When Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa was born, I brought him to the Prophet ﷺ so that he might perform taḥnīk for him and pray for him; this was likewise what he did for children.' The hadiths these people transmit from him, however, are classed as mursal by rigorous scholars of hadith. I therefore separated them from the people of the first division.

The third division contains those listed in the aforementioned books from among the mukhaḍrams—people who lived in both the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods—when no report ever states that they met the Prophet ﷺ or saw him, whether they embraced Islam during his lifetime or not. By consensus of hadith scholars, these are not his Companions. Although some compilers included some of them in books identifying the Companions, those compilers expressly stated that they mentioned them only because of their proximity to that generation, not because they belonged to it.

Among those who expressly stated this was Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, and before him Abū Ḥafṣ ibn Shāhīn, who excused his inclusion of a biography of the Negus on the ground that the Negus affirmed the Prophet ﷺ during his lifetime, among other considerations. Had persons of this kind counted as Companions in his view, he would have needed no excuse.

Anyone who has categorically attributed to Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr the view that they were Companions is mistaken. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's reason for mentioning them is clear in the introduction to his book and accords with what we have explained. By consensus of hadith scholars, the hadiths these persons relate from the Prophet ﷺ are mursal; Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr himself explicitly stated this in al-Tamhīd and elsewhere in his books.

The fourth division contains those included in the aforementioned books through misconception or error. I explain this with the clear demonstration relied upon according to the methods of hadith scholars. I include only cases in which the error is manifest. Where it remains possible that there was no error, I do not include the person unless that possibility is probably invalid.

I know of no predecessor who devised this fourth division or whose thought even circled around it. It is the sought-after lost treasure in this splendid field and the choicest product that the discerning expert can extract from this discipline.

I ask God Most High to assist in completing it, to make it sincerely for His noble countenance, and to reward me through it with the best reward in the abode of His bounty. He is near and responsive.

Before beginning the aforementioned divisions, I shall mention important chapters needed in this field.

**( مقدمة )**

[ قال شيخنا الإمام شيخ الإسلام ، ملك العلماء الأعلام ، حافظ العصر وممليه ، وحامل لواء السنة فيه ، إمام المعدلين والمخرجين : أبو الفضل شهاب الدين أحمد بن علي بن محمد ابن محمد بن علي بن أحمد بن حجر العسقلاني الشافعي ، أبقاه الله في خير وعافية ] :

الحمد لله الذي أحصى كل شيء عددا ، ورفع بعض خلقه على بعض ، فكانوا طرائق قددا . وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، لم يتخذ صاحبة ولا ولدا ، ولم يكن له شريك في الملك ولا يكون أبدا ؛ وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله وصفيه وخليله ، أكرم به عبدا سيدا ، وأعظم به حبيبا مؤيدا ؛ فما أزكاه أصلا ومحتدا ، وأطهره مضجعا ومولدا ، وأكرمه أصحابا ، كانوا نجوم الاهتداء ، وأئمة الاقتداء ؛ صلى الله عليه وعليهم صلاة خالدة ، وسلاما مؤبدا [ وسلم تسليما ] .

أما بعد ؛ فإن من أشرف العلوم الدينية علم الحديث النبوي ، ومن أجل معارفه تمييز أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ممن خلف بعدهم .

وقد جمع في ذلك جمع من الحفاظ تصانيف بحسب ما وصل إليه اطلاع كل منهم ؛ فأول من عرفته صنف في ذلك أبو عبد الله البخاري ؛ أفرد في ذلك تصنيفا ؛ ينقل منه أبو القاسم البغوي وغيره ، وجمع أسماء الصحابة مضموما إلى من بعدهم جماعة من طبقة مشايخه ؛ كخليفة بن خياط ، ومحمد بن سعد ، ومن قرنائه كيعقوب ابن سفيان ، وأبي بكر بن [ أبي ] خيثمة ، وصنف في ذلك جمع بعدهم كأبي القاسم البغوي ، وأبي بكر بن أبي داود ، وعبدان ؛ ومن قبلهم بقليل كمطين ، ثم كأبي علي بن السكن ، وأبي حفص بن شاهين ، وأبي منصور الماوردي ، وأبي حاتم ابن حبان ، وكالطبراني ضمن معجمه الكبير ، ثم كأبي عبد الله بن منده ، وأبي نعيم ؛ ثم كأبي عمر بن عبد البر ، وسمى كتابه الاستيعاب ؛ لظنه أنه استوعب ما في كتب من قبله ؛ ومع ذلك ففاته شيء كثير ؛ فذيل عليه أبو بكر بن فتحون ذيلا حافلا ، وذيل عليه جماعة في تصانيف لطيفة ، وذيل أبو موسى المديني على ابن منده ذيلا كبيرا .

وفي أعصار هؤلاء خلائق يتعسر حصرهم ممن صنف في ذلك أيضا إلى أن كان في أوائل القرن السابع ، فجمع عز الدين بن الأثير كتابا حافلا سماه ' أسد الغابة ' جمع فيه كثيرا من التصانيف المتقدمة ، إلا أنه تبع من قبله : فخلط من ليس صحابيا بهم ، وأغفل كثيرا من التنبيه على كثير من الأوهام الواقعة في كتبهم ؛ ثم جرد الأسماء التي في كتابه مع زيادات عليها الحافظ أبو عبد الله الذهبي ، وعلم لمن ذكر غلطا ولمن لا تصح صحبته ؛ ولم يستوعب ذلك ولا قارب .

وقد وقع لي بالتتبع كثير من الأسماء التي ليست في كتابه ، ولا أصله على شرطهما ؛ فجعت كتابا كبيرا في ذلك ميزت فيه الصحابة من غيرهم ؛ ومع ذلك فلم يحصل لنا من ذلك جميعا الوقوف على العشر من أسامي الصحابة بالنسبة إلى ما جاء عن أبي زرعة الرازي ؛ قال : توفي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن رآه وسمع منه زيادة على مائة ألف إنسان من رجل وامرأة ، كلهم قد روى عنه سماعا أو رؤية .

قال ابن فتحون في ذيل ' الاستيعاب ' - بعد أن ذكر ذلك : أجاب أبو زرعة بهذا سؤال من سأله عن الرواة خاصة ، فكيف بغيرهم ؟ ومع هذا فجميع من في الاستيعاب - يعني ممن ذكر فيه باسم أو كنية ، وهما ثلاثة آلاف وخمسمائة ؛ وذكر أنه استدرك عليه على شرطه قريبا ممن ذكره .

قلت : وقرأت بخط الحافظ الذهبي من ظهر كتابه ' التجريد ' : لعل الجميع ثمانية آلاف إن لم يزيدوا لم ينقصوا ؛ ثم رأيت بخطه أن جميع من في ' أسد الغابة ' سبعة آلاف وخمسمائة [ وأربعة وخمسون نفسا ] .

ومما يؤيد قولي أبي زرعة ما ثبت في الصحيحين عن كعب بن مالك في قصة تبوك : والناس كثير لا يحصيهم ديوان .

وثبت عن الثوري فيما أخرجه الخطيب بسنده الصحيح إليه ، قال : من قدم عليا على عثمان فقد أزرى على اثني عشر ألفا مات رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو عنهم راض ؛ فقال النووي : وذلك بعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم باثني عشر عاما بعد أن مات في خلافة أبي بكر في الردة والفتوح - الكثير ممن لم يضبط أسماؤهم ؛ ثم مات في خلافة عمر في الفتوح وفي الطاعون العام وعمواس وغير ذلك من لا يحصي كثرة .

وسبب خفاء أسمائهم أن أكثرهم أعراب ، وأكثرهم حضروا حجة الوداع . والله أعلم .

وقد كثر سؤال جماعة من الإخوان في تبييضه ، فاستخرت الله تعالى في ذلك ، ورتبته على أربعة أقسام في كل حرف منه :

فالقسم الأول - فيمن وردت صحبته بطريق الرواية عنه أو عن غيره ، سواء كانت الطريق صحيحة أو حسنة أو ضعيفة ، أو وقع ذكره بما يدل على الصحبة بأي طريق كان .

وقد كنت أولا رتبت هذا القسم الواحد على ثلاثة أقسام ، ثم بدا لي أن أجعله قسما واحدا . وأميز ذلك في كل ترجمة .

القسم الثاني - من ذكر في الصحابة من الأطفال الذين ولدوا في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لبعض الصحابة من النساء والرجال ، ممن مات صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في دون سن التمييز ؛ إذ ذكر أولئك في الصحابة ، إنما هو على سبيل الإلحاق : لغلبة الظن على أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم رآهم لتوفر دواعي أصحابه على إحضارهم أولادهم عنده عند ولادتهم ليحنكهم ويسميهم ويبرك عليهم ؛ والأخبار بذلك كثيرة شهيرة : ففي صحيح مسلم من طريق هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يؤتى بالصبيان فيبرك عليهم .

وأخرجه الحاكم في كتاب الفتن في المستدرك عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال : ما كان يولد لأحد مولود إلا أتي به النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فدعا له - الحديث . وأخرج ابن شاهين في كتاب الصحابة في ترجمة محمد بن طلحة بن عبد الله من طريق محمد بن عبد الرحمن مولى أبي طلحة عن ظئر محمد بن طلحة ، قال : لما ولد محمد ابن طلحة أتيت به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليحنكه ويدعو له ، وكذلك كان يفعل بالصبيان ؛ لكن أحاديث هؤلاء عنه من قبيل المراسيل عند المحققين من أهل العلم بالحديث ؛ ولذلك أفردتهم عن أهل القسم الأول .

القسم الثالث - فيمن ذكر في الكتب المذكورة من المخضرمين الذين أدركوا الجاهلية والإسلام ، ولم يرد في خبر قط أنهم اجتمعوا بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، ولا رأوه ، سواء أسلموا في حياته أم لا ؛ وهؤلاء ليسوا أصحابه باتفاق أهل العلم بالحديث ، وإن كان بعضهم قد ذكر بعضهم في كتب معرفة الصحابة فقد أفصحوا بأنهم لم يذكروهم إلا بمقاربتهم لتلك الطبقة ، لا أنهم من أهلها .

وممن أفصح بذلك ابن عبد البر ، وقبله أبو حفص بن شاهين ، فاعتذر عن إخراجه ترجمة النجاشي بأنه صدق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حياته وغير ذلك ، ولو كان من هذا سبيله يدخل عنده في الصحابة ما احتاج إلى اعتذار .

وغلط من جزم في نقله عن ابن عبد البر بأنه يقول بأنهم صحابة ؛ بل مراد ابن عبد البر بذكرهم واضح في مقدمة كتابه بنحو مما قررناه ، وأحاديث هؤلاء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مرسلة بالاتفاق بين أهل العلم بالحديث ؛ وقد صرح ابن عبد البر نفسه بذلك في التمهيد وغيره من كتبه .

القسم الرابع - فيمن ذكر في الكتب المذكورة على سبيل الوهم والغلط ؛ وبيان ذلك البيان الظاهر الذي يعول عليه على طرائق أهل الحديث ، ولم أذكر فيه إلا ما كان الوهم فيه بينا . وأما مع احتمال عدم الوهم فلا ، إلا إن كان ذلك الاحتمال يغلب على الظن بطلانه .

وهذا القسم الرابع لا أعلم من سبقني إليه ، ولا من حام طائر فكره عليه ؛ وهو الضالة المطلوبة في هذا الباب الزاهر ، وزبدة ما يمخضه [ من هذا ] الفن اللبيب الماهر .

والله تعالى أسأل أن يعين على إكماله ، وأن يجعله خالصا لوجهه الكريم ، ويجازيني به خير الجزاء في دار إفضاله ؛ إنه قريب مجيب .

وقبل الشروع في الأقسام المذكورة أذكر فصولا مهمة يحتاج إليها في هذا النوع .

</div>

## Chapter One: Definition of a Companion

The soundest definition I have encountered is [that] a Companion is someone who met the Prophet ﷺ while believing in him and died as a Muslim. This includes anyone who met him, whether the person's association with him was long or brief; anyone who transmitted from him or did not; anyone who campaigned with him or did not; anyone who saw him even without sitting in his company; and anyone who did not see him because of an impediment such as blindness.

The qualification concerning faith excludes a person who met him while an unbeliever and later embraced Islam if that person did not meet him again.

Our phrase 'in him' excludes a person who met him while believing in someone other than him, such as a believer from among the People of the Book who met him before the prophetic mission. Whether one of those people who met him and believed that he would be sent as a prophet is included remains open to consideration. Among these were the monk Baḥīrā and others like him.

Our phrase 'while believing in him' includes every morally responsible being among jinn and humankind. It is therefore necessary to mention those believing jinn whose accounts have been preserved and who meet the stated condition. Ibn al-Athīr's objection to Abū Mūsā for including in his Book of the Companions some jinn who were known is not a valid objection, for the reason I have given.

Ibn Ḥazm said in the Book of Adjudications in al-Muḥallā: 'Whoever claims consensus has lied about the community, for God Most High has informed us that a group of jinn believed and heard the Qur'an from the Prophet ﷺ. They are therefore virtuous Companions. How, then, could one who claims consensus know the view of those jinn?'

We do not agree with what he said there concerning the question of consensus; my purpose was only to transmit his statement that they are Companions.

Are the angels included? This requires examination. Some have said that the question depends on whether he was sent to them. Imam Fakhr al-Dīn transmitted in Asrār al-Tanzīl a consensus that he ﷺ was not sent to the angels. That claimed consensus has been disputed; Shaykh Taqī al-Dīn al-Subkī instead deemed it more likely that he was sent to them and adduced several arguments whose explanation would take too long. The soundness of making this question depend upon that premise is itself plainly open to examination.

Our phrase 'and died as a Muslim' excludes a person who met him while believing in him, then apostatized and died in apostasy—God protect us. A small number of such cases occurred. One was ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh, the husband of Umm Ḥabība: he embraced Islam with her and emigrated to Abyssinia, but then became a Christian and died as one. Another was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khaṭal, who was killed while clinging to the curtains of the Kaʿba. Another was Rabīʿa ibn Umayya ibn Khalaf, whose account I shall explain in his biography in the fourth division under the letter rāʾ.

The definition does include anyone who apostatized and then returned to Islam before dying, whether or not that person met him ﷺ a second time. This is the sound, relied-upon view.

There is no disagreement that the first of those two cases is included. Some have suggested a possible exclusion in the second case, but this is refuted by the hadith scholars' agreement in counting al-Ashʿath ibn Qays among the Companions and transmitting his hadiths in the Ṣaḥīḥ collections and Musnads. He was among those who apostatized and then returned to Islam during the caliphate of Abū Bakr.

This definition is based on the sounder view chosen by the critical scholars, including al-Bukhārī, his teacher Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, and those who followed them. Beyond it are other, anomalous positions. One holds that a person is counted as a Companion only if characterized by one of four attributes: lengthy association with him, preserved transmission from him, a verified record of campaigning with him, or martyrdom in his presence. Likewise anomalous are the positions requiring attainment of puberty for Companionship to be valid, or requiring association with him even if brief.

A number of scholars have stated without qualification that whoever saw the Prophet ﷺ was a Companion. This must be understood as referring to someone who had reached the age of discernment, because sight cannot properly be attributed to one who lacked discernment. It may indeed be said that the Prophet ﷺ saw such a child, making the child a Companion from that perspective, while from the perspective of transmission the child is a Successor. Is someone included who saw him after his death but before burial, as is reported of the poet Abū Dhuʾayb al-Hudhalī? If the report is sound, this requires examination; the stronger view is that such a person is not included.

Among the general statements of the imams about criteria by which a man may be known as a Companion even in the absence of an explicit designation is what Ibn Abī Shayba related in his Muṣannaf through an acceptable chain: during the conquests they appointed none but Companions as commanders. There is also Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's statement that by the year ten there was no one left in Mecca or al-Ṭāʾif who had not embraced Islam and attended the Farewell Pilgrimage with the Prophet ﷺ. Similar is what some have said of the Aws and the Khazraj: by the end of the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime, none remained who had not entered Islam, and when the Prophet ﷺ died none among them openly professed unbelief. والله أعلم.

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

**( الفصل الأول في تعريف الصحابي )**

وأصح ما وقفت عليه من ذلك [ أن ] الصحابي من لقي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مؤمنا به ، ومات على الإسلام ؛ فيدخل فيمن لقيه من طالت مجالسته له أو قصرت ، ومن روى عنه أو لم يرو ، ومن غزا معه أو لم يغز ، ومن رآه رؤية ولو لم يجالسه ، ومن لم يره لعارض كالعمى .

ويخرج بقيد الإيمان من لقيه كافرا ولو أسلم بعد ذلك إذا لم يجتمع به مرة أخرى .

وقولنا : ' به ' يخرج من لقيه مؤمنا بغيره ، كمن لقيه من مؤمني أهل الكتاب قبل البعثة . وهل يدخل من لقيه منهم وآمن بأنه سيبعث أو لا يدخل ؟ محل احتمال . ومن هؤلاء بحيرا الراهب ونظراؤه .

ويدخل في قولنا : ' مؤمنا به ' كل مكلف من الجن والإنس ؛ فحينئذ يتعين ذكر من حفظ ذكره من الجن الذين آمنوا به بالشرط المذكور ، وأما إنكار ابن الأثير على أبي موسى تخريجه لبعض الجن الذين عرفوا في كتاب الصحابة فليس بمنكر لما ذكرته .

وقد قال ابن حزم في كتاب الأقضية من المحلى : من ادعى الإجماع فقد كذب على الأمة ؛ فإن الله تعالى قد أعلمنا أن نفرا من الجن آمنوا وسمعوا القرآن من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ؛ فهم صحابة فضلاء ؛ فمن أين للمدعي إجماع أولئك ؟

وهذا الذي ذكره في مسألة الإجماع لا نوافقه عليه ؛ وإنما أردت نقل كلامه في كونهم صحابة .

وهل تدخل الملائكة ؟ محل نظر ؛ قد قال بعضهم : إن ذلك ينبني على أنه هل كان مبعوثا إليهم أو لا ؟ وقد نقل الإمام فخر الدين في أسرار التنزيل الإجماع على أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يكن مرسلا إلى الملائكة . ونوزع في هذا النقل ؛ بل رجح الشيخ تقي الدين السبكي أنه كان مرسلا إليهم . واحتج بأشياء يطول شرحها . وفي صحة بناء هذه المسألة على هذا الأصل نظر لا يخفى .

وخرج بقولنا : ' ومات على الإسلام ' من لقيه مؤمنا به ثم ارتد ، ومات على ردته والعياذ بالله . وقد وجد من ذلك عدد يسير ؛ كعبيد الله بن جحش الذي كان زوج أم حبيبة ؛ فإنه أسلم معها ، وهاجر إلى الحبشة ، فتنصر هو ومات على نصرانيته . وكعبد الله بن خطل الذي قتل وهو متعلق بأستار الكعبة ، وكربيعة بن أمية ابن خلف على ما سأشرح خبره في ترجمته في القسم الرابع من حرف الراء .

ويدخل فيه من ارتد وعاد إلى الإسلام قبل أن يموت ، سواء اجتمع به صلى الله عليه وسلم مرة أخرى أم لا ؛ وهذا هو الصحيح المعتمد .

والشق الأول لا خلاف في دخوله وأبدى بعضهم في الشق الثاني احتمالا ؛ وهو مردود لإطباق أهل الحديث على عد الأشعث بن قيس في الصحابة ، وعلى تخريج أحاديثه في الصحاح والمسانيد ؛ وهو ممن ارتد ثم عاد إلى الإسلام في خلافة أبي بكر .

وهذا التعريف مبني على الأصح المختار عند المحققين ؛ كالبخاري ، وشيخه أحمد ابن حنبل ، ومن تبعهما ؛ ووراء ذلك أقوال أخرى شاذة : كقول من قال : لا يعد صحابيا إلا من وصف بأحد أوصاف أربعة : من طالت مجالسته ، أو حفظت روايته ، أو ضبط أنه غزا معه ، أو استشهد بين يديه ؛ وكذا من اشترط في صحة الصحبة بلوغ الحلم ، أو المجالسة ولو قصرت .

وأطلق جماعة أن من رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهو صحابي . وهو محمول على من بلغ سن التمييز ؛ إذ من لم يميز لا تصح نسبة الرؤية إليه . نعم يصدق إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رآه فيكون صحابيا من هذه الحيثية ، ومن حيث الرواية يكون تابعيا ؛ وهل يدخل من رآه ميتا قبل أن يدفن كما وقع ذلك لأبي ذؤيب الهذلي الشاعر ؟ إن صح محل نظر . والراجح عدم الدخول . ومما جاء عن الأئمة من الأقوال المجملة في الصفة التي يعرف بها كون الرجل صحابيا وإن لم يرد التنصيص على ذلك - ما أورده ابن أبي شيبة في مصنفه من طريق لا بأس به ، أنهم كانوا في الفتوح لا يؤمرون إلا الصحابة . وقول ابن عبد البر : لم يبق بمكة ولا الطائف أحد في سنة عشر إلا أسلم ، وشهد مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حجة الوداع . ومثل ذلك قول بعضهم في الأوس والخزرج : إنه لم يبق منهم في آخر عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا من دخل في الإسلام ، وما مات النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأحد منهم يظهر الكفر . والله أعلم .

</div>

## Chapter Two: Means of Establishing That a Person Was a Companion

This is established in several ways. First, it may be established by mass transmission that the person was a Companion; next, by widespread transmission and renown; next, through a report from an individual Companion that a certain person possessed Companionship, for example. The same applies to a report from an individual Successor, on the basis that accreditation by a single person is accepted, which is the stronger view. Finally, the person himself may say, provided his uprightness and contemporaneity are established, 'I am a Companion.'

As for the first condition, uprightness, al-Āmidī and others stated it categorically. Before the person's uprightness is established, accepting his statement 'I am a Companion,' or its equivalent, would entail establishing his uprightness, because all Companions are upright. It would thus be equivalent to someone's saying, 'I am upright,' which is not accepted.

As for the second condition, contemporaneity, it is assessed by the passage of one hundred and ten years from the Hijra of the Prophet ﷺ, because he ﷺ said to his Companions near the end of his life: 'Consider this night of yours: at the end of one hundred years from it, no one who is on the face of the earth today will remain.' Al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmitted it from Ibn ʿUmar. Muslim added, in the hadith of Jābir, that this occurred one month before his ﷺ death. Its wording is: 'I heard the Prophet ﷺ say one month before he died: By God, no living soul upon the earth today will still be alive one hundred years from now.'

For this reason, the imams did not believe anyone who claimed Companionship after that limit. A number of people made the claim and were declared liars. The last of them was Ratan al-Hindī, as we shall mention in the biographies of all of them in the fourth division, because their claims were evidently false according to the principle I have established.

The preceding statement of al-Āmidī and those who followed him entails that the Companionship of a person whose circumstances are known only through his own statement is not established. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn al-Qaṭṭān reported disagreement on the question and deemed non-establishment the stronger view. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, however, categorically accepted such a claim on the basis that the apparent presumption is the person's freedom from discredit. He reinforced this by pointing to the hadith imams' practice of including the hadiths of such people in their Musnads. There can be no doubt that someone known by this route ranks below those discussed previously.

One form of this case is that a Successor says, 'So-and-so informed me [for example] that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say ...,' whether or not he names that person. But if he says, 'A man informed me, for example, from the Prophet ﷺ that ...,' establishing Companionship from this is unlikely because an omitted intermediary remains possible. A distinction may perhaps be drawn: if the speaker is a senior Successor, acceptance is more likely; if a junior Successor, rejection is more likely. Even so, compilers of works on the Companions did not refrain from including persons known by this route in their books. والله أعلم.

A criterion: knowledge of this principle establishes the Companionship of a large group for whom a description implying that they were Companions is sufficient. It is derived from three reports.

The first: Ibn Abī Shayba transmitted through a chain that 'they appointed none but Companions as commanders during military campaigns.' Anyone who traces the reports about the wars of apostasy and the conquests will find many such people. They belong to the first division.

The second: al-Ḥākim transmitted in the hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf that whenever a child was born to anyone, the child was brought to the Prophet ﷺ and he prayed for the child. Many people may likewise be identified from this, and they belong to the second division.

[The third]: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr transmitted through a chain that 'by the year ten, no one remained in Mecca or al-Ṭāʾif who had not embraced Islam and attended the Farewell Pilgrimage.' They were, in fact, too numerous to count. An individual among them can nevertheless be recognized through evidence that the person was alive at that time, and is then attached to the first or second division because they saw the Prophet ﷺ, even if he did not see them. والله أعلم.

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

**( الفصل الثاني في الطريق إلى معرفة كون الشخص صحابيا )**

وذلك بأشياء : أولها أن يثبت بطريق التواتر أنه صحابي ، ثم بالاستفاضة والشهرة ، ثم بأن يروى عن آحاد من الصحابة أن فلانا له صحبة مثلا ؛ وكذا عن آحاد التابعين ، بناء على قبول التزكية من واحد ؛ وهو الراجح ثم بأن يقول هو إذا كان ثابت العدالة والمعاصرة : أنا صحابي .

أما الشرط الأول - وهو العدالة - فجزم به الآمدي وغيره ؛ لأن قوله قبل أن تثبت عدالته : أنا صحابي أو ما يقوم مقام ذلك - يلزم من قبو قوله إثبات عدالته ؛ لأن الصحابة كلهم عدول ، فيصير بمنزلة قول القائل : أنا عدل ؛ وذلك لا يقبل .

وأما الشرط الثاني - وهو المعاصرة - فيعتبر بمضي مائة سنة وعشر سنين من هجرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ؛ لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في آخر عمره لأصحابه : أرأيتكم ليلتكم هذه ، فإن على رأس مائة سنة منها لا يبقى على وجه الأرض ممن هو اليوم عليها أحد ' . رواه البخاري ، ومسلم من حديث ابن عمر . زاد مسلم من حديث جابر أن ذلك كان قبل موته صلى الله عليه وسلم بشهر . ولفظه : سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول قبل أن يموت بشهر : ' أقسم بالله ، ما على الأرض من نفس منفوسة اليوم يأتي عليها مائة سنة وهي حية يومئذ ' .

ولهذه النكتة لم يصدق الأئمة أحدا ادعى الصحبة بعد الغاية المذكورة . وقد ادعاها جماعة فكذبوا ؛ وكان آخرهم رتن الهندي على ما سنذكر تراجمهم كلهم في القسم الرابع ؛ لأن الظاهر كذبهم في دعواهم على ما قررته .

ثم من لم يعرف حاله إلا من جهة نفسه فمقتضى كلام الآمدي الذي سبق ومن تبعه ألا تثبت صحبته . ونقل أبو الحسن بن القطان فيه الخلاف ورجح عدم الثبوت . وأما ابن عبد البر فجزم بالقبول بناء على أن الظاهر سلامته من الجرح ، وقوى ذلك بتصرف أئمة الحديث في تخريجهم أحاديث هذا الضرب في مسانيدهم . ولا ريب في انحطاط رتبة من هذا سبيله عمن مضى . ومن صور هذا الضرب أن يقول التابعي : أخبرني فلان [ مثلا ] أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول ، سواء أسماه أم لا . أما إذا قال أخبرني رجل ، مثلا ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بكذا فثبوت الصحبة بذلك بعيد ؛ لاحتمال الإرسال . ويحتمل التفرقة بين أن يكون القائل من كبار التابعين ، فيرجح القبول ، أو صغارهم فيرجح الرد . ومع ذلك فلم يتوقف من صنف في الصحابة في إخراج من هذا سبيله في كتبهم . والله أعلم .

ضابط : يستفاد من معرفته صحبة جمع كثير يكتفى فيهم بوصف يتضمن أنهم صحابة ؛ وهو مأخوذ من ثلاثة آثار : الأول : أخرج ابن أبي شيبة من طريق قال : كانوا لا يؤمرون في المغازي إلا الصحابة ؛ فمن تتبع الأخبار الواردة في الردة والفتوح وجد من ذلك شيئا كثيرا ؛ وهم من القسم الأول .

الثاني : أخرج الحاكم من حديث عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال : كان لا يولد لأحد مولود إلا أتى به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فدعا له ؛ وهذا يؤخذ منه شيء كثير أيضا ، وهم من القسم الثاني .

[ الثالث ] : وأخرج ابن عبد البر من طريق قال : لم يبق بمكة والطائف أحد في سنة عشر إلا أسلم ، وشهد حجة الوداع . هذا وهم في نفس الأمر عدد لا يحصون ؛ لكن يعرف الواحد منهم بوجود ما يقتضي أنه كان في ذلك الوقت موجودا ، فيلحق بالقسم الأول أو الثاني لحصول رؤيتهم بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن لم يرهم هو . والله أعلم .

</div>

## Chapter Three: The Uprightness of the Companions

The People of the Sunna agree that all the Companions are upright; none have dissented except anomalous adherents of innovation. Al-Khaṭīb included an excellent chapter on this in al-Kifāya. He said: The uprightness of the Companions is established and known through God's declaration of their uprightness, His report of their purity, and His choosing them. Among the evidence is His statement, Most High: 'You are the best community brought forth for humankind'; His statement: 'Thus We made you a middle community'; His statement: 'God was certainly pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you beneath the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts'; His statement: 'The first forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers and those who followed them with excellence—رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه (“God is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him”)'; His statement: 'O Prophet, God is sufficient for you and for the believers who follow you'; and His statement: '[A share is] for the poor Emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their property, seeking bounty and good pleasure from God and supporting God and His Messenger. It is they who are truthful ...' through His statement: 'You are indeed Most Kind, Most Merciful.' There are many verses whose citation would take too long and famous hadiths too numerous to enumerate. All of this makes their uprightness certain, and after God's declaration that a Companion is upright, that Companion needs no declaration from any created being.

Indeed, even had nothing of what we have mentioned come from God and His Messenger concerning them, the state in which they lived—their emigration and struggle, their support of Islam, their sacrifice of lives and property, their fighting against fathers and sons, their sincere counsel in religion, and the strength of their faith and certainty—would itself require certainty of their uprightness, belief in their moral purity, and recognition that they were better than all who succeeded them, including every accreditor who came after them.

This is the doctrine of all authoritative scholars.

Al-Khaṭīb then transmitted with his chain to Abū Zurʿa al-Rāzī, who said: 'If you see a man disparaging any of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ, know that he is a heretic. The Messenger is true, the Qur'an is true, and what he brought is true. The Companions conveyed all of it to us. These people wish to discredit our witnesses in order to invalidate the Book and the Sunna. They themselves are more deserving of discredit: they are heretics.' End of quotation.

The hadiths concerning the excellence of the Companions are numerous. Among the clearest for our purpose is what al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Ḥibbān transmitted in his Ṣaḥīḥ from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'God! God! Concerning my Companions: do not make them targets. Whoever loves them does so out of love for me; whoever hates them does so out of hatred for me. Whoever harms them has harmed me; whoever harms me has harmed God; and whoever harms God is soon to be seized by Him.'

Abū Muḥammad ibn Ḥazm said: All the Companions are categorically among the people of Paradise. God Most High said: 'Those among you who spent and fought before the victory are not equal to those who did so afterward. They are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterward, though God has promised the best reward to all.' And He, Most High, said: 'Those for whom the best reward has already gone forth from Us will be kept far away from it.' It is thus established that they are all among the people of Paradise and that none of them will enter the Fire, because they are the people addressed by the preceding verse.

It may be objected: qualifying the statement by spending and fighting excludes anyone not characterized by them. Likewise, the qualification 'with excellence' in the earlier verse—His statement, Most High, 'The first forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers and those who followed them with excellence'—excludes anyone not characterized by it, although that verse is among the clearest evidence for the intended point. For this reason al-Māzirī said in his commentary on al-Burhān: 'When we say that the Companions are upright, we do not mean everyone who saw him ﵌ on some day, visited him on a rare occasion, or met him for a purpose and soon departed. We mean those who remained with him, supported and aided him, and followed the light sent down with him; it is they who are successful.' End of quotation.

The answer is that the stated qualifications describe what was generally the case; the intended class includes everyone characterized by spending and fighting either actually or potentially. Al-Māzirī's statement was not accepted; rather, a number of distinguished scholars objected to it. Shaykh Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn al-ʿAlāʾī said: 'It is an anomalous position that would exclude from the judgment of uprightness many people famous for Companionship and transmission, such as Wāʾil ibn Ḥujr, Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayrith, ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ, and others who came to him ﷺ as delegations, remained only briefly, and departed. It would likewise exclude those Bedouins of the tribes who are known only through transmission of a single hadith, when the length of their stay is unknown. The general application is what the majority explicitly affirmed, and it is the authoritative view. والله سبحانه وتعالى أعلم.'

Veneration for the Companions, even when their meeting with him ﷺ had been brief, was an established principle among the Rightly Guided Caliphs and others. One example is what I read in the Book of Reports about the Khārijites, composed by Muḥammad ibn Qudāma al-Marwazī, in the handwriting of someone who heard it from him in the year 247. It said: ʿAlī ibn al-Jaʿd related to us; Zuhayr—meaning al-Juʿfī—related to us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Nubayḥ al-ʿAnazī, who said: 'I was with Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī.'

I also recited it in Damascus to Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad al-Murādī, from Zaynab bint al-Kamāl by audition, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Qumayra by authorization, from Shuhda al-Kātiba by audition. She said: al-Ḥusayn ibn Aḥmad ibn Ṭalḥa informed us; Abū ʿUmar ibn Mahdī informed us; Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaʿqūb related to us; my grandfather Yaʿqūb ibn Shayba related to us; Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd al-Qazwīnī, Abū Saʿīd, related to us; Abū Khaythama Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiya al-Juʿfī related to us, from al-Aswad—meaning Ibn Qays—from Nubayḥ—meaning al-ʿAnazī—from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said:

'We were with him while he was reclining. We mentioned ʿAlī and Muʿāwiya, and a man spoke abusively of Muʿāwiya. Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī sat upright and then said: We used to travel in separate companies with the Messenger of God ﷺ. We were in a company that included Abū Bakr, and we stopped among the people of some dwellings. Among them was a pregnant woman, and with us was a Bedouin man. He said to the pregnant woman, Would you like to give birth to a boy? She said, Yes. He said, If you give me a sheep, you will give birth to a boy. She gave it to him, and he recited rhymed phrases for her. He then went to the sheep, slaughtered and cooked it, and we sat eating from it, with Abū Bakr among us. When he learned what had happened, he stood and vomited everything he had eaten.

'I later saw that Bedouin brought before ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb because he had satirized the Helpers. ʿUmar said to them: Were it not that he had Companionship with the Messenger of God ﷺ, I do not know what he would have suffered for it—you would have dealt with him for me. But he has Companionship with the Messenger of God ﷺ.'

This is the wording of ʿAlī ibn al-Jaʿd. The men in this hadith are trustworthy. ʿUmar ﵁ refrained from reproaching the man, let alone punishing him, because he knew that the man had met the Prophet ﷺ.

This is the clearest testimony that they believed nothing equaled the distinction of Companionship. It is likewise established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that he ﷺ said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend in gold the like of Mount Uḥud, he would not attain one mudd given by one of them, nor even half of it.'

It is mass-transmitted from him ﷺ that he said: 'The best people are my generation, then those who follow them.'

Bahz ibn Ḥakīm related from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ: 'You complete the number of seventy communities; you are the best and most honored of them before الله عز وجل (God, Mighty and Majestic).'

Al-Bazzār transmitted in his Musnad, through a chain whose men are deemed trustworthy, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, from Jābir, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'God chose my Companions above the two weighty races—humankind and jinn—apart from the prophets and messengers.'

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hāshim al-Ṭūsī said: Wakīʿ related to us; he said: I heard Sufyān say concerning God's statement, Most High, 'Say: Praise be to God, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen': 'They are the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ.' Reports on this subject are exceedingly numerous, so let us limit ourselves to this amount; it is sufficient.

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

**( الفصل الثالث في بيان حال الصحابة من العدالة )**

اتفق أهل السنة على أن الجميع عدول ، ولم يخالف في ذلك إلا شذوذ من المبتدعة ، وقد ذكر الخطيب في ' الكفاية ' فصلا نفيسا في ذلك ، فقال : عدالة الصحابة ثابتة معلومة بتعديل الله لهم ، وإخباره عن طهارتهم ، واختياره لهم ؛ فمن ذلك قوله تعالى : ^ ( كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس ) ^ ، وقوله : ^ ( وكذلك جعلناكم أمة وسطا ) ^ . وقوله : ^ ( لقد رضي الله عن المؤمنين إذ يبايعونك تحت الشجرة فعلم ما في قلوبهم ) ^ . وقوله : ^ ( والسابقون الأولون من المهاجرين والأنصار والذين اتبعوهم بإحسان رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه ) ^ وقوله : ^ ( يا أيها النبي حسبك الله ومن اتبعك من المؤمنين ) ^ وقوله : ^ ( للفقراء المهاجرين الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم وأموالهم يبتغون فضلا من الله ورضوانا ، وينصرون الله ورسوله أولئك هم الصادقون . . . ) ^ إلى قوله : ^ ( إنك رءوف رحيم ) ^ - في آيات كثيرة يطول ذكرها ، وأحاديث شهيرة يكثر تعدادها ؛ وجميع ذلك يقتضي القطع بتعديلهم ، ولا يحتاج أحد منهم مع تعديل الله له إلى تعديل أحد من الخلق ؛ على أنه لو لم يرد من الله ورسوله فيهم شيء مما ذكرناه لأوجبت الحال التي كانوا عليها من الهجرة والجهاد . ونصرة الإسلام ، وبذل المهج والأموال ، وقتل الآباء والأبناء . والمناصحة في الدين ، وقوة الإيمان واليقين - القطع على تعديلهم ، والاعتقاد لنزاهتهم ، وأنهم أفضل من جميع الخالفين بعدهم ، والمعدلين الذين يجيئون من بعدهم .

هذا مذهب كافة العلماء ، ومن يعتمد قوله .

ثم روى بسنده إلى أبي زرعة الرازي ، قال : إذا رأيت الرجل ينتقص أحدا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاعلم أنه زنديق ؛ وذلك أن الرسول حق ، والقرآن حق ، وما جاء به حق ؛ وإنما أدى إلينا ذلك كله الصحابة ؛ وهؤلاء يريدون أن يجرحوا شهودنا ليبطلوا الكتاب والسنة ، والجرح بهم أولى ، وهم زنادقة . انتهى .

والأحاديث الواردة في تفضيل الصحابة كثيرة ؛ من أدلها على المقصود ما رواه الترمذي وابن حبان في صحيحه ، من حديث عبد الله بن مغفل . قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' الله الله في أصحابي لا تتخذوهم غرضا ، فمن أحبهم فبحبي أحبهم ، ومن أبغضهم فببغضي أبغضهم ، ومن آذاهم فقد آذاني ، ومن آذاني فقد آذى الله ، ومن آذى الله فيوشك أن يأخذه ' .

وقال أبو محمد بن حزم : الصحابة كلهم من أهل الجنة قطعا ؛ قال الله تعالى : ^ ( لا يستوي منكم من أنفق من قبل الفتح وقاتل أولئك أعظم درجة من الذين أنفقوا من بعد وقاتلوا وكلا وعد الله الحسنى ) ^ وقال تعالى : ^ ( إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون ) ^ : فثبت أن الجميع من أهل الجنة ، وأنه لا يدخل أحد منهم النار ، لأنهم المخاطبون بالآية السابقة .

فإن قيل : التقييد بالإنفاق والقتال يخرج من لم يتصف بذلك ، وكذلك التقييد بالإحسان في الآية السابقة ؛ وهي قوله تعالى : ^ ( والسابقون الأولون من المهاجرين والأنصار والذين اتبعوهم بإحسان ) ^ الآية - يخرج من لم يتصف بذلك ؛ وهي من أصرح ما ورد في المقصود ؛ ولهذا قال المازري في شرح البرهان : لسنا نعني بقولنا : الصحابة عدول - كل من رآه صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله وسلم يوما ما ، أو زاره لماما ، أو اجتمع به لغرض وانصرف عن كثب ، وإنما نعني به الدين لازموه وعزروه ونصروه ، واتبعوا النور الذي أنزل معه أولئك هم المفلحون . انتهى .

والجواب عن ذلك أن التقييدات المذكورة خرجت مخرج الغالب ، وإلا فالمراد من اتصف بالإنفاق والقتال بالفعل أو القوة . وأما كلام المازري فلم يوافق عليه ؛ بل اعترضه جماعة من الفضلاء . وقال الشيخ صلاح الدين العلائي : هو قول غريب يخرج كثيرا من المشهورين بالصحبة والرواية عن الحكم بالعدالة : كوائل بن حجر ، ومالك بن الحويرث ، وعثمان بن أبي العاص ، وغيرهم ؛ ممن وفد عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم ، ولم يقم عنده إلا قليلا وانصرف ؛ وكذلك من لم يعرف إلا برواية الحديث الواحد ، ولم يعرف مقدار إقامته من أعراب القبائل ، والقول بالتعميم هو الذي صرح به الجمهور ، وهو المعتبر ، والله سبحانه وتعالى أعلم .

وقد كان تعظيم الصحابة - ولو كان اجتماعهم به صلى الله عليه وسلم قليلا - مقررا عند الخلفاء الراشدين وغيرهم ؛ فمن ذلك ما قرأت في كتاب أخبار الخوارج تأليف محمد ابن قدامة المروزي بخط بعض من سمعه منه في سنة سبع وأربعين ومائتين ، قال : حدثنا علي بن الجعد ، حدثنا زهير - هو الجعفي ، عن الأسود بن قيس بن نبيح العنزي ، قال : كنت عند أبي سعيد الخدري ، وقرأت على أبي الحسن علي بن أحمد المرادي بدمشق ، عن زينب بنت الكمال سماعا ، عن يحيى بن القميرة ، إجازة ، عن شهدة الكاتبة سماعا قالت : أخبرنا الحسين بن أحمد بن طلحة ، أخبرنا أبو عمر بن مهدي ، حدثنا محمد بن أحمد بن يعقوب ، حدثنا جدي يعقوب بن شيبة . حدثنا محمد بن سعيد القزويني أبو سعيد ، حدثنا أبو خيثمة زهير بن معاوية الجعفي ، عن الأسود - يعني ابن قيس ، عن نبيح - يعني العنزي ، عن أبي سعيد الخدري ، قال : كنا عنده وهو متكئ . فذكرنا عليا ومعاوية ، فتناول رجل معاوية ، فاستوى أبو سعيد الخدري جالسا ، ثم قال : كنا ننزل رفاقا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فكنا في رفقة فيها أبو بكر ، فنزلنا على أهل أبيات ، وفيهم امرأة حبلى ، ومعنا رجل من أهل البادية ، فقال للمرأة الحامل : أيسرك أن تلدي غلاما ؟ قالت : نعم , قال : إن أعطيتني شاة ولدت غلاما . فأعطته . فسجع لها أسجاعا ، ثم عمد إلى الشاة فذبحها وطبخها ، وجلسنا نأكل منها ، ومعنا أبو بكر ؛ فلما علم بالقصة قام فتقيأ كل شيء أكل . قال : ثم رأيت ذلك البدوي أتى به عمر بن الخطاب وقد هجا الأنصار ؛ فقال لهم عمر : لولا أن له صحبة من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أدري ما نال فيها لكفيتموه ، ولكن له صحبة من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم .

لفظ علي بن الجعد : ورجال هذا الحديث ثقات ؛ وقد توقف عمر رضي الله عنه عن معاتبته فضلا عن معاقبته لكونه علم أنه لقي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم .

وفي ذلك أبين شاهد على أنهم كانوا يعتقدون أن شأن الصحبة لا يعد له شيء . كما ثبت في الصحيحين عن أبي سعيد الخدري من قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' والذي نفسي بيده لو أنفق أحدكم مثل أحد ذهبا ما أدرك مد أحدهم ولا نصيفه .

وتواتر عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله : ' خير الناس قرني ثم الذين يلونهم ' .

قال بهز بن حكيم ، عن أبيه ، عن جده . عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' أنتم توفون سبعين أمة أنتم خيرها وأكرمها على الله عز وجل ' .

وروى البزار في مسنده بسند رجاله موثقون من حديث سعيد بن المسيب ، عن جابر ، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' إن الله اختار أصحابي على الثقلين سوى النبيين والمرسلين ' .

وقال عبد الله بن هاشم الطوسي : حدثنا وكيع ، قال : سمعت سفيان يقول في قوله تعالى : ^ ( قل الحمد لله وسلام على عباده الذين اصطفى ) ^ - قال : هم أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والأخبار في هذا كثيرة جدا فلنقتصر على هذا القدر ففيه مقنع .

### A Useful Note

The seven Companions who issued the most legal opinions in absolute terms were ʿUmar, ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Zayd ibn Thābit, and ʿĀʾisha—may the good pleasure of God Most High be upon them all.

Ibn Ḥazm said: The legal opinions of each one of these could be collected into a large volume. He said: They are followed by twenty: Abū Bakr, ʿUthmān, Abū Mūsā, Muʿādh, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, Abū Hurayra, Anas, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, Salmān, Jābir, Abū Saʿīd, Ṭalḥa, al-Zubayr, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, Abū Bakra, ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit, Muʿāwiya, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Umm Salama. He said: The legal opinions of each one of them could be collected into a small fascicle.

He said: Among the Companions are approximately one hundred and twenty persons who issued very few legal opinions. No more than one, two, or three questions are transmitted from any one of them. After investigation, all of their legal opinions could be collected into a small fascicle. They include Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Abū Ṭalḥa, al-Miqdād, and others [and he listed the rest].

I say: In the biography of each person whom Ibn Ḥazm mentioned in this category, I shall note that Ibn Ḥazm counted that person among the jurists of the Companions, for this is one of their merits.

I have placed the mark (z) by every name I include in addition to those in al-Dhahabī's al-Tajrīd and its source [and by every name additional to those in its source alone]. God is the One asked to guide us to the straight path, to lead us along the ways of those who investigate rigorously, to grant us sound direction and success, and to place us among those upon whom He has bestowed favor, together with the best company and the highest Companion. Amen, amen.

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

**( فائدة )**

أكثر الصحابة فتوى مطلقا سبعة : عمر ، وعلي ، وابن مسعود ، وابن عمر ، وابن عباس ، وزيد بن ثابت ، وعائشة رضوان الله تعالى عليهم أجمعين .

قال ابن حزم : يمكن أن يجمع من فتيا كل واحد من هؤلاء مجلد ضخم ؛ قال : ويليهم عشرون وهم : أبو بكر ، وعثمان ، وأبو موسى ، ومعاذ ، وسعد بن أبي وقاص ، وأبو هريرة ، وأنس ، وعبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص ، وسلمان ، وجابر ، وأبو سعيد ، وطلحة ، والزبير ، وعبد الرحمن بن عوف ، وعمران بن حصين ، وأبو بكرة ، وعبادة بن الصامت ، ومعاوية ، وابن الزبير ، وأم سلمة . قال : يمكن أن يجمع من فتيا كل واحد منهم جزء صغير .

قال : وفي الصحابة نحو من مائة وعشرين نفسا مقلون في الفتيا جدا ، لا يروى عن الواحد منهم إلا المسألة والمسألتان والثلاث ، يمكن أن يجمع من فتيا جميعهم جزء صغير بعد البحث ؛ كأبي بن كعب ، وأبي الدرداء ، وأبي طلحة ، والمقداد وغيرهم [ وسرد الباقين ] .

قلت : وسأذكر في ترجمة كل من ذكره من هذا القسم أن ابن حزم ذكر أنه من فقهاء الصحابة ؛ فإن ذلك من جملة المناقب .

وقد جعلت على كل اسم أوردته زائدا على ما في تجريد الذهبي وأصله [ وعلى ما في أصله فقط ] ( ز ) . والله المسئول أن يهدينا سواء الطريق ، وأن يسلك بنا مسالك أولي التحقيق ، وأن يرزقنا التسديد والتوفيق ، وأن يجعلنا في الذين أنعم عليهم مع خير فريق وأعلى رفيق آمين آمين .

</div>

## Source unit 1 · printed entry 1

### English candidate

Ābī al-Laḥm al-Ghifārī was a well-known Companion. His report was transmitted by al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, and al-Ḥākim. Al-Ḥākim also narrated through his chain from Abū ʿUbayda, who said: ‘Ābī al-Laḥm’s name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ghifār. He was a man of standing and a poet. He witnessed Ḥunayn, accompanied by his client ʿUmayr. He was called Ābī al-Laḥm only because he used to refuse to eat meat.’ Al-Wāqidī said that he lived at al-Ṣafrāʾ. Khalīfa ibn Khayyāṭ likewise gave this name and lineage. Al-Haytham ibn ʿAdī and Hishām ibn al-Kalbī said that his name was Khalaf ibn ʿAbd al-Malik. Others said that his name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik. It has also been said that his name was al-Ḥuwayrith ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khalaf ibn Mālik. Al-Marzubānī said: ‘His name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Malik. He was a man of standing and a poet who lived into the pre-Islamic period.’ I say: I saw it in the handwriting of al-Raḍī al-Shāṭibī as ‘ʿAbd Malak,’ with the lām bearing a fatḥa and without the alif and lām. Muslim transmitted in his Ṣaḥīḥ the report of ʿUmayr, the client of Ābī al-Laḥm, who said: ‘My master ordered me to cut meat into strips. A poor man came to me, so I fed him from it’—and the report continues. It includes: ‘I said, “O Messenger of God, may I give any of my master’s property in charity?” He said, “Yes, and the reward is shared between you both.”’ Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: ‘He was among the earliest and most senior Companions. There is no disagreement that he witnessed Ḥunayn and was killed there.’

## Source unit 2 · printed entry 2

### English candidate

Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ ibn Umayya ibn ʿAbd Manāf, the Qurashī and Umayyad. Al-Bukhārī, Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, and Ibn Ḥibbān said that he had Companionship. His father was one of the leading men of Quraysh and had distinguished sons. Khālid and ʿAmr were among those who embraced Islam early, and Abān composed concerning them the well-known verses that begin:

Would that a dead man at al-Ẓarībiyya could witness
what ʿAmr and Khālid are fabricating concerning religion.

Thereafter, ʿAmr and Khālid were among those who emigrated to Abyssinia, where they remained. Abān was present at Badr as a polytheist. His two brothers, al-ʿĀṣ and ʿUbayda, were killed there while still polytheists, whereas he escaped. He remained in Mecca until, at the time of al-Ḥudaybiyya, he granted protection to ʿUthmān, who conveyed the message of the Messenger of God ﷺ. Abān said to him:

Let [your garment] hang loose; come forward, and fear no one.
The sons of Saʿīd are mighty within the Sanctuary.

Then ʿAmr and Khālid returned from Abyssinia and corresponded with Abān. He followed them until all three came to the Prophet ﷺ, Abān arriving during the days of Khaybar. He witnessed Khaybar with the Prophet ﷺ; then the Prophet ﷺ sent him out on an expedition. Al-Wāqidī related all of this; the scholars of historical reports agreed with him, and this is the well-known account. Ibn Isḥāq disagreed with them, counting Abān among those who emigrated to Abyssinia, together with his wife Fāṭima bint Ṣafwān al-Kināniyya. الله أعلم.

Ibn Abī Khaythama transmitted, by way of Mūsā ibn ʿUbayda al-Rabadhī—one of the weak transmitters—from Iyās ibn Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ, from his father, who said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ sent ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān to Mecca. Abān ibn Saʿīd granted him protection, mounted him on his saddle behind himself, and carried him until he entered Mecca.’

Al-Haytham ibn ʿAdī said: ‘It reached me that Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: “When my father was killed on the day of Badr, I was under the guardianship of my paternal uncle, Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, and he was an excellent guardian. He went to Syria as a merchant.”’ He then related a long story about an encounter Abān had with a monk called Yakkā. The monk described the Prophet ﷺ to him, acknowledged his prophethood, and said, ‘Convey greetings of peace to the righteous man.’ Abān returned, gathered his people, and told them about it; then he journeyed to Medina and embraced Islam.

In al-Bukhārī and Abū Dāwūd, Abū Hurayra said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ sent Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ at the head of an expedition toward Najd. He and his companions came to the Messenger of God ﷺ at Khaybar’—the report.

Al-Wāqidī said: Ibrāhīm ibn Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who said: ‘The Prophet ﷺ died while Abān ibn Saʿīd was in Bahrain. Abān then came to Abū Bakr, proceeded to Syria, and was killed on the day of Ajnādayn in the year thirteen.’ This was stated by Mūsā ibn ʿUqba and most genealogists. Ibn Isḥāq said that he was killed on the day of al-Yarmūk, and Sayf ibn ʿUmar agreed with him in al-Futūḥ. It has also been said that he was killed on the day of Marj al-Ṣuffar; Ibn al-Barqī reported this. Abū Ḥassān al-Ziyādī said that he died in the year twenty-seven, during the caliphate of ʿUthmān.

Among the evidence that his death occurred after Abū Bakr’s caliphate is what Ibn Abī Dāwūd and al-Baghawī transmitted by way of Sulaymān ibn Wahb al-Anbārī, who said: al-Nuʿmān ibn Bazraj related to us that, when the Messenger of God ﷺ died, Abū Bakr sent Abān ibn Saʿīd to Yemen. Fayrūz spoke to him concerning the blood of Dādhawayh, whom Qays ibn Makshūḥ had killed. Abān said to Qays, ‘Did you kill a Muslim man?’ Qays denied that Dādhawayh had been a Muslim and said that he had killed him in retaliation for his father and paternal uncle. Abān then delivered an address, saying: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ set aside every blood-claim that arose in the pre-Islamic period. Whoever commits an offense in Islam, we shall hold him accountable for it.’ Abān then said to Qays, ‘Go to the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUmar, and I shall write to him that I have adjudicated between you.’ He wrote to ʿUmar accordingly, and ʿUmar confirmed his judgment.

Al-Baghawī said: ‘I know of no other musnad report belonging to Abān ibn Saʿīd.’ I say: al-Bukhārī also mentioned it briefly in Abān’s notice. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr preferred the first view, but then ended the notice by saying: ‘Abān was the one who undertook to dictate ʿUthmān’s codex to Zayd ibn Thābit; ʿUthmān instructed the two of them to do that. Ibn Shihāb reported this from Khārija ibn Zayd ibn Thābit, from his father.’ End of quotation. This statement entails contradiction and conflict: ʿUthmān ordered that only during his caliphate, so how could someone who was killed during Abū Bakr’s caliphate have lived into ʿUthmān’s caliphate? Rather, the report to which Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr alluded is anomalous. Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād alone transmitted it from al-Darāwardī. The well-known account is that the person instructed to do this was Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who was Abān ibn Saʿīd’s nephew. والله أعلم.

## Source unit 3 · printed entry 3

### English candidate

Abān al-Muḥāribī, of the Banū Muḥārib ibn ʿAmr ibn Wadīʿa ibn Lukayz ibn Afṣā ibn ʿAbd al-Qays; he is therefore also called Abān al-ʿAbdī. Ibn al-Sakan said: ‘He had Companionship, and a report of his is among the Basran material.’ Ibn Ḥibbān said: ‘Abān al-ʿAbdī came to the Prophet ﷺ as a delegate. He is counted among the people of Basra.’

Al-Baghawī transmitted for him, by way of Abān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh, from al-Ḥakam ibn Ḥayyān al-Muḥāribī, from Abān al-Muḥāribī—who was among the delegation from ʿAbd al-Qays that came to the Messenger of God ﷺ—that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘There is no Muslim servant who says upon entering the morning, “Praise belongs to God, my Lord; I associate nothing with Him,” except that his sins are forgiven.’ Al-Baghawī said: ‘I know of no report of his other than this one.’

I say: I found another. Ibn Shāhīn transmitted it, and we narrated it in the second part of the Fawāʾid of Abū Bakr ibn Khallād al-Naṣībī, by way of Ziyād al-Bakkāʾī, who said: Abū ʿUbayda al-ʿAtakī related to us, from al-Ḥakam ibn Ḥayyān, from Abān al-Muḥāribī, who said: ‘I was among the delegation, and I saw the whiteness of the armpits of the Messenger of God ﷺ when he raised his hands and turned them toward the qibla.’

Al-Dāraquṭnī indicated in al-Afrād that Abān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh was alone in transmitting the first report, and he is weak—extremely frail. If Abān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh had the kunya Abū ʿUbayda, then it is indeed established that he alone transmitted the report from the aforementioned al-Ḥakam.

## Source unit 4 · printed entry 4

### English candidate

Ibrāhīm ibn Jābir had been enslaved to Kharasha al-Thaqafī. He came down to the Prophet ﷺ from the fortress of al-Ṭāʾif as one of the group of their slaves who came down during the siege. The Prophet freed him, placed him in the care of Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr, and instructed Usayd to provide for him and teach him. Al-Wāqidī mentioned him. Ibn Fatḥūn supplied his omitted notice because he lived for a long time after the Prophet ﷺ.

## Source unit 5 · printed entry 5

### English candidate

Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Khālid ibn Ṣakhr ibn ʿĀmir ibn Kaʿb ibn Taym ibn Murra, the Qurashī and Taymī. Al-Bukhārī said: ‘He emigrated with his father.’ Ibn Manda transmitted, with a sound chain, from Yazīd ibn al-Hād, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, that his father was one of the Emigrants.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said in the notice of his father, al-Ḥārith ibn Khālid: ‘He emigrated to Abyssinia, where Mūsā, Zaynab, and Ibrāhīm were born to him, and they died in the land of Abyssinia.’ Muṣʿab stated this. Someone else said: ‘Al-Ḥārith set out with them, intending to reach Medina. They drank from some water and died, except for al-Ḥārith.’

I say: perhaps he had another son called Ibrāhīm, distinct from Ibrāhīm the father of Muḥammad; for how could someone who died at that time have a son, Muḥammad, born to him after a very long interval? Ibn Manda transmitted, by a chain in which there is no serious fault, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from his father, who said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ sent us out on an expedition’—the report. If this is established, then Ibrāhīm was one person and lived beyond the Prophet ﷺ.

## Source unit 10 · printed entry 10

### English candidate

Ibrāhīm al-Ṭāʾifī. Al-Baghawī and al-Ṭabarānī transmitted, by way of Abū ʿĀṣim, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn Hurmuz, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAṭāʾ ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from his grandfather, that he heard the Prophet ﷺ teaching the people at Minā and saying, ‘Fit the sandals with toe-straps.’ Al-Baghawī said, ‘I know of no other report of his.’ Al-Dhahabī related from Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr that he said, ‘It is not sound to include him among the Companions, because his report is mursal’—meaning that he was therefore a Successor. I say: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr’s wording is, ‘The isnād of his report is not sound, his Companionship is not established in my judgment, and his report is mursal.’ End quote. If by irsāl he meant a break between any two of its transmitters, that is one matter. Otherwise, the report explicitly states that he heard the Prophet ﷺ, so he is a Companion if the isnād of his report is established. Its pivot, however, is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn Hurmuz, who is weak, and his teacher is unknown. There is disagreement over the form of its chain from Abū ʿĀṣim. It has been given as above; and it is also given as Yaḥyā ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from his father, from his grandfather, as related by Ibn Abī Ḥātim. On this version, the Companion is ʿAṭāʾ. Ibn al-Sakan preferred it, and both he and Ibn Shāhīn transmitted it by way of ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī al-Fallās from Abū ʿĀṣim. Al-Baghawī also transmitted it from Ibn al-Junayd, from Abū ʿĀṣim, and gave the name as Ibrāhīm ibn Yaḥyā ibn ʿAṭāʾ. It is also given as Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAṭāʾ, and as Yaḥyā ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿAṭāʾ. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it and included a biography of ʿAṭāʾ among the Companions; Ibn Ḥibbān, Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim, Muṭayyan, and others did likewise. The first version is strengthened by what Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Dughūlī related: ‘I asked Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī whether there was anyone among the Companions named Ibrāhīm. He said, “Yes. Ibrāhīm is an ancient name. A man who heard the Prophet ﷺ bore it; the Meccans transmitted the report from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father.”’ والله أعلم.

## Source unit 16 · printed entry 16

### English candidate

Another Abraha. Ibn Fatḥūn said in al-Dhayl: He was one of the eight Syrians who came in a delegation with Jaʿfar, together with thirty-two men from Abyssinia. They were those whom God meant in His words, ‘Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it believe in it.’ Al-Māwardī related this from Qatāda. End quote. Muqātil named the eight just mentioned as Abraha, Idrīs, Ashraf, Ayman, Baḥīrā, Tamām, Tamīm, and Nāfiʿ. Abū Mūsā related this in al-Dhayl. Ibn al-Athīr thought this Baḥīrā was the famous monk who saw the Prophet ﷺ before the prophetic mission, and said, ‘Ibn Manda already mentioned him, so there is no basis for adding him in a supplement.’ End quote. It appears that he is a different man, because that one saw him in the land of Syria, while this other man was from Abyssinia. How far the south is from the north! There is nothing to prevent two men from bearing the same name. Abū al-Shaykh and others transmitted in Qurʾānic commentary, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning this verse, that he said: The believers among the companions of the Negus said to the Negus, ‘Give us permission so that we may go to this Prophet whom we used to find described in the Scripture.’ They came to the Prophet ﷺ and fought at Uḥud alongside him. This indicates that the account has a basis. والله أعلم.

## Source unit 17 · printed entry 17

### English candidate

Abzā al-Khuzāʿī, their client and the father of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. Ibn al-Sakan said: Al-Bukhārī mentioned him in al-Wuḥdān. A single report is related from him, with a sound isnād; his report was found in Khurasan: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Bisṭām told us: Aḥmad ibn Bukayr told us: Abū Wahb Muḥammad ibn Muzāḥim told us: Bukayr ibn Maʿrūf told us, from Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, from ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abzā, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he addressed the people, spoke well of various groups of Muslims, and then said, ‘What is the matter with people who do not learn from their neighbors and do not seek understanding?’—and he related the report. He said: It is transmitted only through this isnād. Ibn Manda said that neither Companionship nor sight of the Prophet is established for him. He then transmitted his report from Ibn al-Sakan, regarded it as singular, and said that Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh transmitted it in al-Musnad from Muḥammad ibn Abī Sahl—who is Muḥammad ibn Muzāḥim—with this isnād. I say: It is as he said. We have transmitted it in Isḥāq’s Musnad, in Ibn Mardawayh’s recension from him, in precisely this form. Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh, however, transmitted it from his father with the isnād reading ‘from ʿAlqama ibn Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from his grandfather.’ Al-Ṭabarānī placed it in the biography of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abzā. Abū Nuʿaym preferred this version and said that neither transmission nor sight of the Prophet is established for Abzā. Ibn al-Athīr approved his position. I say: Ibn al-Sakan’s statement answers him, and the principal reliance in this matter is upon al-Bukhārī, with whom the matter ends. Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh’s version is anomalous, because ʿAlqama was Saʿīd’s brother, not his son. والله أعلم.

## Source unit 19 · printed entry 19

### English candidate

Abyaḍ ibn Ḥammāl—with an unpointed ḥāʾ—ibn Murthid ibn Dhī Liḥyān—with the lām vocalized ḍamma—ibn Saʿd ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAdī ibn Mālik, al-Maʾribī al-Sabaʾī. Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā, Ibn Mājah, and Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ transmitted his report: when he came to the Prophet ﷺ in a delegation, he asked him to grant him the salt deposit at Maʾrib. He granted it to him and then asked him to return it. According to another route, Abyaḍ ibn Ḥammāl had a scaly lesion on his face—ringworm—which had spread over his nose. The Prophet ﷺ wiped his face, and before that day was over no trace of it remained. Al-Bukhārī and Ibn al-Sakan said: He had Companionship and reports, and is counted among the people of Yemen. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted that he came in a delegation to Abū Bakr when the officials of Yemen rebelled against him. Abū Bakr confirmed him upon the alms arrangement that the Prophet ﷺ had concluded with him. That arrangement then lapsed after Abū Bakr, and the matter reverted to alms.

## Source unit 25 · printed entry 25

### English candidate

Ubayy ibn Umayya ibn Ḥirthān ibn al-Iskir al-Kinānī al-Laythī. He and his brother Kilāb accepted Islam and emigrated to the Prophet ﷺ. Their father Umayya then said: ‘When the dove in the vale of Wajj weeps
over her eggs, I call for Kilāb.’ Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī mentioned him. When Ibn al-Kalbī mentioned him, he said that the incident occurred to them in the time of ʿUmar. Ibn al-Athīr added him in a supplement. I say: Al-Fākihī mentioned in Akhbār Makka, from Ibn Abī ʿUmar, from Sufyān, from Abū Saʿd, that whenever a traveler arrived, ʿUmar would ask him about the people. A traveler arrived, and he asked, ‘Where are you from?’ He replied, ‘From al-Ṭāʾif.’ He asked, ‘And what news?’ He replied, ‘I saw an old man there saying: “You left your father with trembling hands,
and your mother unable to swallow a drink.
Whenever the dove cries in the vale of Wajj
over her eggs, it calls Kilāb to mind.”’ He asked, ‘Who is Kilāb?’ He replied, ‘The son of the old man just mentioned; he was away on campaign.’ ʿUmar wrote concerning him, and he returned. I say: This account will appear at greater length in the biography of Umayya, إن شاء الله تعالى.

Abū Dāwūd, Ibn Mājah, and al-Ḥākim transmitted it, but its isnād is weak. Abū Ḥātim stated that it is an error and that the correct person is Abū Ubayy ibn Umm Ḥarām. الله أعلم. Al-Baghawī reported that he was Ubayy ibn ʿUbāda. Ibn Ḥibbān said, ‘He prayed toward both qiblas, although I do not rely upon the isnād of his report.’ I say: Ibn al-Kalbī related from his father that he met him, and that his father ʿImāra met Khālid ibn Sinān al-ʿAbsī, who is said to have been a prophet. I shall mention that in Khālid’s biography.

## Source unit 32 · printed entry 32

### English candidate

Ubayy ibn Kaʿb ibn Qays ibn ʿUbayd ibn Zayd ibn Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār al-Anṣārī, Abū al-Mundhir and Abū al-Ṭufayl, master of the Qurʾān reciters. He was one of the participants in the Second ʿAqaba and witnessed Badr and all the campaigns. The Prophet ﷺ said to him, ‘May knowledge bring you joy, Abū al-Mundhir,’ and told him, ‘God has commanded me to recite to you.’ ʿUmar called him ‘master of the Muslims,’ would say, ‘Recite, Ubayy,’ and also transmitted that designation from the Prophet ﷺ. The leading compilers included his reports in their Ṣaḥīḥ collections. Masrūq counted him among the six Companions qualified to give legal opinions. Al-Wāqidī said that he was the first to write for the Prophet ﷺ and the first to write at the end of a document, ‘So-and-so son of so-and-so wrote it.’ He was of medium stature, with a white beard, and did not dye his gray hair. Companions who transmitted from him included ʿUmar—who asked him about new cases and submitted difficult questions to his judgment—Abū Ayyūb, ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit, Sahl ibn Saʿd, Abū Mūsā, Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Hurayra, Anas, Sulaymān ibn Ṣurad, and others. Ibn Abī Khaythama said: I heard Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn say that Ubayy ibn Kaʿb died in 20 or 19 AH. Al-Wāqidī said, ‘I saw Ubayy’s family and our colleagues say that he died in 22 AH,’ whereupon ʿUmar said, ‘Today the master of the Muslims has died.’ He added, ‘I have heard some say that he died in 30 AH during ʿUthmān’s caliphate, and this is the soundest position.’ Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said that most held he died during ʿUmar’s caliphate. I say: Abū Nuʿaym judged it sound that he died in 30 during ʿUthmān’s caliphate, arguing that Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh met him then. Al-Bukhārī related in his History from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abzā: ‘I said to Ubayy, when the people became embroiled in the matter of ʿUthmān’—and he related the account. Al-Baghawī related from al-Ḥasan, in an account of his, that Ubayy died one week before ʿUthmān was killed. Ibn Ḥibbān said that he died in 22 during ʿUmar’s caliphate, though it has also been said that he survived into ʿUthmān’s. It is established from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that a Muslim asked, ‘Messenger of God, what do we receive for these illnesses that afflict us?’ He replied, ‘Expiations.’ Ubayy ibn Kaʿb asked, ‘Even if they are slight?’ He replied, ‘Even a thorn, and anything greater.’ Ubayy then prayed that fever never leave him until he died, while not distracting him from pilgrimage, ʿumra, jihad, or an obligatory congregational prayer. Thereafter, no one touched his body without feeling its heat, until he died. Aḥmad, Abū Yaʿlā, and Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted it; Ibn Ḥibbān authenticated it. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted its meaning from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb with a fair isnād.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

أبي بن كعب بن قيس بن عبيد بن زيد بن معاوية بن عمرو بن مالك بن النجار الأنصاري أبو المنذر وأبو الطفيل سيد القراء كان من أصحاب العقبة الثانية وشهد بدرا والمشاهد كلها قال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليهنك العلم أبا المنذر وقال له إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك وكان عمر يسميه سيد المسلمين ويقول اقرأ يا أبي ويروي ذلك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أيضا وأخرج الأئمة أحاديثه في صحاحهم وعده مسروق في الستة من أصحاب الفتيا قال الواقدي وهو أول من كتب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأول من كتب في آخر الكتاب وكتب فلان بن فلان وكان ربعة أبيض اللحية لا يغير شيبه وممن روى عنه من الصحابة عمر وكان يسأله عن النوازل ويتحاكم إليه في المعضلات وأبو أيوب وعبادة بن الصامت وسهل بن سعد وأبو موسى وابن عباس وأبو هريرة وأنس وسليمان بن صرد وغيرهم قال بن أبي خيثمة سمعت يحيى بن معين يقول مات أبي بن كعب سنة عشرين أو تسع عشرة وقال الواقدي ورأيت آل أبي وأصحابنا يقولون مات سنة اثنتين وعشرين فقال عمر اليوم مات سيد المسلمين قال وقد سمعت من يقول مات في خلافة عثمان سنة ثلاثين وهو أثبت الأقاويل وقال بن عبد البر الأكثر على أنه في خلافة عمر قلت وصحح أبو نعيم أنه مات في خلافة عثمان سنة ثلاثين واحتج له بأن رز بن حبيش لقيه في خلافة عثمان وروى البخاري في تاريخه عن عبد الرحمن بن أبزى قال قلت لأبي لما وقع الناس في أمر عثمان فذكر القصة وروى البغوي عن الحسن في قصة له أنه مات قبل قتل عثمان بجمعة وقال بن حبان مات سنة ثنتين وعشرين في خلافة عمر وقد قيل أنه بقي إلى خلافة عثمان وثبت عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن رجلا من المسلمين قال يا رسول الله أرأيت هذه الأمراض التي تصيبنا مالنا فيها قال كفارات فقال أبي بن كعب يا رسول الله وإن قلت قال وإن شوكة فما فوقها فدعا أبي ألا يفارقه الوعك حتى يموت وألا يشغله عن حج ولا عمرة ولا جهاد ولا صلاة مكتوبة في جماعة قال فما مس إنسان جسده إلا وجد حره حتى مات رواه أحمد وأبو يعلى وابن أبي الدنيا وصححه بن حبان ورواه الطبراني من حديث أبي بن كعب بمعناه وإسناده حسن

## Source unit 33 · printed entry 33

### English candidate

Ubayy ibn Mālik al-Qushayrī, also said to be al-Ḥarashī, of the Banū ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa; counted among the people of Basra. Ibn Ḥibbān said he was said to have Companionship and gave his lineage as Ubayy ibn Mālik ibn ʿAmr ibn Rabīʿa ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Rabīʿa ibn ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa al-Qushayrī, Abū Mālik; Basrans transmitted from him. Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī transmitted from Shuʿba, from Qatāda, from Zurāra ibn Awfā, from Ubayy ibn Mālik, that the Prophet ﷺ said, ‘Whoever lives to see both parents, or one of them, and then enters the Fire—may God cast him far away.’ ʿAlī ibn al-Jaʿd, Ghundar, ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAlī, ʿAmr ibn Marzūq, Ādam ibn Abī Iyās, and Bahz ibn Asad corroborated Shuʿba. ʿAbd al-Ṣamad reported from Shuʿba, ‘from Mālik or Ubayy ibn Mālik’; Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith said ‘from a man’ without naming him; and Shabāba said ʿAmr ibn Mālik. The first is soundest from Qatāda. Ibn al-Sakan reported al-Bukhārī as saying that this report is variously ascribed to Mālik ibn ʿAmr, Ibn al-Ḥārith, and Ibn Mālik, but the correct form is Ubayy ibn Mālik. Al-Baghawī and others preferred this too. Ibn Abī Khaythama, however, reported Ibn Maʿīn striking out Ubayy ibn Mālik and saying, ‘This is an error. There is no Ubayy ibn Mālik among the Companions; it is ʿAmr ibn Mālik.’ I say: He may have relied on Shabāba’s anomalous version. ʿAlī ibn Zayd ibn Judʿān transmitted it from Zurāra ibn Awfā from a man of his people called Mālik, Abū Mālik, or Ibn Mālik. Al-Thawrī and Hushaym gave Mālik al-Qushayrī; Ashʿath gave Mālik, Abū Mālik, or ʿĀmir ibn Mālik. Mālik ibn ʿAmr and Ibn al-Ḥārith are also reported through Ḥammād ibn Salama; ʿAmr ibn Mālik through al-Thawrī; and Mālik ibn ʿAwf and Ibn al-Ḥārith through Hushaym. I say: Shuʿba’s report from Qatāda is strengthened by Ibn Isḥāq’s account of the spoils of Ḥunayn, in which Ubayy ibn Mālik al-Qushayrī addressed the Messenger of God. Ibn Durayd’s al-Akhbār al-Manthūra calls him Ubayy ibn Mālik ibn Muʿāwiya al-Qushayrī, brother of the famous poet Nuhayk ibn Mālik, and relates that al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Sufyān later reproached him: ‘Do you forget my service, Ubayy ibn Mālik,
on the morning the Messenger turned from you, stern-faced?’ This report will appear under Marwān ibn Qays al-Dawsī. All this strengthens al-Bukhārī’s preference. والله أعلم.

أبي بن مالك القشيري ويقال الحرشي من بني عامر بن صعصعة عداده في أهل البصرة قال بن حبان يقال إن له صحبة ونسبه فقال أبي بن مالك بن عمرو بن ربيعة بن عبد الله بن كعب بن ربيعة بن عامر بن صعصعة القشيري أبو مالك روى عنه البصريون وقال أبو داود الطيالسي في مسنده حدثنا شعبة عن قتادة عن زرارة أوفى عن أبي بن مالك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وسلم قال من أدرك والديه أو أحدهما ثم دخل النار فأبعده الله وتابعه على بن الجعد وغندر وعاصم بن علي وعمرو بن مرزوق وآدم بن أبي إياس وبهز بن أسد عن شعبة ورواه عبد الصمد عن شعبة فقال عن مالك أو أبي بن مالك ورواه خالد بن الحارث عن شعبة فقال عن رجل ولم يسمه ورواه شبابة عن شعبة فقال عمرو بن مالك والأول أصح عن قتادة قال بن السكن قال البخاري يقال في هذا الحديث مالك بن عمرو ويقال بن الحارث ويقال بن مالك والصحيح من ذلك أبي بن مالك وكذلك رجح البغوي وغيره وأما بن أبي خيثمة فحكى عن بن معين أنه ضرب على أبي بن مالك وقال هذا خطا ليس في الصحابة أبي بن مالك وإنما هو عمرو بن مالك قلت لعله اعتمد رواية شبابة ولكنها شاذه وقد روى علي بن زيد بن جدعان هذا الحديث عن زرارة بن أوفى عن رجل من قومه يقال له مالك أو أبو مالك أو بن مالك ورواه الثوري وهشيم عن علي بن زيد عن زرارة عن مالك القشيري ورواه أشعث عن علي بن زيد فقال مالك أو أبو مالك أو عامر بن مالك وقيل مالك بن عمرو وقيل بن الحارث وهي رواية عن حماد بن سلمة عن علي بن زيد وقيل عمرو بن مالك وهي رواية الثوري عن علي وكلاهما عن أحمد وقيل مالك بن عوف وقيل بن الحارث وهي رواية هشيم عن علي عن أحمد قلت ومما يقوي رواية شعبة عن قتادة ما ذكره بن إسحاق في المغازي في أمر غنائم حنين قال فقال أبي بن مالك القشيري يا رسول الله فذكر قصته وفي الأخبار المنثورة لابن دريد قال فقال أبي بن مالك بن معاوية القشيري وهو أخو نهيك بن مالك الشاعر المشهور فذكر قصة فيها أن الضحاك بن سفيان عتب على أبي بن مالك في شيء بعد ذلك فقال <br />

## Source unit 35 · printed entry 35

### English candidate

Athāl ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Ḥanafī. ʿAbdān transmitted, by way of al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUbayd al-Iyādī, from his father, from Athāl ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Ḥanafī, who said: “Furāt ibn Ḥayyān and I came to the Prophet ﷺ and greeted him. He returned our greeting, although we had not yet accepted Islam. He then granted Furāt ibn Ḥayyān a tract of land.” Al-Ṭabarī transmitted that Athāl was with Thumāma ibn Athāl in the fighting against Musaylima during the Ridda. Ibn Fatḥūn said, “Perhaps he was Thumāma’s father.” I say: No; Thumāma’s father was named Athāl ibn Salama, as will appear in the biography of ʿĀmir ibn Salama.

## Source unit 36 · printed entry 36

## Source unit 52 · printed entry 52

### English candidate

Al-Aḥwaṣ ibn ʿAbd ibn Umayya ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf. Ibn al-Kalbī and al-Balādhurī mentioned that he served Muʿāwiya as governor of Bahrain and interceded with Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam in an affair. This implies that he had Companionship and lived to an advanced age, for his father died an unbeliever. His descendants included Manṣūr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Aḥwaṣ, mentioned in Syria in the Umayyad period; his son ʿAbd Allāh also governed part of Syria for Muʿāwiya. The Muwaṭṭaʾ relates from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, that al-Aḥwaṣ died in Syria when his wife entered the bleeding of her third menstruation. Muʿāwiya wrote to Zayd ibn Thābit, who ruled that his wife had no inheritance. Ibn ʿUyayna transmitted from al-Zuhrī, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, that it was ‘al-Aḥwaṣ ibn so-and-so’ or ‘so-and-so ibn al-Aḥwaṣ,’ and related a similar account. Ibn al-Ḥadhdhāʾ said the stronger view is that it concerned al-Aḥwaṣ ibn ʿAbd, though it may have concerned his son ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Aḥwaṣ; Ibn ʿUyayna’s report from al-Zuhrī does not name him.
