## Source unit 286 · printed entry 286

### English candidate

Anas al-Juhanī, father of Muʿādh. Khalīfa mentioned him among the Companions who settled in Syria. In al-Ṭabarī’s History, from Abū Kurayb, from Rushdayn ibn Saʿd, from Zabbān ibn Fāʾid, from Sahl ibn Muʿādh ibn Anas, from his father, from his grandfather, the Prophet ﷺ used to say: “Shall I tell you why God named His intimate friend ‘the one who fulfilled’? It was because every morning and every evening he would say, ‘So glory be to God when you enter evening and when you enter morning.’”

Ibn Manda transmitted, by way of Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād from Rushdayn with this chain, an interpretation of “By the earth that splits open.” Aḥmad in his Musnad and Tammām in his Fawāʾid transmitted by way of Ibn Lahīʿa; al-Ṭabarānī in Musnad al-Shāmiyyīn and Abū al-Maymūn ibn Rāshid in his Fawāʾid transmitted by way of Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz; both routes were from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Muʿādh ibn Sahl ibn Anas, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abū al-Dardāʾ, a report concerning the merit of headache and illness. In this recension Sahl was ascribed to his grandfather. The correct form is Muʿādh ibn Sahl ibn Muʿādh ibn Anas, so the report is from Muʿādh ibn Anas, from Abū al-Dardāʾ.

The compilers of the Sunan transmitted reports from Muʿādh ibn Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, none of which has “from his father.” Other reports containing disagreement occur in the works of some who wrote on the Companions. Among them is what al-Baghawī transmitted: ʿAbbās related to us; Yūnus ibn Muḥammad related to us; al-Layth related to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Muʿādh ibn Anas, from his father—who was one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—who raised it: “Ride these animals while they are sound, and do not take them as chairs.” There is also a route from al-Layth, from Zabbān ibn Fāʾid, from Muʿādh ibn Anas, from his father. Al-Baghawī said: “Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb and Zabbān have transmitted reports from Sahl ibn Muʿādh, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ; none has Muʿādh ibn Anas from Anas except this one.”

I say: A link was dropped from its route, producing this mistake. Aḥmad transmitted it in his Musnad from Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad, from al-Layth, through both chains together, as a report from the son of Muʿādh ibn Anas, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ. He also transmitted it from Mūsā ibn Dāwūd and Abū al-Walīd al-Ṭayālisī, both from al-Layth, from Yazīd; and from Ḥasan ibn Mūsā, from Ibn Lahīʿa, from Zabbān, from Sahl ibn Muʿādh, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ. Abū Yaʿlā likewise transmitted it from Abū Khaythama, from Yūnus ibn Muḥammad, with both chains, separating them. Al-Ḥākim likewise transmitted it by way of ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAlī and Saʿīd ibn Sulaymān, both from al-Layth. Ibn ʿAsākir said in his History: “Al-Baghawī’s recension is an error; والله أعلم.” Al-Ḥākim also has, by way of Ibrāhīm ibn Dīzil, from Shabāba, from al-Layth, exactly what occurs in al-Baghawī, in error. Al-Dārimī transmitted it in his Musnad from ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba, from Shabāba, in the correct form found in Aḥmad and others.

I say: Supporting the correct form is the fact that Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb and Zabbān ibn Fāʾid did not meet Muʿādh ibn Anas; rather, they narrate from his son Sahl ibn Muʿādh ibn Anas. والله أعلم.

## Source unit 287 · printed entry 287

### English candidate

Anasa, client of the Prophet ﷺ. He is also said to have been called Abū Anasa. It is said that he was martyred on the Day of Badr; that he was Abū Masrūḥ; and that he was Abū Masraḥ. Muṣʿab al-Zubayrī said that Anasa bore the kunya Abū Masraḥ, served as an usher for the Prophet ﷺ, was one of those born in al-Sarāt, and died during Abū Bakr’s caliphate. Al-Khaṭīb said: “I do not know that he transmitted anything from the Prophet ﷺ.”

Mūsā ibn ʿUqba mentioned him, from Ibn Shihāb, among those who witnessed Badr and were martyred there. Ibn Isḥāq and al-Wāqidī likewise mentioned him among those who witnessed Badr. Al-Madāʾinī said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Thābit related to us, from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, with the same report, except that he called him Abū Anasa. Ibn ʿAsākir transmitted it in his History by way of Khalīfa from al-Madāʾinī, where it says “he was martyred.” Al-Wāqidī likewise mentioned it from Ibn Abī Ḥabība, from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn with his chain. Abū ʿUmar said that this is the preserved version.

Al-Wāqidī said: “I found the learned authorities affirming that he witnessed Uḥud and remained alive for some time afterward.” He said: Ibn Abī al-Zinād related to me, from Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf, who said: Anasa died after the Prophet ﷺ, during the caliphate of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq. Khalīfa said: “Anīsa, his client, served as an usher for the Prophet ﷺ.” I do not know whether he meant this man or another.

Then I found that Muṣʿab had stated that Anasa, the client of the Prophet ﷺ, served as his usher, bore the kunya Abū Masrūḥ, witnessed Badr and Uḥud, was one of those born in al-Sarāt, and died during the caliphate of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁. Al-Khaṭīb said: “I do not know that he transmitted anything from the Prophet ﷺ.” والله أعلم.

## Source unit 289 · printed entry 289

### English candidate

Unays ibn Junāda ibn Sufyān ibn ʿUbayd ibn Ḥarām ibn Ghifār, al-Ghifārī, brother of Abū Dharr; he was older than him. Muslim and al-Baghawī transmitted, by way of Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīra, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣāmit, who said that Abū Dharr said:

My brother Unays said to me, “A need has arisen for me to go to Mecca. Will you take care of things until I return to you?” I said, “Yes.” Unays went to Mecca, was delayed in returning to me, and then came back. He said, “I met a man in Mecca who follows your religion and claims that God has sent him. They call him the Ṣābiʾ.” I asked, “What do the people say?” He replied, “They claim that he is a liar, a sorcerer, and a poet. I have heard his speech; by God, it is not what they say. I have heard their speech too; by God, I consider him truthful.” The report continues at length. In it, Unays said, “I have no aversion to your religion; I have embraced Islam and affirmed it.”

In al-Mustadrak, by way of ʿUrwa ibn Ruwaym—“ʿĀmir ibn Ludayn al-Ashʿarī related to me; I heard Abū Laylā al-Ashʿarī; Abū Dharr related to me”—the story of Abū Dharr’s conversion is given at length. At its end he said: “I went out until I reached my mother and my brother and told them the news. They said, ‘We have no wish to remain apart from that which you have entered.’ They embraced Islam. Then we departed and came to Medina.”

## Source unit 293 · printed entry 293

### English candidate

Unays ibn Qatāda ibn Rabīʿa ibn Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUbayd ibn Zayd ibn Mālik ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, the Anṣārī of the Aws. He witnessed Badr and was martyred at Uḥud.

Al-Wāqidī said: Ibn Akhī al-Zuhrī related to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jāriya, from his paternal uncle Mujammiʿ ibn Jāriya: Khansāʾ bint Khidhām was married to Unays ibn Qatāda. When he was killed at Uḥud and left her a widow, her father married her to a man of Muzayna. She disliked him and went to the Messenger of God ﷺ, who annulled the marriage. She then married Abū Lubāba and bore him al-Sāʾib ibn Abī Lubāba.

Al-Bukhārī and others transmitted it by way of Mālik, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, from his father, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Mujammiʿ, the two sons of Yazīd ibn Jāriya al-Anṣārī, from Khansāʾ bint Khidhām: her father married her while she was unwilling. This version does not name her husband.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: “He was killed as a martyr on the Day of Uḥud.” Authorities other than al-Wāqidī called him Anas, but Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr rejected that. والله أعلم.

Ibn Saʿd said: Muḥammad ibn Ḥumayd informed us, from Maʿmar, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jaḥshī, who said: A woman called Khansāʾ bint Khidhām was married to Unays ibn Qatāda al-Anṣārī. When he was killed at Uḥud and left her a widow, her father married her to a man. She came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “My children’s paternal uncle is dearer to me.” He placed the matter in her hands. Further details concerning the routes of this report will come in the biography of Khansāʾ bint Khidhām, إن شاء الله تعالى.

## Source unit 295 · printed entry 295

### English candidate

Anīs ibn Abī Marthad al-Anṣārī. Al-Baghawī transmitted in his Muʿjam, Baqī ibn Makhlad in his Musnad, al-Bukhārī in his Tārīkh, and Abū ʿAlī ibn al-Sakan, by way of al-Layth, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Khālid ibn Abī ʿImrān, that al-Ḥakam ibn Masʿūd related to him that Anīs ibn Abī Marthad al-Anṣārī related to him that the Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘There will be a mute, blind, and deaf tribulation. The one lying down during it is better than the one sitting...’—the remainder of the report. Ibn Shāhīn cited it by this route, but said, ‘from Anīs ibn Marthad al-Anṣārī.’ Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr gave him the heading Anīs ibn Marthad ibn Abī Marthad al-Ghanawī and alluded to this report in his biography, saying, ‘Al-Ḥakam ibn Masʿūd transmitted from him his report concerning the tribulation.’ End. Ibn al-Sakan and others distinguished Anīs ibn Abī Marthad al-Anṣārī from Anas ibn Abī Marthad al-Ghanawī, which is correct. Al-ʿAskarī included Anīs ibn Abī Marthad al-Anṣārī among the Companions. Ibn Ḥibbān, however, included him among the trustworthy Followers. If Anas ibn Marthad ibn Abī Marthad al-Ghanawī was called Anīs in the diminutive, he is someone other than this man. والله أعلم.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

أنيس بن أبي مرثد الأنصاري روى البغوي في معجمه وبقي بن مخلد في مسنده والبخاري في تاريخه وأبو علي بن السكن من طريق الليث عن يحيى بن سعيد عن خالد بن أبي عمران أن الحكم بن مسعود حدثه أن أنيس بن أبي مرثد الأنصاري حدثه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ستكون فتنة بكماء عمياء صماء المضطجع فيها خير من القاعدة الحديث وأورده بن شاهين من هذا الوجه لكن قال عن أنيس بن مرثد الأنصاري وترجم له بن عبد البر أنيس بن مرثد بن أبي مرثد الغنوي وأشار إلى هذا الحديث في ترجمته فقال روى عنه الحكم بن مسعود حديثه في الفتنة انتهى وقد فرق بن السكن وغيره بين أنيس بن أبي مرثد الأنصاري وأنس بن أبي مرثد الغنوي وهو الصواب وذكر العسكري أنيس بن أبي مرثد الأنصاري في الصحابة وأما بن حبان فذكره في ثقات التابعين وأن كان أنس بن مرثد بن أبي مرثد الغنوي يدعى أنيسا مصغرا فهو غير هذا والله أعلم

## Source unit 296 · printed entry 296

### English candidate

Anīs al-Aslamī, mentioned in the report of the hired laborer. Al-Bukhārī, Muslim, and others transmitted, by way of al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba, from Abū Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī, that two men brought a dispute before the Messenger of God ﷺ. He then related the report, which includes: ‘My son was a hired laborer for this man and committed illicit intercourse with his wife. I was told that my son was liable to stoning, so I ransomed him from him for one hundred sheep and a slave girl. I then asked the learned, and they told me that my son was liable to one hundred lashes and banishment for a year, while this man’s wife was liable to stoning’—the report. At its end, the Prophet ﷺ said, ‘Go in the morning, Anīs’—addressing a man of Aslam—‘to this man’s wife. If she confesses, stone her.’ He went to her in the morning; she confessed, and he stoned her. Ibn al-Sakan said, ‘I do not know who the Anīs mentioned in this report is, and I have found no narration of his other than what is mentioned in this report.’ He is said to be Anīs ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Aslamī. Another said that he was Anīs ibn Abī Marthad, but that is an error, because Ibn Abī Marthad was Ghanawī whereas this report establishes that this man was Aslamī.

## Source unit 307 · printed entry 307

### English candidate

Ahbān ibn Aws al-Aslamī, also called Wahbān. He embraced Islam early, prayed toward both qiblas, settled in Kufa, and died there during the governorship of al-Mughīra. Al-Bukhārī said, ‘He possessed companionship and is counted among the people of Kufa.’ In his Ṣaḥīḥ he transmitted from him, by way of Mujazzaʾa ibn Zāhir, a report stopped at Ahbān. It states that he had companionship and was one of the Companions of the Tree. In his Tārīkh al-Bukhārī transmitted, by way of Anīs ibn ʿAmr, from Ahbān ibn Aws, that he was among his sheep when a wolf charged one of them. He shouted at it, and it sat upon its haunches and said, ‘Who will care for her on the day when he is kept busy away from her?’ Al-Bukhārī said, ‘Its isnad is not strong.’ I say: that is because it contains ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir al-Aslamī, who is weak. In his biography Ibn al-Sakan included the report of Abū Naḍra, from Abū Saʿīd, who said: While a shepherd was tending sheep outside Medina, a wolf sprang upon one of his sheep. The shepherd intervened between it and her. The wolf sat upon its haunches and said, ‘Do you come between me and provision that God has driven [to me]?’—to the end of the report. Ibn al-Kalbī, Abū ʿUbayd, al-Balādhurī, and al-Ṭabarī mentioned that the man to whom the wolf spoke was Ahbān ibn al-Akwaʿ ibn ʿIyādh. Ibn Ḥibbān said that Ahbān ibn Aws died during the governorship of al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba in Kufa, when al-Mughīra was Muʿāwiya’s governor there.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

أهبان بن أوس الأسلمي ويقال وهبان قديم الإسلام صلى القبلتين ونزل الكوفة ومات بها في ولاية المغيرة قال البخاري له صحبة يعد في أهل الكوفة وروى له في صحيحه حديثا موقوفا من رواية مجزأة بن زاهر عنه وفيه أنه كان له صحبة وكان من أصحاب الشجرة وروى في تاريخه من طريق أنيس بن عمرو عن أهبان بن أوس أنه كان في غنم له فشد الذئب على شاة منها فصاح عليه فأقعى على ذنبه قال فخاطبني فقال من لها يوم يشغل عنها قال البخاري إسناده ليس بالقوي قلت لأن فيه عبد الله بن عامر الأسلمي وهو ضعيف وأورد بن السكن في ترجمته حديث أبي نضرة عن أبي سعيد قال بينما راع يرعى غنما بظهر المدينة إذ عدا الذئب على شاة من غنمه فحال بينه وبينها فأقعى الذئب فقال تحول بيني وبين رزق ساقه الله إلى الحديث وذكر بن الكلبي وأبو عبيد والبلاذري والطبري أن مكلم الذئب هو أهبان بن الأكوع بن عياذ قال بن حبان مات أهبان بن أوس في ولاية المغيرة بن شعبة بالكوفة حيث كان واليا عليها لمعاوية

</div>

## Source unit 308 · printed entry 308

### English candidate

Ahbān ibn Ṣayfī al-Ghifārī, also called Wahbān, with the kunya Abū Muslim. Al-Tirmidhī transmitted a report from him and graded his report ḥasan; Ibn Mājah and Aḥmad also transmitted from him. Al-Ṭabarānī said that he died in Basra. Al-Muʿallā ibn Jābir ibn Muslim transmitted from his father, from ʿUdaysa bint Wahbān ibn Ṣayfī, that when her father was at the point of death he instructed that he be shrouded in two garments. They shrouded him in three, but when they awoke they found the third garment upon the bed. Al-Ṭabarānī likewise transmitted it by way of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd, from ʿUdaysa bint Ahbān. Ibn Ḥibbān reported that Ahbān, the son of Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī’s sister, was Ahbān ibn Ṣayfī; Ibn Manda rejected that identification.

## Source unit 311 · printed entry 311

### English candidate

Ahwad ibn ʿIyāḍ al-Azdī. Wathīma mentioned in al-Ridda, from Ibn Isḥāq, who said: While Ḥimyar were assembled with their chiefs, a rider from al-Azd named Ahwad ibn ʿIyāḍ approached and said, ‘People of Ḥimyar, I announce to you the death of the Messenger of God ﷺ.’ Ibn Dhī Aṣbaḥ said to him, ‘May God mutilate you as an envoy of a people! You lie; he has not died.’ He replied, ‘Yes, by Him who sent him with the truth. What is your grief? By God, I am more grief-stricken than you. Had I found hearts more tender than yours and eyes more abundant in tears, I would have announced his death to them.’ They expelled him from among them. He was a devout worshipper, and said, ‘O God, I announced to them the death of Your Messenger only lest they be led into tribulation after him and so that they might console me in my grief for him.’ When successive riders confirmed his death, they later gave Ahwad shelter. Concerning that, Ibn Dhī Aṣbaḥ said:

Ahwad made the heart grieve
when he announced Muḥammad’s death to me.
Would that I had never seen
Ahwad, the brother of al-Azd.

These are among verses that he cited.

## Source unit 315 · printed entry 315

### English candidate

Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafī. The compilers of the four Sunan transmitted sound reports from him through Syrian transmitters. ʿAbbās reported from Ibn Maʿīn that Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafī and Aws ibn Abī Aws al-Thaqafī were one person. It is said that Ibn Maʿīn erred in that and that the correct view is that they were two men. Abū Dāwūd and others followed Ibn Maʿīn in that view. The established conclusion is that they were two: whoever called Aws ibn Aws ‘Aws ibn Abī Aws’ erred, just as ‘Aws ibn Aws’ was said of Aws ibn Abī Aws, which too is an error. As for Aws ibn Abī Aws, his father’s name was Ḥudhayfa, as will appear.

## Source unit 317 · printed entry 317

### English candidate

Aws ibn Thābit ibn al-Mundhir ibn Ḥarām, the brother of Ḥassān al-Anṣārī. His mother was Sakhṭā bint Ḥāritha ibn Lawdhān, a paternal cousin of the mother of his brother Ḥassān. He was the father of the well-known Companion Shaddād ibn Aws. Ibn Isḥāq mentioned him among those who attended the Second ʿAqaba, Badr, and Uḥud, and said that he was killed at Uḥud. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmāra al-Qaddāḥ said the same in Nasab al-Anṣār. Concerning him, Ḥassān ibn Thābit says in an ode:

Among us is the slain man of the mountain pass, Aws ibn Thābit,
a martyr—and the battlefields made his renown sublime.

Al-Wāqidī claimed that he attended the Trench, Khaybar, and all the campaigns, and lived until the caliphate of ʿUthmān. الله أعلم. That claim is supported by what Ibn Zabāla mentioned in Akhbār al-Madīna, which I cited in the biography of Shaddād ibn Aws. The first view, however, is better established, because Ḥassān testified that he was present at the mountain pass. The cited ode is established in the recension of Ḥassān’s Dīwān prepared by Abū Saʿīd al-Sukkarī. Its opening is:

Lo, tell those who would hear of a battle
at which gray-haired, homebound women start up.

I shall mention some of it in the biography of his son Shaddād ibn Aws, إن شاء الله.

## Source unit 318 · printed entry 318

### English candidate

Aws ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī. Abū al-Shaykh related in his Tafsīr, by way of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ajlaḥ al-Kindī, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The people of the Jāhiliyya did not give inheritance to daughters or to young sons until they reached maturity. A man of the Anṣār called Aws ibn Thābit died, leaving two daughters and a young son. His two paternal cousins, Khālid and ʿArafaṭa, came and took his inheritance. His wife told the Prophet ﷺ of this, and God revealed: ‘For men is a share of what parents and close relatives leave’ [Qurʾān 4:7]. He sent word to Khālid and ʿArafaṭa: ‘Do not move anything from the inheritance.’

Abū al-Shaykh related it by another route from al-Kalbī, in which he named them Qatāda and ʿArafaṭa. Al-Thaʿlabī related it in his Tafsīr and named them Suwayd and ʿArafaṭa; in his version they were the two brothers of Aws. Ibn Manda stated in this man’s biography that he was Aws ibn Thābit, the brother of Ḥassān. This is an error, because none of Aws’s brothers or paternal uncles was called ʿArafaṭa or Khālid. Muqātil related it in his Tafsīr and said that Aws ibn Mālik died on the day of Uḥud, leaving his wife Umm Kujja and two daughters; he then related the story. More concerning this will appear in the biography of Umm Kujja among the women known by kunyahs, إن شاء الله تعالى.

## Source unit 319 · printed entry 319

### English candidate

Another Aws ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī. ## Source unit 320 · printed entry 320

### English candidate

Aws ibn Thaʿlaba ibn Zafar ibn ʿAmr ibn Aws al-Taymī. Al-Ḥākim said in his Tārīkh that he was among the Companions. He then related by way of Yazīd ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAbbād al-Taymī that Aws ibn Thaʿlaba entered Khurasan with Saʿīd ibn ʿUthmān, after which Saʿīd sent him to Herat. Sallamawayh stated that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir sent Aws ibn Thaʿlaba to Būshanj—that is, in the year 31.

Ibn ʿAsākir said in his Tārīkh: Aws ibn Thaʿlaba ibn Zafar ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Wadīʿa ibn Mālik ibn Taym Allāh ibn Thaʿlaba. Abū al-Qāsim al-Zajjājī gave him this lineage from Ibn Durayd. I say: al-Marzubānī also mentioned him in Muʿjam al-shuʿarāʾ and gave him that lineage, except that he said: Zafar ibn ʿAmr ibn Aws ibn Wadīʿa. He transmitted from Diʿbil that Aws was a poet who spanned the Jāhiliyya and Islam. Ibn Durayd related from Abū Ḥātim, from Abū ʿUbayda, from Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd, that Aws ibn Thaʿlaba, the owner of Qaṣr Aws in Basra, became involved in a contest with Ṭalḥa al-Ṭalaḥāt. Aws fled to Muʿāwiya, and he related to him the story and some verse. I say: Had al-Ḥākim not said that he was among the Companions, I would not have included him in this section.

## Source unit 321 · printed entry 321

### English candidate

Aws ibn Thaʿlaba al-Anṣārī. Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī mentioned in al-Maghāzī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that Aws was one of those who stayed behind the Messenger of God ﷺ on the campaign of Tabuk and one of those who tied himself to a pillar, until the words ‘And others have acknowledged their sins ...’ [Qurʾān 9:102] were revealed.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd said in his Tafsīr: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn ʿAṭāʾ informed us, from Saʿīd, from Qatāda, that it was revealed concerning seven men. Four of them tied themselves to the pillars: Abū Lubāba, Mirdās, Aws—whose lineage he did not give—and another whom he left unnamed. Ibn Jarīr related it by this route and named the fourth Khidām. He related the story by several routes but named only Abū Lubāba in them. In the biography of Aws ibn Khidām there will appear their number with their names, and that they were six.

## Source unit 324 · printed entry 324

### English candidate

Aws ibn Ḥāritha al-Ṭāʾī. Ibn Qāniʿ related by way of Ḥumayd ibn Munahhib, from his grandfather Aws ibn Ḥāritha, who said: ‘I came to the Prophet ﷺ with seventy riders of Ṭayyiʾ and pledged allegiance to him upon Islam.’ Ibn al-Dabbāgh added him as a supplement. Ibn Qāniʿ gave Aws ibn Ḥāritha’s lineage as ‘ibn Laʾm ibn ʿAmr,’ and so on. This is an error, for Aws ibn Ḥāritha ibn Laʾm died in the Jāhiliyya; it was his descendants who lived into Islam, such as ʿUrwa ibn Muḍarris ibn Ḥāritha and Hāniʾ ibn Qabīṣa ibn Aws. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr mentioned Buḥayr ibn Aws ibn Ḥāritha ibn Laʾm and said: ‘There is doubt concerning his Islam.’

I say: Aws ibn Ḥāritha is not Ḥumayd ibn Munahhib’s immediate grandfather. He is Ḥumayd ibn Munahhib ibn Ḥāritha ibn Khuraym ibn Aws ibn Ḥāritha ibn Laʾm ibn ʿAmr ibn Ṭarīf ibn Mālik ibn Judʿāʾ ibn Dhuhl ibn Rūmān ibn Jundab ibn Khārija ibn Saʿd ibn Fiṭra ibn Ṭayyiʾ. Khuraym ibn Aws, the grandfather of Ḥumayd’s father, had Companionship, as will appear. Perhaps the report originally said ‘from his grandfather Khuraym ibn Aws ibn Ḥāritha,’ and Khuraym dropped out. والله أعلم.

I found evidence supporting this. Ibn Qāniʿ said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Akhbārī related to us; Zakariyyā ibn Yaḥyā related to us; Zaḥr ibn Ḥuṣayn related to us, from his grandfather Ḥumayd ibn Munahhib, from his grandfather Aws ibn Ḥāritha ibn Laʾm al-Ṭāʾī, who said: ‘I came to the Prophet ﷺ with seventy riders of my people and pledged allegiance to him upon Islam’—the lengthy report. I say: Ibn Qāniʿ abridged it, mentioning one part and then saying, ‘He related a lengthy report.’ We transmitted that report in the fascicle of Abū al-Sikkīn—namely the aforementioned Zakariyyā ibn Yaḥyā al-Ṭāʾifī—through Abū ʿUbayd ibn Jarmawayh the judge, from him. He said: ‘My father’s paternal uncle, Zaḥr ibn Ḥuṣn, related to us, from his grandfather Ḥumayd ibn Munahhib, who said: My grandfather Khuraym ibn Aws ibn Ḥāritha said, “I migrated to the Messenger of God ﷺ when he was returning from Tabuk. I came to him and embraced Islam.”’ He then related a lengthy report. It thus became clear that the report belongs to Khuraym ibn Aws, not to Aws. والله أعلم.

In al-Tārīkh al-Muẓaffarī it is reported that Aws ibn Ḥāritha ibn Laʾm al-Ṭāʾī came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, ‘Stretch out your hand.’ The Prophet asked, ‘For what?’ Aws replied, ‘So that I may bear witness that there is no god but God, without doubt; that you are the Messenger of God, without misgiving; and that with this’—he pointed to his sword—‘I will strike whomever you command me to strike.’ The Prophet said, ‘You have done well. May God bless you.’ His son Khuraym ibn Aws was a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ. End of quotation. Perhaps Aws lived long enough to reach Islam.

I then saw in Ibn al-Kalbī’s Jamhara that Aws ibn Ḥāritha lived for two hundred years. Abū Mikhnaf Lūṭ ibn Yaḥyā stated in Kitāb al-Muʿammarīn that this Aws ibn Ḥāritha lived for two hundred years, until he became decrepit and lost his hearing and reason. He had been the chief of his people. His sons departed and left him in their open courtyard until he perished there, abandoned. They are reviled for that to this day. Al-Asḥam ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Ṭarīf ibn ʿAmr ibn Thumāma ibn Mālik ibn Judʿāʾ al-Ṭāʾī said concerning it:

News came to me in the encampment that Aws,
at Laḥmān, died of wasting away.
His family moved on and left him entrusted
to a worn cloak woven of wool.

End of quotation. This indicates that he died in the Jāhiliyya.

## Source unit 326 · printed entry 326

### English candidate

Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān ibn ʿAwf ibn Rabīʿa ibn Saʿīd ibn Yarbūʿ ibn Wāthila ibn Dahmān ibn Naṣr ibn Muʿāwiya ibn Bakr ibn Hawāzin, al-Naṣrī—with nūn. Ibn Ḥibbān said that he was said to have Companionship.

Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim related by way of ʿUmar ibn Ṣahbān—who is weak—from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān, from his father, as a report traced back to the Prophet: ‘Give the zakāt al-fiṭr: one ṣāʿ of food’—the report. Ibn Manda mentioned it and said that it was an error. Ibn Manda also related by way of Abū Ḍamra, from Salama ibn Wardān, from Mālik ibn Aws, from his father, as a report traced back to the Prophet: ‘Whoever abandons lying while he is in the wrong, a house will be built for him in the outskirts of Paradise’—the report. The chain through Salama is disputed, in addition to his weakness.

I read in Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr’s handwriting: ‘Were it not for the report of Kaʿb ibn Mālik, I would not affirm Companionship for him.’ I say: He means the report Muslim transmitted by way of Abū al-Zubayr, from a son of Kaʿb ibn Mālik, from his father: the Prophet ﷺ sent him and Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān to proclaim during the Days of Tashrīq, ‘The days of Minā are days of eating and drinking.’ Ibn Manda said: ‘This is a sound, uncommon report; we know it only by this route.’

## Source unit 327 · printed entry 327

### English candidate

Aws ibn Ḥudhayfa ibn Rabīʿa ibn Abī Salama ibn Ghayra ibn ʿAwf. It is also said that Ḥudhayfa was the son of Abī ʿAmr ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf ibn Wahb ibn ʿĀmir ibn Yasār ibn Mālik ibn Ḥuṭayṭ ibn Jusham al-Thaqafī. He is Aws ibn Abī Aws. Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī, and Ibn Māja transmitted from him, and sound reports have come by his route. He was the father of ʿAmr ibn Aws and the grandfather of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aws.

Aḥmad said: ‘Aws ibn Abī Aws is Aws ibn Ḥudhayfa.’ Al-Bukhārī said in his Tārīkh, as did Ibn Ḥibbān: ‘Aws ibn Ḥudhayfa, father of ʿAmr; he is also called Aws ibn Abī Aws and Aws ibn Aws.’ Abū Nuʿaym said: ‘The earlier authorities disagreed concerning this man’; he then listed the three forms. He next said: ‘As for Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafī, the Syrians relate from him; he too has been called Aws ibn Abī Aws.’ He then said that Aws ibn Ḥudhayfa died in the year 59.

## Source unit 331 · printed entry 331

### English candidate

Aws ibn Khālid ibn Qurṭ ibn Qays ibn Wahb ibn Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār al-Anṣārī al-Najjārī. They omitted him from their accounts of the Companions, but he was a Companion, because his son Ṣafwān ibn Aws was a well-known Successor. Ṣafwān was married to ʿAmra bint Abī Ayyūb al-Anṣārī. This Ṣafwān’s mother was Nāʾila bint al-Rabīʿ ibn Qays ibn ʿĀmir, one of the women who pledged allegiance.

On this reasoning, Aws was a Companion: had he died in the Jāhiliyya, his son would have had Companionship; but the son was a Successor. This indicates that his father died after the Prophet ﷺ. No one among the Anṣār in Medina remained an unbeliever during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ.

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

## Source unit 332 · printed entry 332

### English candidate

Aws ibn Khālid ibn Yazīd ibn Munhib al-Ṭāʾī, a paternal cousin of Zayd al-Khayl. Ibn al-Kalbī mentioned him and said that he came as a delegate. He also had a story from the time of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. During his caliphate, ʿUmar sent a man called Abū Sufyān to test the recitation of the desert people; whoever could not recite, he beat. He tested Aws ibn Khālid, who could not recite, so Abū Sufyān struck him with several lashes, from which he died. His mother then stood lamenting him. When she told Ḥurayth ibn Zayd al-Khayl al-Ṭāʾī the news, he rushed at Abū Sufyān and killed him. He said verses about that, including:

“Do not grieve, O mother of Aws, for indeed
every barefoot man and every shod man meets death.
If you kill Aws, a mighty man, then I
have killed Abū Sufyān as he clung to the saddle.”

Abū al-Faraj al-Iṣbahānī mentioned this from Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī and added that the slain Abū Sufyān was a man of Quraysh.

## Source unit 333 · printed entry 333

### English candidate

Aws ibn Khidām al-Anṣārī. Abū al-Shaykh transmitted in his Tafsīr, by way of al-Thawrī, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Sufyān, from Jābir, who said: Six men were among those who stayed behind when the Messenger of God ﷺ went to Tabūk: Abū Lubāba, Aws ibn Khidām, Thaʿlaba ibn Wadīʿa, Kaʿb ibn Mālik, Murāra ibn al-Rabīʿ, and Hilāl ibn Umayya. Abū Lubāba, Aws, and Thaʿlaba came, tied themselves to the pillars, and brought their property. They said, “O Messenger of God, take it. This is what kept us from you.” He said, “I will not release them until there is fighting.” Then the Qurʾan was revealed: “And others have acknowledged their sins ...” [Qurʾan 9:102]. Its chain is strong.

Ibn Manda transmitted it by this route and added after it, “Others transmitted it from al-Aʿmash.” Ibn Mardawayh cited it by way of al-ʿAwfī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, similarly and more fully, but he named only Abū Lubāba among them. It was stated above in the biography of Aws ibn Thaʿlaba that they were seven. والله أعلم.

## Source unit 334 · printed entry 334

### English candidate

Aws ibn Khawlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUbayd ibn Mālik ibn Sālim ibn Ghanm ibn ʿAwf ibn al-Khazraj, the Anṣārī of the Khazraj. He is also called Aws ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Khawlī. Ibn al-Madīnī said that his kunya was Abū Laylā.

Al-Baghawī said in his Muʿjam: ʿAlī ibn Muslim related to us; Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm Abū Yūsuf related to us; Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād related to us, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “Those who washed the Prophet ﷺ were ʿAlī and al-Faḍl.” The Anṣār said, “We adjure you by God and by our right!” So they admitted with them a man called Aws ibn Khawlī, a strong man who carried the water jar in his hand. More than one transmitter followed Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād in this report.

Ibn Shāhīn transmitted something similar by way of Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ibn ʿAbbās. Ibn Isḥāq mentioned something similar in al-Maghāzī without a chain. Al-Baghawī said: “I know of no musnad report from Aws.” I say: Ibn Manda cited for him a report by way of Hind ibn Abī Hāla, from Aws ibn Khawlī, that the Prophet ﷺ said to him, “Whoever humbles himself before God, God raises him.” Its chain contains Khārija ibn Muṣʿab, who is weak, and also someone who is unknown.

I say: Aws is also mentioned in other reports. Among them is what Ibn Isḥāq mentioned in al-Sīra, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, who said: “Those who descended into the grave of the Messenger of God ﷺ were ʿAlī, al-Faḍl, Qutham, Shuqrān, and Aws ibn Khawlī.” He also transmitted it from Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it by this latter route; Ḥusayn is weak.

Al-Madāʾinī and others mentioned that during the Fulfilled ʿUmra the Prophet ﷺ stationed him at Dhū Ṭuwā to thwart any stratagem should Quraysh devise one against him, and stationed Bashīr ibn Saʿd at Marr al-Ẓahrān. Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd mentioned him, from al-Zuhrī, from a son of Kaʿb ibn Mālik, among those who set out to fight Ibn Abī al-Ḥuqayq. Al-Zuhrī, Mūsā ibn ʿUqba, Ibn Isḥāq, and others mentioned him among those who witnessed Badr. The Messenger of God ﷺ established brotherhood between him and Shujāʿ ibn Wahb. Ibn Saʿd said that Aws ibn Khawlī died before the siege of ʿUthmān.

## Source unit 336 · printed entry 336

### English candidate

Aws ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ al-ʿĀmirī. He was among those who embraced Islam at the Conquest, settled in Medina, and marked out a house there. Ibn Fatḥūn mentioned him from ʿUmar ibn Shabba. I found a report indicating that he lived until ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān’s governorship over Medina, or until his caliphate.

Al-Fākihī transmitted by way of Ibn Jurayj: ʿIkrima ibn Khālid ibn Aws ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ, a man of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, informed me: “We had a dwelling in Dār al-Ḥakam. During his governorship, ʿAbd al-Malik said, ‘Sell me your dwelling that is in Dār Abī al-ʿĀṣ.’ I replied, ‘It is not Dār Abī al-ʿĀṣ; it is our own house. It was ours in the Age of Ignorance, and then we embraced Islam in it.’ He said, ‘It was never yours—by my life!’ I said, ‘Whatever it may have been, it is ours by the judgment of the Messenger of God ﷺ.’ He said, ‘You have spoken truly. Sell it to me.’ I replied, ‘Not for money, but for a house.’ So I sold it to him in exchange for a house at Ḥirmānas.”

## Source unit 339 · printed entry 339

### English candidate

Aws ibn Samʿān al-Anṣārī. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: “He has a report whose chain is not strong.” I say: Ibn Manda transmitted it by way of Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd, from Hilāl ibn Yazīd ibn Yasār—Abū ʿIqāl, one of the weak transmitters—who said: Anas ibn Mālik informed me that the Messenger of God ﷺ said, “God sent me as guidance and mercy to all beings, and sent me to obliterate flutes and musical instruments.” Aws ibn Samʿān said, “O Messenger of God, by the One who sent you with the truth, I find it likewise in the Torah.” Ibn Manda said: “Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam alone transmitted it from Ibrāhīm.”

## Source unit 341 · printed entry 341

### English candidate

Aws ibn Shuraḥbīl, one of Banū al-Mujammaʿ. He had Companionship, and his report is known among the Syrians; Ibn Ḥibbān said this. He will appear under Shuraḥbīl ibn Aws.

Abū Bakr ibn ʿĪsā distinguished the two in his History of the People of Homs, saying: “Among the Companions who settled in Homs were Shuraḥbīl ibn Aws and Aws ibn Shuraḥbīl.” Thus he made them two people. Ibn Shāhīn likewise allowed this possibility. Al-Baghawī said: “In my view the more correct form is Shuraḥbīl ibn Aws.”

Al-Bukhārī cited his report without a full chain in al-Tārīkh, while Ibn Shāhīn and al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it with a Syrian chain by way of al-Zubaydī, from ʿAyyāsh ibn Muʾnis, from Abū al-Ḥasan Nimrān ibn Makhmar: Aws ibn Shuraḥbīl, one of Banū al-Mujammaʿ, related to him that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, “Whoever walks with an oppressor in order to aid him, knowing that he is an oppressor, has departed from faith.”

## Source unit 342 · printed entry 342

### English candidate

Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit ibn Qays ibn Aṣram ibn Fihr ibn Thaʿlaba ibn Ghanm ibn Sālim ibn ʿAwf ibn al-Khazraj, the Anṣārī, brother of ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit. They mentioned him among those who witnessed Badr and the other campaigns.

Abū Dāwūd said: Hārūn ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us; Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl related to us; Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha: Jamīla was married to Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit, who was a man afflicted by spells of mental disturbance. She then related the report of ẓihār. Shādhān followed ʿĀrim in transmitting it connected. Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl transmitted it from Ḥammād as a disconnected report. Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh and a group likewise transmitted it from Hishām, from his father, as a disconnected report.

Al-Bazzār transmitted by way of Abū Ḥamza al-Thumālī, who is weak, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “In the Age of Ignorance, when a man said to his wife, ‘You are to me like my mother’s back,’ she became forbidden to him. The first man to pronounce ẓihār in Islam was a man married to a paternal cousin called Khuwayla.” He transmitted it without naming the man. Ibn Shāhīn and Ibn Manda transmitted it by this route with the wording: “The first ẓihār in Islam was by Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit; he was married to a paternal cousin.”

ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it from Ibn ʿUyayna, from Thābit al-Thumālī, from ʿIkrima, as a disconnected report. He called her Khawla and called him Uways ibn al-Ṣāmit, in the diminutive, and related the story at length.

Abū Dāwūd transmitted by way of Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, from Khuwayla bint Mālik ibn Thaʿlaba, who said: “My husband Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit pronounced ẓihār against me.” She related the report. Its chain is sound.

Al-Dāraquṭnī and al-Ṭabarānī, in Musnad al-Shāmiyyīn, transmitted by way of Saʿīd ibn Bashīr, from Qatāda, from Anas, that Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit pronounced ẓihār against his wife Khawla bint Thaʿlaba. Ibn Manda said: “Saʿīd ibn Bashīr alone transmitted it connected.” Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba transmitted it from Qatāda as a disconnected report.

Abū Dāwūd transmitted by way of ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit, a report. He then said: “ʿAṭāʾ did not meet Aws. He was one of the people of Badr and died early.” Ibn Ḥibbān said that he died during the days of ʿUthmān at the age of eighty-five. Another authority said that he died in the year thirty-four at Ramla, at the age of seventy-two.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

أوس بن الصامت بن قيس بن أصرم بن فهر بن ثعلبة بن غنم بن سالم بن عوف بن الخزرج الأنصاري أخو عبادة بن الصامت ذكروه فيمن شهد بدرا والمشاهد وقال أبو داود حدثنا هارون بن عبد الله حدثنا محمد بن الفضل حدثنا حماد بن سلمة عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أن جميلة كانت تحت أوس بن الصامت وكان رجلا به لمم فذكر حديث الظهار وتابع عازما على وصله شاذان ورواه موسى بن إسماعيل عن حماد مرسلا وهكذا رواه إسماعيل بن عياش وجماعة عن هشام عن أبيه مرسلا وروى البراز من طريق أبي حمزة الثمالي وفيه ضعف عن عكرمة عن بن عباس قال كان الرجل إذا قال لزوجته في الجاهلية أنت علي كظهر أمي حرمت عليه وكان أول من ظاهر في الإسلام رجل كان تحته بنت عم له يقال لها خويلة كذا أخرجه مبهما وقد رواه بن شاهين وابن منده من هذا الوجه بلفظ أول ظهار كان في الإسلام من أوس بن الصامت كانت تحته بنت عم له وأخرجه عبد الرزاق عن بن عيينة عن ثابت الثمالي عن عكرمة مرسلا فسماها خولة وسماه أويس بن الصامت بالتصغير وساق القصة مطولة وروى أبو داود من طريق يوسف بن عبد الله بن سلام عن خويلة بنت مالك بن ثعلبة قالت ظاهر مني زوجي أوس بن الصامت فذكر الحديث وإسناده حسن وروى الدار قطني والطبراني في مسند الشاميين من طريق سعيد بن بشير عن قتادة عن أنس أن أوس بن الصامت ظاهر من امرأته خولة بنت ثعلبة قال بن منده تفرد بوصله سعيد بن بشير ورواه سعيد بن أبي عروبة عن قتادة مرسلا وروى أبو داود من طريق عطاء بن أبي رباح عن أوس بن الصامت حديثا وقال بعده عطاء لم يدرك أوسا هو من أهل بدر قديم الموت وقال بن حبان مات في أيام عثمان وله خمس وثمانون سنة وقال غيره مات سنة أربع وثلاثين بالرملة وهو بن اثنتين وسبعين سنة

## Source unit 344 · printed entry 344

### English candidate

Aws ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥajar al-Aslamī, with the kunya Abū Tamīm. He is sometimes ascribed to his grandfather and called Aws ibn Ḥajar. Al-Baghawī, Ibn al-Sakan, and Ibn Manda transmitted by way of Fayḍ ibn Wathīq, from Ṣakhr ibn Mālik ibn Iyās ibn Mālik ibn Aws ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥajar al-Aslamī, a shaykh from al-ʿArj, who said: My father, Mālik ibn Iyās ibn Mālik, informed me that his father Iyās informed him that his father Mālik ibn Aws informed him that his father Aws ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥajar al-Aslamī was passed by the Messenger of God ﷺ and Abū Bakr while they were heading toward Medina, among large trees between al-Juḥfa and Harshā. They were riding one camel, so he mounted them upon a breeding male from his camels and sent with them a servant named Masʿūd, telling him, ‘Take them by the passes of the road that you know, and do not leave them.’ He then related the report. Al-Ṭabarānī also transmitted it; in his wording, [Ṣakhr’s] father Mālik ibn Aws ibn Ḥajar informed him that his father Aws ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥajar said, ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ passed by me’—then he related it. Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Sarrāj transmitted it in his Tārīkh from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād al-ʿUklī, from his brother Mūsā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yasār, from Iyās ibn Mālik ibn Aws, who said, ‘When the Messenger of God ﷺ emigrated...’ and related it as a mursal report. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said, ‘The channel for his report is through his descendants, and it is a ḥasan report.’ He said, ‘It has also been said that he was Abū Aws ibn Tamīm ibn Ḥajar.’ I say: one of the transmitters inverted it. Al-Ḥākim transmitted in al-Iklīl by way of al-Wāqidī: Ibn Abī Sabra related to me, from al-Ḥārith ibn Fuḍayl: Ibn Masʿūd ibn Hunayda related to me, from his father, from his grandfather Masʿūd, who said: I met the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said, ‘Where are you headed, Masʿūd?’ I replied, ‘I came to greet you. Abū Tamīm Aws ibn Ḥajar has set me free.’ He said, ‘May God bless you.’ Another route for his report will appear in the biography of Mālik ibn Aws. I say: Ibn Mākūlā vocalized the name of Aws’s father with two fatḥas, Ḥajar; it is also said with the first letter ḍamma and the second quiescent, Ḥujr.

## Source unit 351 · printed entry 351

### English candidate

Aws ibn Qayẓī ibn ʿAmr ibn Zayd ibn Jusham ibn Ḥāritha ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Aws al-Anṣārī al-Awsī, the father of ʿUrāba. He attended Uḥud, as did his two sons ʿUrāba and ʿAbd Allāh. It is said that Aws ibn Qayẓī was a hypocrite and that he was the one who said, ‘Our houses are exposed.’ Abū al-Shaykh transmitted in his Tafsīr by way of Ibn Isḥāq, who said: A trustworthy man related to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: Shās ibn Qays, a Jew of immense unbelief, passed by a group of al-Aws and al-Khazraj who were conversing. The harmony he saw among them after their former enmity angered him. He ordered a Jewish youth with him to sit among them and remind them of the Day of Buʿāth. The youth did so, and they disputed and quarreled until two men sprang up: Aws ibn Qayẓī of al-Aws and Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr of al-Khazraj. They exchanged words, the two parties became angry, and they leapt up to fight. The news reached the Messenger of God ﷺ, who came, admonished them, and reconciled them. They listened and obeyed. God then revealed concerning Aws, Jabbār, and those with them: ‘O you who believe, if you obey a group of those who were given the Scripture, they will turn you back, after your faith, as unbelievers.’ And concerning Shās ibn Qays: ‘People of the Scripture, why do you bar from God’s path those who believe...?’—the verse. The report is long; I have abridged it. Its isnad is mursal and contains an unnamed transmitter. Abū ʿUmar cited it.

## Source unit 358 · printed entry 358

### English candidate

Aws ibn Muʿayr, Abū Maḥdhūra. He will appear under the kunyās. Khalīfa and al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār gave his name as Aws; Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, Ibn Maʿīn, Ibn Saʿd, and Abū Khaythama gave it as Samura. It is also reported from Ibn Maʿīn that his name was Muʿayr ibn Nufayr; Ibn Shāhīn transmitted it thus. Abū ʿUmar said, ‘It has been said that Aws ibn Muʿayr was the brother of Abū Maḥdhūra, but that is open to question. The first view’—meaning that Aws was Abū Maḥdhūra’s personal name—‘is sounder and better known.’ He then transmitted from Ibn al-Zubayr that Abū Maḥdhūra’s name was Aws and that he had a brother named Anīs who was killed as an unbeliever. Ibn Ḥazm stated this categorically and declared those who disagreed mistaken. Abū al-Yaqẓān reported that Abū Maḥdhūra’s name was Samura, while his brother’s name was Aws and he was killed at Badr as an unbeliever.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

أوس بن معير أبو محذورة يأتي في الكنى سماه خليفة والزبير بن بكار أوسا وسماه أحمد بن حنبل وابن معين وابن سعد وأبو خيثمة سمرة وقيل عن بن معين اسمه معير بن نفير كذا نقله بن شاهين وقال أبو عمر قد قيل إن أوس بن معير أخو أبي محذورة وفي ذلك نظر والأول يعني أنه اسم أبي محذورة أصح وأشهر ثم نقل عن بن الزبير أن اسم أبي محذورة أوس وأن له أخا اسمه أنيس قتل كافرا وبه جزم بن حزم وخطأ من خالفه وعن أبي اليقظان أن اسم أبي محذورة سمرة وأن أخاه اسمه أوس وقتل يوم بدر كافرا

</div>

## Source unit 376 · printed entry 376

### English candidate

Iyās ibn Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr mentioned him among the Companions and said, “He praised the Prophet ﷺ in verse.” This is questionable.

I say: If he is the man from whom Abū al-ʿUmays transmitted, then he did not have Companionship, because he was born in the time of ʿUthmān. If Salama had another son also called Iyās, then it is possible. Al-Marzubānī preceded Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr in mentioning this in his Muʿjam, but he did not expressly say that Iyās had Companionship. Rather, in his biography of him he said: “He is the one who said, praising the Prophet ﷺ:

‘Generous in character, glorious; and his speech
is truth, containing mercy and chastisement.
The children of Qayla around him are in a thicket,
like lions, around which the cubs strut.’”

The reason for questioning the claim is that praising the Prophet ﷺ does not necessarily mean that a man had Companionship.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

إياس بن سلمة بن الأكوع ذكره بن عبد البر في الصحابة وقال مدح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بشعر وفيه نظر قلت إن كان هو الذي روى عنه أبو العميس فليست له صحبة لأنه ولد في زمن عثمان وإن كان لسلمة بن يقال له إياس أيضا فهو محتمل وقد سبق بن عبد البر إلى ذلك المرزباني في معجمه لكن لم يصرح بان له صحبة بل قال في ترجمته هو القائل يمدح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم <br />
 سمح الخليقة ماجد وكلامه <br />
 حق وفيه رحمة ونكال <br />
 أولاد قيلة حوله في غابة <br />
 كالاسد ترفأ حولها الاشبال وكان وجه النظر من كونه لا يلزم من مدحه للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يكون له صحبة

</div>

## Source unit 377 · printed entry 377

### English candidate

Iyās ibn Sahl al-Juhanī, an ally of the Anṣār. Ibn Manda mentioned him. Abū Nuʿaym said, “I think he was a Successor.”

Ibn Manda transmitted by way of Mūsā ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard someone who related to me from Iyās al-Juhanī that he used to say: Muʿādh said, “O Prophet of God, which faith is best?” He replied, “That you love for God, hate for God, and keep your tongue working in the remembrance of God.”

He also transmitted that Muṣʿab ibn al-Miqdām reported from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Madanī, from Abū Ḥāzim, that Abū Ḥāzim sat with Iyās ibn Sahl al-Anṣārī in the mosque of Banū Sāʿida. Iyās said to him, “Turn toward me, Abū Ḥāzim, so that I may relate to you from the Prophet ﷺ.”

I say: The first chain is disconnected. In the second is Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm—namely Ibn Abī Ḥumayd—one of the weak transmitters.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

إياس بن سهل الجهني حليف الأنصار ذكره بن منده قال أبو نعيم أظنه تابعيا روى بن منده من طريق موسى بن جبير سمعت من حدثني عن إياس الجهني أنه كان يقول قال معاذ يا نبي الله أي الإيمان أفضل قال تحب لله وتبغض لله وتعمل لسانك في ذكر الله قال وروى مصعب بن المقدام عن محمد بن إبراهيم المدني عن أبي حازم أنه جلس إلى إياس بن سهل الأنصاري في مسجد بني ساعدة فقال لي أقبل علي أبا حازم أحدثك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قلت الإسناد الأول منقطع وفي الثاني محمد بن إبراهيم وهو بن أبي حميد أحد الضعفاء

## Source unit 383 · printed entry 383

### English candidate

Iyās ibn ʿAbd, Abū ʿAwf al-Muzanī. Al-Bukhārī and Ibn Ḥibbān said that he had Companionship. The compilers of the Sunan and Aḥmad transmitted one report from him concerning the sale of water. Al-Baghawī and Ibn al-Sakan said that he transmitted no other report. His kunya is also said to have been Abū al-Furāt. He settled in Kufa.

Al-Baghawī said: ʿAlī ibn Salama related to us; Ibn ʿUyayna related to us. He said: “I inquired about him in Kufa and was informed that he was one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ.”

Al-Baghawī also transmitted by way of Ibn ʿUyayna, who said: I asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿqil ibn Muqarrin al-Muzanī, “Do you know Iyās ibn ʿAbd al-Muzanī?” He replied, “He is my maternal grandfather.”

He also transmitted by way of ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Abū al-Minhāl—ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muṭʿim—who said: “I heard Iyās ibn ʿAbd, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ,” and he related a report that stopped with the Companion.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

إياس بن عبد أبو عوف المزني قال البخاري وابن حبان له صحبة روى له أصحاب السنن وأحمد حديثا في بيع الماء قال البغوي وابن السكن لم يرو غيره ويقال كنيته أبو الفرات نزل الكوفة قال البغوي حدثنا علي بن سلمة حدثنا بن عيينة قال سألت عنه بالكوفة فأخبرت أنه من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وروى أيضا من طريق بن عيينة قال سألت عبد الله بن الوليد بن عبد الله بن معقل بن مقرن المزني قلت تعرف إياس بن عبد المزني فقال هو جدي أبو أمي وروى أيضا من طريق عمرو بن دينار عن أبي المنهال وهو عبد الرحمن بن مطعم قال سمعت إياس بن عبد صاحب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكر حديثا موقوفا

## Source unit 387 · printed entry 387

### English candidate

Iyās ibn Muʿādh al-Anṣārī al-Ashhalī. Ibn al-Sakan and Ibn Ḥibbān said that he had Companionship. Al-Bukhārī mentioned him in al-Tārīkh al-Awsaṭ among the earliest Emigrants and Anṣār who died during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, and gave him a biography in al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr.

Muṣʿab al-Zubayrī said: “Iyās came to Mecca as a youth before the Hijra, then returned and died before the Prophet’s ﷺ migration. His people reported that he died a Muslim.”

Ibn Isḥāq said in al-Maghāzī: al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿd ibn Muʿādh related to me, from Maḥmūd ibn Labīd, who said: When Abū al-Ḥaysar Anas ibn Rāfiʿ came to Mecca accompanied by youths of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal, among them Iyās ibn Muʿādh, seeking an alliance from Quraysh against their people of al-Khazraj, the Messenger of God ﷺ heard of them. He came and sat with them and said, “Would you like something better than that for which you have come?” They asked, “What is that?” He replied, “I am the Messenger of God. God sent me to His servants to call them to worship Him and not associate anything with Him.” He then explained Islam to them and recited the Qurʾan to them.

Iyās ibn Muʿādh said, “My people, by God, this is better than that for which you came.” Abū al-Ḥaysar took a handful of gravel from al-Baṭḥāʾ, struck Iyās in the face with it, and said, “Leave us alone! By my life, we came for something other than this.” Iyās fell silent. They rose and departed. The battle of Buʿāth then took place between al-Aws and al-Khazraj. Not long afterward, Iyās ibn Muʿādh died.

Maḥmūd ibn Labīd said: Someone from Iyās’s people who was present at his death informed me that they continued to hear him declare God’s oneness, magnify Him, praise Him, and glorify Him until he died. They had no doubt that he died a Muslim.

A group transmitted it in this form from Ibn Isḥāq, and it is among his sound reports. Ziyād al-Bakkāʾī, however, transmitted it from Ibn Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr instead of al-Ḥusayn. The first is more likely; al-Bukhārī indicated this in his History.

إياس بن معاذ الأنصاري الأشهلي قال بن السكن وابن حبان له صحبة وذكره البخاري في تاريخه الأوسط فيمن مات على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من المهاجرين الأولين والأنصار وترجم له في التاريخ الكبير وقال مصعب الزبيري قدم إياس مكة وهو غلام قبل الهجرة فرجع ومات قبل هجرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وذكر قومه أنه مات مسلما وقال بن إسحاق في المغازي حدثني الحصين بن عبد الرحمن بن عمرو بن سعد بن معاذ عن محمود بن لبيد قال لما قدم أبو الحيسر أنس بن رافع مكة ومعه فتية من بني عبد الأشهل فيهم إياس بن معاذ يلتمسون الحلف من قريش على قومهم من الخزرج سمع بهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأتاهم فجلس إليهم فقال لهم هل لكم إلى خير مما جئتم له قالوا وما ذاك قال أنا رسول الله بعثني إلى العباد ادعوهم إلى أن يعبدوه ولا يشركوا به شيئا ثم ذكر لهم الإسلام وتلا عليهم القرآن فقال إياس بن معاذ ياقوم هذا والله خير مما جئتم به فأخذ أبو الحيسر حفنة من البطحاء فضرب وجهه بها وقال دعنا منك فلعمري لقد جئنا لغير هذا فسكت وقام وانصرفوا فكانت وقعة بعاث بين الأوس والخزرج ثم لم يلبث إياس بن معاذ أن هلك قال محمود بن لبيد فأخبرني من حضره من قومه أنهم لم يزالوا يسمعونه يهلل الله ويكبره ويحمده ويسبحه فكانوا لايشكون أنه مات مسلما رواه جماعة عن بن إسحاق هكذا وهو من صحيح حديثه لكن رواه زياد البكائي عن بن إسحاق عن محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن عمرو بدل الحصين والأول أرجح اشار إلى ذلك البخاري في تاريخه

## Source unit 388 · printed entry 388

### English candidate

Iyās ibn Hilāl ibn Ribāb ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī, Abū Qurra. He and his son had Companionship; Ibn Qutayba said this.

Al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Māja, Ibn Abī Khaythama, Ibn al-Sakan, al-Bāwardī, and others transmitted by way of Yūsuf ibn al-Mubārak, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs, from Khālid ibn Abī Karīma, from Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra, from his father: the Prophet ﷺ sent his father—the grandfather of Muʿāwiya—to a man who had consummated marriage with his son’s wife; he struck off the man’s head and took one-fifth of his property. Its chain is sound.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Waḍḍāḥ and Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAtakī likewise transmitted it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs. Ibn al-Sakan said: “He is known as Yūsuf. No trustworthy transmitter other than him narrated it.”

I say: Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh transmitted it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs without mentioning Qurra in its chain. Ibn Abī Khaythama reported from Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn: “This is a sound report. It is as though Ibn Idrīs gave it a connected chain for some people and a disconnected chain for others.”

Ibn Qāniʿ, al-Bāwardī, and Ibn ʿAdī transmitted in al-Kāmil, by way of Furāt ibn Abī al-Furāt, from Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra, from his father, that he went with his father to the Prophet ﷺ and saw the Prophet’s waist-wrapper loosened. He inserted his hand and placed it on the seal.

إياس بن هلال بن رئاب بن عبد الله المزني أبو قرة له ولولده صحبة قاله بن قتيبة وروى النسائي وابن ماجة وابن أبي خيثمة وابن السكن والباوردي وغيرهم من طريق يوسف بن المبارك عن عبد الله بن إدريس عن خالد بن أبي كريمة عن معاوية بن قرة عن أبيه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث أباه جد معاوية إلى رجل عرس بامرأة ابنه فضرب عنقه وخمس ماله إسناده حسن وهكذا رواه عبد الله بن الوضاح وأحمد بن عبد الله العتكي عن عبد الله بن إدريس وقال بن السكن هو معروف بيوسف لم يروه من الثقات غيره قلت قد رواه إسحاق بن راهويه عن عبد الله بن إدريس فلم يذكر قرة في إسناده وقال بن أبي خيثمة عن يحيى بن معين هذا حديث صحيح كأن بن إدريس اسنده لقوم وأرسله لآخرين وروى بن قانع والباوردي وابن عدي في الكامل من طريق فرات بن أبي الفرات عن معاوية بن قرة عن أبيه أنه ذهب مع أبيه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فرآه محلول الإزار فأدخل يده فوضعها في الخاتم

## Source unit 392 · printed entry 392

### English candidate

Iymāʾ ibn Rukhṣa ibn Khirba ibn Khifāf ibn Ḥāritha ibn Ghifār. He embraced Islam early. Ibn al-Madīnī said that he had Companionship.

Ḥanẓala al-Aslamī transmitted from Khifāf ibn Iymāʾ ibn Raḥḍa the report of the qunūt. Some transmitters instead said, “from Iymāʾ ibn Raḥḍa.”

Muslim transmitted in his Ṣaḥīḥ the story of Abū Dharr’s conversion by way of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣāmit, from Abū Dharr. It states: “We came to our people, and half of them embraced Islam before the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Medina. Iymāʾ ibn Raḥḍa al-Ghifārī used to lead them in prayer.”

Aḥmad, however, mentioned the disagreement in this report from Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīra: was the narrator Khifāf ibn Iymāʾ, or his father Iymāʾ ibn Raḥḍa? On that basis, it is possible that Khifāf’s Islam preceded his father’s. والله أعلم.

Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār mentioned, from a report of Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām, that Iymāʾ ibn Raḥḍa was present at Badr with the polytheists, which would place his Islam after that. Ibn Saʿd said that he embraced Islam near the time of al-Ḥudaybiya. This conflicts with Muslim’s recension.

Ibn Saʿd said that he lived at Ghayqa near al-Suqyā and would go for refuge or residence to Medina. His son Khifāf will be mentioned in his proper place.

The cited story from Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām says: “ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa hurried out, and I went out with him so that no good might escape me. ʿUtba was weeping over Iymāʾ ibn Raḥḍa al-Ghifārī, who had presented ten camels to the polytheists.”

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

إيماء بن رخصة بن خربة بن خفاف بن حارثة بن غفار قديم الإسلام قال بن المديني له صحبة قال وقد روى حنظلة الأسلمي عن خفاف بن إيماء بن رحضة حديث القنوت وقال بعضهم عن إيماء بن رحضة وروى مسلم في صحيحه قصة إسلام أبي ذر من طريق عبد الله بن الصامت عن أبي ذر وفيها جئنا قومنا فأسلم نصفهم قبل أن يقدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة وكان يأمهم إيماء بن رحضة الغفاري ولكن ذكر أحمد في هذا الحديث الاختلاف على رواية سليمان بن المغيرة هل هو خفاف بن إيماء أو أبوه إيماء بن رحضة وعلى هذا فيمكن أن يكون إسلام خفاف تقدم على إسلام أبيه والله أعلم وذكر الزبير بن بكار من حديث حكيم بن حزام أن إيماء بن رحضة حضر بدرا مع المشركين فيكون إسلامه بعد ذلك وذكر بن سعد أنه أسلم قريبا من الحديبية وهذا يعارض رواية مسلم وقال بن سعد كان سكن غيقة من ناحية السقيا ويأوى إلى المدينة وسيأتي ذكر ابنه خفاف في موضعه والقصة المذكورة عن حكيم بن حزام فيها قال فخرج عتبة بن ربيعة مبادرا وخرجت معه لئلا يفوتني من الخير شيء وعتبة يبكي على إيماء بن رحضة الغفاري وقد أهدى إلى المشركين عشر جزائر

## Source unit 393 · printed entry 393

### English candidate

Ayman ibn Khuraym ibn al-Akhram ibn Shaddād ibn ʿAmr ibn Fātik ibn al-Qulayb ibn ʿAmr ibn Asad ibn Khuzayma ibn Mudrika al-Asadī.

Al-Mubarrad said in al-Kāmil that he had Companionship and cited poetry by him concerning the killing of ʿUthmān. In it he says:

“Those who foolishly undertook his killing
met sin and loss, and they did not profit.”

Al-Marzubānī said, “It is said that he had Companionship.” Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said that he embraced Islam on the Day of the Conquest while a pubescent youth. Ibn al-Sakan said, “He is said to have Companionship.”

Al-Tirmidhī transmitted a report from him, from the Prophet ﷺ, called it strange, and said, “We do not know of any hearing by Ayman from the Prophet ﷺ.” Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr did not encounter this report and said: “Al-Dāraquṭnī said that Ayman narrated from the Prophet ﷺ. As for me, I have found no narration of his except from his father and his paternal uncle.”

Al-Ṣūlī said: “Ayman was called the Intimate of the Caliphs because they admired him, his conversation, his eloquence, and his learning. He had leukoderma, which he colored with saffron. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān, while governor of Egypt, would eat with him and tolerate his leukoderma because of his admiration for him.”

Ibn ʿUyayna reported from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: On the Day of al-Marj, Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam said to Ayman ibn Khuraym, “Will you not go out and fight with us?” He replied, “My father and my paternal uncle witnessed Badr and charged me not to fight a Muslim.” The report continues. The statement here that they witnessed Badr is an error, as we will explain in the biography of Khuraym, إن شاء الله تعالى.

## Source unit 394 · printed entry 394

### English candidate

Ayman ibn Umm Ayman. He was Ayman ibn ʿUbayd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Bilāl ibn Abī al-Jarbāʾ ibn Qays ibn Mālik ibn Sālim ibn Ghanm ibn ʿAwf ibn al-Khazraj; that is the lineage given by Ibn Saʿd and Ibn Manda. Abū ʿUmar, however, said: Ayman ibn ʿUbayd al-Ḥabashī, who was Ayman ibn Umm Ayman and the maternal half-brother of Usāma ibn Zayd.

During the Jāhiliyya in Mecca, Umm Ayman married the aforementioned ʿUbayd ibn ʿAmr. He had come to Mecca and settled there, then took Umm Ayman to Yathrib, where she bore him Ayman. He died and left her a widow, so she returned to Mecca and married Zayd ibn Ḥāritha. Al-Balādhurī stated this from Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar, from al-Haytham ibn ʿAdī, from al-Shaʿbī. Ayman is mentioned in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī. That will appear in the biography of his son al-Ḥajjāj ibn Ayman, in the section for those who saw the Prophet. It is said that he was the Ayman from whom ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid related the report concerning amputation for theft. I established its soundness through its supporting reports in Mukhtaṣar al-Tahdhīb.

Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī said: Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf related to us; Ibn Wahb related to us; ʿAmr informed me that Sulaymān ibn Ziyād told him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith told him that Ayman and some young men with him stripped naked and struck one another. The Prophet ﷺ kept saying, ‘They felt no shame before God, nor did they cover themselves before His Messenger.’ Umm Ayman was saying, ‘Messenger of God, seek forgiveness for them,’ and only after much urging did he seek forgiveness for them. Al-Ṭabarānī also related it. Ibn Abī Khaythama distinguished Ayman al-Ḥabashī from Ayman ibn Umm Ayman, and that is correct.

## Source unit 397 · printed entry 397

### English candidate

Ādam ibn Rabīʿa ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim. Ibn Ḥazm and others mentioned that he was the one of whom the Prophet ﷺ said, ‘The first blood-claim I set aside is the blood of the son of Rabīʿa ibn al-Ḥārith.’ Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār also named him.

Al-Balādhurī said that Ḥudhayfa ibn Anas, the Hudhalī poet, set out with his people intending to attack Banū ʿAdī ibn al-Dīl. He found that they had departed their encampment and that Banū Saʿd ibn Layth had occupied it. Ādam ibn Rabīʿa was being foster-nursed among them, and he was killed when Ḥudhayfa raided them. The Messenger of God ﷺ remitted his blood-claim on the day of the Conquest.

It is also said that ‘Ādam’ is a scribal corruption. Al-Dāraquṭnī said in Kitāb al-Ikhwa: ‘It is only “the blood of the son of Rabīʿa.”’ That is what he said, but it is open to question. It is also said that the son’s name was Iyās; Abū Saʿd al-Naysābūrī mentioned this. Other names are given as well. He will appear among the unnamed persons, إن شاء الله تعالى.

## Source unit 398 · printed entry 398

### English candidate

Ibrāhīm, son of the master of humankind, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim. His mother was Māriya the Copt. She bore him in Dhū al-Ḥijja of the year 8, according to Muṣʿab al-Zubayrī. He died in the year 10, as al-Wāqidī stated categorically, on Tuesday after ten nights of Rabīʿ al-Awwal had elapsed. ʿĀʾisha said that he lived eighteen months. Muḥammad ibn al-Muʾammal said that he reached seventeen months and eight days.

Ibn Manda transmitted by way of Ibn Lahīʿa, from ʿUqayl and Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb—both from Ibn Shihāb, from Anas—that when Ibrāhīm was born to Māriya, the Prophet’s bondwoman, something concerning him troubled the Prophet ﷺ inwardly until Gabriel ﵇ came to him and said, ‘Peace be upon you, father of Ibrāhīm.’ This is an uncommon report by way of al-Zuhrī.

Aḥmad said in his Musnad: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd related to us; my father related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr related to me, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: ‘Ibrāhīm, son of the Prophet ﷺ, died when he was eighteen months old, and he did not perform the funeral prayer over him.’ Its chain is sound. Al-Bazzār and Abū Yaʿlā also related it, and Ibn Ḥazm declared it sound. Aḥmad, however, called it an objectionable report in Ḥanbal’s transmission from him. Al-Khaṭṭābī said: ‘ʿĀʾisha’s report has a better-connected chain than the report that says he prayed over him, and it is the more worthy account.’ Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said that ʿĀʾisha’s report is not sound, then suggested that it might mean he did not pray over him in a congregation, or that he ordered his Companions to pray over him but did not attend with them.

Ibn Māja related from Ibn ʿAbbās that when Ibrāhīm, son of the Prophet ﷺ, died, he said: ‘He has a wet nurse in Paradise. Had he lived, he would have been a man of perfect truth and a prophet. Had he lived, his maternal kinsmen among the Copts would have been freed, and no Copt would have been enslaved.’ Its chain contains Abū Shayba al-Wāsiṭī, Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUthmān, who is weak. Ibn Manda transmitted it by this route as well; it reached us through him with a shorter chain, and he called it uncommon.

Ibn Saʿd and Abū Yaʿlā related, by way of ʿAṭāʾ ibn ʿAjlān—who is weak—from Anas, that the Prophet ﷺ performed the funeral prayer over his son Ibrāhīm and pronounced four takbīrs over him. Al-Bazzār related the same by way of Abū Naḍra, from Abū Saʿīd; that route contains ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mālik ibn Maʿqil, who is weak. Aḥmad related by way of Jābir al-Juʿfī—one of the weak transmitters—from al-Shaʿbī, from al-Barāʾ, who said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ did perform the funeral prayer over his son Ibrāhīm, who died at sixteen months.’ Ibn Abī Shayba related it in his Muṣannaf without mentioning al-Barāʾ, and ʿAbd al-Razzāq did likewise. Al-Bayhaqī related in al-Dalāʾil, by way of Sulaymān ibn Bilāl, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ performed the funeral prayer over his son Ibrāhīm when he died. Al-Nawawī said that the majority held that he prayed over him and pronounced four takbīrs.

Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī states, with uncertainty, that he lived seventeen or eighteen months. Ibn Manda transmitted by way of Abū ʿĀmir al-Asadī, from Sufyān, from al-Suddī, from Anas, who said: ‘Ibrāhīm, son of the Prophet ﷺ, died at sixteen months. He said, “Bury him in al-Baqīʿ, for he has a wet nurse in Paradise who will complete his nursing.”’ Ibn Manda called it uncommon and said, ‘We know it from al-Thawrī’s hadith only by this route.’

I say: al-Bukhārī transmitted by way of Muḥammad ibn Bishr, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, who said: ‘I asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Awfā, “Did you see Ibrāhīm, son of the Prophet ﷺ?” He replied, “He died young. Had it been decreed that there should be a prophet after Muḥammad, his son Ibrāhīm would have lived; but there is no prophet after him.”’ Aḥmad transmitted from Wakīʿ, from Ismāʿīl, that he heard Ibn Abī Awfā say, ‘If there were to be a prophet after the Prophet ﷺ, his son Ibrāhīm would not have died.’ Ismāʿīl al-Suddī related from Anas: ‘Ibrāhīm had filled the cradle. Had he remained, he would have been a prophet; but he was not to remain, for your Prophet is the last of the prophets.’

Ibn Manda also transmitted by way of Ibrāhīm ibn Ḥumayd, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid: ‘I asked Ibn Abī Awfā, “Did you see Ibrāhīm, son of the Prophet ﷺ?” He said, “Yes. He was the person who most resembled him. He died young.”’ Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr objected to Anas’s report. After citing it in al-Tamhīd, he said: ‘I do not know what this is. Noah ﵇ had a son who was not a prophet. If prophets begot only prophets, everyone would be a prophet, for all are descendants of Noah.’ Yet the report just mentioned does not entail what he says, for a reason that is evident.

Al-Nawawī said in Ibrāhīm’s biography in his Tahdhīb: ‘As for what is related from some of the early authorities—“Had Ibrāhīm lived, he would have been a prophet”—it is false, an audacious pronouncement about matters unseen, a reckless assertion, and a venture into a grave matter.’ End of quotation. This is surprising, given that it is reported from three Companions. It seems that the possible interpretation did not occur to him, so he went too far in rejecting it. The answer is that a conditional proposition does not entail that its condition will occur. We do not suppose that a Companion would venture such a claim merely on conjecture. والله أعلم.

Thābit al-Bunānī said that Anas said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘A boy was born to me tonight, and I named him after my forefather Ibrāhīm’—the report. Al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmitted it. It contains the account of Ibrāhīm’s death: the Prophet entered upon him while he was breathing his last, and his eyes began to shed tears. It includes: ‘The eye sheds tears, the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord. We are indeed grieved for you, Ibrāhīm.’

Muslim also transmitted by way of ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Anas: ‘I never saw anyone more compassionate toward children than the Messenger of God ﷺ. Ibrāhīm was being foster-nursed for him in the upper districts of Medina. He would go there with us, take him, and kiss him.’ He then related the account of his death.

Ibrāhīm died in Rabīʿ al-Awwal. It is also said that he died in Ramaḍān, and it is said that he died in Dhū al-Ḥijja. This third view is untenable if he died in the year 10, because the Prophet ﷺ was then on the Farewell Pilgrimage—unless he died at the end of Dhū al-Ḥijja. Al-Bayhaqī also reported a view that he lived only seventy days; on that view he died in the year 8. والله أعلم.

إبراهيم بن سيد البشر محمد بن عبد الله بن عبد المطلب بن هاشم أمة مارية القبطية ولدته في ذي الحجة سنة ثمان قال مصعب الزبيري ومات سنة عشر جزم به الواقدي وقال يوم الثلاثاء لعشر خلون من شهر ربيع الأول ابنه إبراهيم وكبر عليه أربعا وروى البزار من طريق أبي نضرة عن أبي سعيد مثله وفيه عبد الرحمن بن مالك بن معقل وهو ضعيف وروى أحمد من طريق جابر الجعفي أحد الضعفاء عن الشعبي عن البراء قال قد صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على ابنه إبراهيم ومات وهو بن ستة عشر شهرا ورواه بن أبي شيبة في مصنفه فلم يذكر البراء وكذا عبد الرزاق وروى البيهقي في لدلائل من طريق سليمان بن بلال عن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى على ابنه إبراهيم حين مات قال النووي الذي ذهب إليه الجمهور أنه صلى عليه وكبر عليه أربع تكبيرات وفي صحيح البخاري أنه عاش سبعة عشر شهرا أو ثمانية عشر شهرا على الشك وأخرج بن منده من طريق أبي عامر الأسدي عن سفيان عن السدي عن أنس قال توفي إبراهيم بن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بن ستة عشر شهرا فقال ادفنوه بالبقيع فإن له مرضعا تتم رضاعه في الجنة وقال غريب لا نعرفه من حديث الثوري الا من هذا الوجه قلت أخرج البخاري من طريق محمد بن بشر عن إسماعيل بن أبي خالد قلت لعبد الله بن أبي أوفى رأيت إبراهيم بن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أكبر قال مات صغيرا ولو قضى أن يكون بعد محمد نبي عاش ابنه إبراهيم ولكن لا نبي بعده وأخرجه أحمد عن وكيع عن إسماعيل سمعت بن أبي أوفى يقول لو كان بعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نبي ما مات ابنه إبراهيم وروى إسماعيل السدي عن أنس كان إبراهيم قد ملأ المهد ولو بقي لكان نبيا لكن لم يكن ليبقى فإن نبيكم آخر الأنبياء وأخرج بن منده أيضا من طريق إبراهيم بن حميد عن إسماعيل بن أبي خالد قلت لابن أبي أوفى هل رأيت إبراهيم بن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال نعم كان أشبه الناس به مات وهو صغير وقد استنكر بن عبد البر حديث أنس فقال بعد إيراده في التمهيد لا أدري ما هذا فقد ولد نوح عليه السلام غير نبي ولو لم يلد النبي الا نبيا لكان كل أحد نبيا لأنهم من ولد نوح ولا يلزم من الحديث المذكور ما ذكره لما لا يخفى وقال النووي في ترجمة إبراهيم من تهذيبه وأما ما روي عن بعض المتقدمين لو عاش إبراهيم لكان نبيا فباطل وجسارة على الكلام على المغيبات ومجازفة وهجوم على عظيم انتهى وهو عجيب مع وروده عن ثلاثة من الصحابة وكأنه لم يظهر له وجه تأويله فبالغ في إنكاره وجوابه أن القضية الشرطية لا نستلزم الوقوع ولا نظن بالصحابي أنه يهجم على مثل هذا بظنه والله أعلم قال ثابت البناني قال أنس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولد لي الليلة غلام فسميته باسم أبي إبراهيم الحديث أخرجه البخاري ومسلم وفيه قصة موته وأنه دخل عليه وهو يجود بنفسه فجعلت عيناه تذرفان وفيه إن العين تدمع والقلب يحزن ولا نقول الا ما يرضي ربنا وإنا بك يا إبراهيم لمحزونون ولمسلم من طريق عمرو بن سعيد عن أنس ما رأيت أحدا ارحم بالعيال من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إبراهيم مسترضعا له في عوالي المدينة وكان الا إن كان مات في آخر ذي الحجة وقد حكى البيهقي قولا بأنه عاش سبعين يوما فقط فعلى هذا يكون مات سنة ثمان والله أعلم

## Source unit 399 · printed entry 399

### English candidate

Another Ibrāhīm, son of the Prophet ﷺ. ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Junayd al-Rāzī mentioned in his Tārīkh—which is a small fascicle—that Khadīja bore the Prophet ﷺ his four daughters, and after the daughters she bore al-Qāsim, al-Ṭāhir, Ibrāhīm, and al-Ṭayyib. The boys died while they were still nursing. He did not mention Māriya the Copt. In his account of Khadīja he said that she bore Ibrāhīm and that he died young. I have not seen anyone else report this. He did not mention Māriya or the child the Prophet had by her. What he stated was not wholly a simple error; rather, his mind appears to have shifted, so that he assumed all the children were by Khadīja and overlooked Māriya.

## Source unit 402 · printed entry 402

### English candidate

Ibrāhīm ibn Khallād ibn Suwayd al-Anṣārī. Ibn Manda said: ‘He was brought to the Prophet ﷺ when he was young, and a mursal report has come from him.’ Al-Bāwardī transmitted by way of Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd, from Ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Labīd, from al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibrāhīm ibn Khallād ibn Suwayd, who said: ‘Gabriel came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “O Muḥammad, be abundant in talbiya and sacrificial slaughter.”’

Abū Tumayla transmitted it from Ibn Isḥāq but said, ‘from Ibrāhīm ibn Khallād, from his father.’ I say: his having heard from his father is not sound either. Al-Thawrī and Mūsā ibn ʿUqba transmitted it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Labīd, from al-Muṭṭalib, from Khallād ibn al-Sāʾib, from Khallād ibn Suwayd, from Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī; that is the preserved route.

Al-Dimyāṭī took issue with Ibn Manda's statement, saying: ‘The correct genealogy of this Ibrāhīm is Ibrāhīm ibn Khallād ibn al-Sāʾib ibn Khallād ibn Suwayd al-Anṣārī. His father, Khallād ibn al-Sāʾib, was placed by Ibn Saʿd in the second generation of the Successors, so how could his son possibly have been born in the time of the Prophet ﷺ?’ I say: this objection is open to question. The subject of this entry may have been a brother of the Companion al-Sāʾib ibn Khallād, who will be discussed later, and he would therefore be the paternal uncle of the father of the Ibrāhīm mentioned by al-Dimyāṭī. والله أعلم.

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

إبراهيم بن خلاد بن سويد الأنصاري قال بن منده أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو صغير وجاء عنه حديث مرسل روى الباوردي من طريق إبراهيم بن سعد عن بن إسحاق عن عبد الله بن أبي لبيد عن المطلب بن عبد الله عن إبراهيم بن خلاد بن سويد قال جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا محمد كن عجاجا ثجاجا ورواه أبو تميلة عن بن إسحاق فقال عن إبراهيم بن خلاد عن أبيه قلت ولا يصح أيضا سماعه من أبيه وقد رواه الثوري وموسى بن عقبة عن عبد الله بن أبي لبيد عن المطلب عن خلاد بن السائب عن خلاد بن سويد عن زيد بن خالد الجهني وهو المحفوظ وتعقب الدمياطي قول بن منده بان قال الصواب في نسب إبراهيم هذا أنه إبراهيم بن خلاد بن السائب بن خلاد بن سويد الأنصاري قال وأبوه خلاد بن السائب ذكره بن سعد في الطبقة الثانية من التابعين فكيف يمكن أن يكون ولده ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قلت وفي هذا التعقيب نظر فيحتمل أن يكون صاحب الترجمة أخا السائب بن خلاد الصحابي الآتي ذكره وهو جد إبراهيم الذي ذكره الدمياطي فيكون صاحب الترجمة عم أبيه والله أعلم

## Source unit 404 · printed entry 404

### English candidate

Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, al-Zuhrī, the Medinan. Al-Wāqidī and others said that he was born during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ. His mother was Umm Kulthūm bint ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ.

Al-Bukhārī said in al-Awsaṭ: Yūnus transmitted from Ibn Shihāb, who said, “Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf informed me that the Prophet ﷺ prayed for rain.” Some transmitters said, “He prayed for rain for us.” Al-Bukhārī said, “That is not sound, because his mother was Umm Kulthūm, whose brother al-Walīd arranged her marriage during the days of the Conquest.”

Yaʿqūb ibn Shayba said, “He was counted in the first generation of the Followers. We know of no other child of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān who transmitted directly from ʿUmar.”

Ibn Abī Shayba said: Ibn ʿUlayya related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Umayya, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father—Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf—who said, “I remember the hide of a sheep that my mother ordered slaughtered when ʿUmar struck Abū Bakra. Its hide was placed on his back because of the severity of the beating.”

A wording found in Abū Nuʿaym’s work would entail that Ibrāhīm was born before the Hijra. On that basis he would belong to the first section, but it is not sound. The correct view is that he was born before the death of the Prophet ﷺ. Muslim included him in the first generation of the Followers of Medina. He died in 75 or 76 AH.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف الزهري المدني قال الواقدي وغيره ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمه أم كلثوم بنت عقبة بن أبي معيط قال البخاري في الأوسط روى يونس عن بن شهاب قال أخبرني إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال استسقى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال بعضهم استسقى بنا قال ولا يصح لأن أمة أم كلثوم زوجها أخوها الوليد أيام الفتح وقال يعقوب بن شيبة كان يعد في الطبقة الأولى من التابعين ولا نعلم أحدا من من ولد عبد الرحمن روى عن عمر سماعا غيره وقال بن أبي شيبة حدثنا بن علية عن إسماعيل بن أمية عن سعد بن إبراهيم عن أبيه هو إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال إني لأذكره مسك شاة أمرت بها أمي فذبحت حين ضرب عمر أبا بكر فجعل مسكها على ظهره من شدة الضرب ووقع عند أبي نعيم ما يقتضى أنه ولد قبل الهجرة فعلى هذا يكون من أهل القسم الأول لكنه لا يصح والصواب فبل موت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وذكره مسلم في الطبقة الأولى من تابعي المدينة مات سنة خمس أو ست وسبعين من الهجرة

## Source unit 407 · printed entry 407

### English candidate

Ibrāhīm ibn Nuʿaym ibn al-Naḥḥām al-ʿAdawī. His lineage will appear in his father’s biography. The chain of a report will also appear there stating that Nuʿaym had been called Nuʿaym and that the Prophet ﷺ named him Ṣāliḥ.

Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said that Ibrāhīm was born during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Saʿd mentioned that Usāma divorced a wife while he was a young man during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ; Nuʿaym ibn al-Naḥḥām then married her, and she bore him Ibrāhīm. Al-Zubayr said that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb married this Ibrāhīm to one of his daughters.

I say: al-Balādhurī states that Ibrāhīm was married to Ruqayya, daughter of ʿUmar by Umm Kulthūm bint ʿAlī. Al-Bukhārī mentioned him in his Tārīkh and said that he was killed on the Day of al-Ḥarra. Ibn Ḥibbān listed him among the trustworthy Followers.

Al-Bukhārī transmitted in his Tārīkh through Mujāhid, who said: “I said to him, ‘the ʿulūj.’ Ibrāhīm ibn Nuʿaym said to me, ‘Repent to God, for an ʿilj is an unbeliever.’”

He is mentioned in a report containing an error. Ibn Manda transmitted through Abū Yūsuf, from Abū Ḥanīfa, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Jābir, that a slave belonging to Ibrāhīm ibn al-Naḥḥām had been made mudabbar. He then needed the slave’s price, so the Prophet ﷺ sold him for eight hundred dirhams. Ibn Manda said, “It is transmitted by more than one route from Jābir that the Prophet ﷺ sold a slave belonging to Ibn al-Naḥḥām”—meaning that Ibrāhīm is not named in it.

Abū Nuʿaym objected that Ibn Manda had made a scribal error. He said that the wording was, “A slave belonged to Ibn Nuʿaym,” and that the copyist turned the attribution into Ibrāhīm. I say: this does not work, because even if it read “Ibn Nuʿaym,” that would not establish Companionship for Ibn Nuʿaym. What the reliable transmitters related from ʿAṭāʾ was “Nuʿaym ibn al-Naḥḥām.” Ibn al-Munkadir, Abū al-Zubayr, and others likewise transmitted it from Jābir; some did not name the owner. As for Ibrāhīm, his name is not soundly established in this report.

Muṣʿab al-Zubayrī said: “Ibrāhīm ibn Nuʿaym ibn al-Naḥḥām was married to a daughter of ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. When she died, ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb took him by the hand, brought him into his house, and presented his two daughters, Umm ʿĀṣim and Ḥafṣa, to him. He said, ‘Choose.’ Ibrāhīm chose Ḥafṣa, and ʿĀṣim married her to him. He was asked, ‘You left Umm ʿĀṣim, though she is the more beautiful of the two?’ He replied, ‘I saw a splendid young woman and heard that the family of Marwān had mentioned her. I thought that perhaps she might obtain some of their worldly fortune.’ ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān then married her, and she bore him ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz. Umm ʿĀṣim later died while married to ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz. Ibrāhīm was killed on the Day of al-Ḥarra, and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz then married her sister Ḥafṣa.”

I also saw Ibrāhīm mentioned among those who witnessed ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar’s endowment of his land.
