## Source unit 410 · printed entry 410

### English candidate

Azhar ibn Mukammil ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAbd ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Zuhra, al-Qurashī al-Zuhrī.

Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said in his account of Banū Zuhra: “Among the descendants of al-Ḥārith ibn Zuhra was Azhar ibn Mukammil.” He then mentioned him and said, “Some people used to say that he would assume the caliphate.”

Al-Zubayr then related through a chain from Ḥafṣ and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, the two sons of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, that the two disputed over something. ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān ordered that they be brought before him. They came, but Ḥafṣ arrived later than his brother. ʿAbd al-Malik asked him, “What delayed you?” He replied, “I passed Azhar ibn Mukammil while he was dying, so I remained with him until he died and then buried him.” ʿAbd al-Malik had been reclining; he sat upright and asked, “Are you telling the truth?” Ḥafṣ said, “Yes.” ʿAbd al-Malik said, “Then what the People of the Book say is false,” referring to their claim that Azhar would assume the caliphate.

I say: this Azhar is not the Azhar who was the father of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar, mentioned previously; their lineages make the distinction clear. I found no mention of Mukammil among the Companions. It therefore appears that he died while still a polytheist and left this son young during the Prophetic period. God Most High knows best.

## Source unit 414 · printed entry 414

### English candidate

Asʿad ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf ibn Wahb, the Anṣārī, Abū Umāma, who is well known by his teknonym. He was born two years before the death of the Prophet ﷺ. He was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, who performed taḥnīk for him and named him after his maternal grandfather, Abū Umāma Asʿad ibn Zurāra.

He transmitted reports from the Prophet ﷺ in disconnected form. He also transmitted from a number of Companions, including ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, Zayd ibn Thābit, his father, his paternal uncle ʿUthmān, and others. Abū Zurʿa denied that he heard from ʿUmar.

Al-Bukhārī said, “He lived into the time of the Prophet ﷺ but did not hear from him.” Al-Baghawī, Ibn al-Sakan, Ibn Ḥibbān, and others said the same. Ibn Abī Dāwūd said, “He accompanied the Prophet ﷺ and pledged allegiance to him.” This was rejected by Ibn Manda, who said that al-Bukhārī’s statement is sounder. Al-Bāwardī said, “His Companionship is disputed, but he was born during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ.”

Aḥmad ibn Ṣāliḥ said: ʿAnbasa informed us, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb, who said, “Abū Umāma ibn Sahl related to me; he had lived into the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet named him and performed taḥnīk for him.”

Al-Ṭabarānī said that Abū Umāma had sight of him. Khalīfa and others said that he died in the year 100 AH. Ibn al-Kalbī said that the people agreed to have him lead them in prayer while ʿUthmān was under siege.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

أسعد بن سهل بن حنيف بن واهب الأنصاري أبو إمامة مشهور بكنيته ولد قبل وفاة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعامين وأتى به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فحنكه وسماه باسم جده لأمه أبي أمامة أسعد بن زرارة وقد روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أحاديث ارسلها وروى عن جماعة من الصحابة كعمر وعثمان وزيد بن ثابت وأبيه وعمه عثمان وغيرهم وأنكر أبو زرعة سماعه من عمر وقال البخاري أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يسمع منه وكذا قال البغوي وابن السكن وابن حبان وغيرهم وقال بن أبي داود صحب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وبايعه وأنكر ذلك عليه وابن منده وقال قول البخاري أصح وقال الباوردي مختلف في صحبته الا أنه ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال أحمد بن صالح أخبرنا عنبسة عن يونس عن بن شهاب حدثني أبو أمامة بن سهل وكان قد أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وسماه حنكة وقال الطبراني له رؤية وقال خليفة وغيره مات سنة مائة وقال بن الكلبي تراضى الناس أن يصلي بهم وعثمان محصور

## Source unit 416 · printed entry 416

### English candidate

Iyās ibn ʿAmr ibn Muʾammil ibn Ḥabīb ibn Tamīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qurṭ ibn Razāḥ ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb, al-Qurashī al-ʿAdawī. He lived into the Islamic period.

### English candidate

Ayyūb ibn Bashīr ibn Saʿd ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Anṣārī. Al-Mizzī gave his lineage thus in al-Tahdhīb, assigned him the kunya Abū Sulaymān, and said: Abū ʿUbayda al-Ājurrī reported from Abū Dāwūd that he was Ayyūb ibn Bashīr ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Akkāl, of the Anṣār. Al-ʿAdawī, citing Ibn al-Qaddāḥ, likewise traced his father’s lineage and said that his father [Bashīr] attended Uḥud, the Trench, and the other campaigns with his own father. As for Bashīr ibn Saʿd, the father of al-Nuʿmān, his grandfather’s name was Thaʿlaba. Ibn Shāhīn included Ayyūb among the Companions and transmitted with his isnad from al-Zuhrī, from Ayyūb ibn Bashīr, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said, ‘The best charity is that given to a hostile relative.’ This is mursal and does not establish companionship for him. Al-Bukhārī, Ibn Ḥibbān, and more than one other authority stated decisively that he was a Successor. Abū Dāwūd declared him trustworthy. Al-Mizzī said that he was born during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ and transmitted from him in mursal form. He then quoted Ibn Saʿd: ‘He was trustworthy but did not transmit many reports. He was present at al-Ḥarra and received several wounds there; he died two years later, aged seventy-five.’ I say: on that reckoning, he would have lived through twenty years of the Prophet’s ﷺ lifetime, and I think that the stated amount of his age is an error. Ibn Ḥibbān likewise erred over the date of his death when, after listing him among the trustworthy Successors, he said that he died in the year one hundred and thirteen. He confused him with Ayyūb ibn Bushayr—with the initial consonant vocalized ḍamma—for that is the man who died in that year. The reliable authority for the date of the present man’s death is Ibn Saʿd. The isnad cited by Ibn Shāhīn contains a weak transmitter. This report was also transmitted by Imām ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad in his Ziyādāt and by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr, by way of Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn, from al-Zuhrī, from Ayyūb ibn Bashīr ibn Ḥizām. This is preferable, although it too is defective, because the reports from Ayyūb ibn Bashīr differ. Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿshā transmitted it from Ayyūb ibn Bashīr, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī. Al-Bukhārī included it under this biography in al-Adab al-Mufrad, as did Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, through Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. Ayyūb has another mursal report, transmitted by al-Dhuhlī in al-Zuhriyyāt from Aḥmad ibn Khālid al-Wahbī, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, from Ayyūb, from Bashīr ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Akkāl al-Anṣārī, one of Banū Muʿāwiya. He said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘Pour water over me from seven waterskins drawn from different wells, so that I may go out to the people and give them final instructions’—the report. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it in al-Awsaṭ by another route from Ibn Isḥāq, but his text suffered an egregious scribal corruption to which Ibn ʿAsākir drew attention. Its wording was: ‘From Ayyūb ibn Bashīr: I heard Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān say that the Messenger of God ﷺ said...’ Ibn ʿAsākir said that it had originally read, ‘from Ayyūb ibn Bashīr ibn al-Nuʿmān, one of Banū Muʿāwiya.’ The copyist took ‘one of Banū Muʿāwiya’ to mean ‘Muʿāwiya related to me,’ then changed ‘related to me’ into ‘I heard’ and supplied Muʿāwiya’s descent from Abū Sufyān. Al-Tirmidhī transmitted it by way of al-Darāwardī from Suhayl but did not include Ayyūb ibn Bashīr in its isnad. Others transmitted it from al-Darāwardī and did include Ayyūb. It is also said to be from Ayyūb ibn Bashīr, from ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾisha. Ibn Abī Ḥātim confined himself to this last form when identifying Ayyūb, saying in his notice: ‘He narrated from ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr and al-Zuhrī.’ ʿAbdān ibn Muḥammad al-Marwazī also listed him among the Companions; Abū Mūsā reported that in al-Dhayl and transmitted through him, by way of al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥibbān, that Ayyūb ibn Bashīr said to the Messenger of God ﷺ, ‘I have resolved to make one-third of my prayer a supplication for you’—the report. Abū Mūsā said: ‘It appears that this is a Companion distinct from al-Zuhrī’s shaykh.’ He added that this statement has been transmitted of someone else as something he said to the Prophet ﷺ. Aḥmad and others transmitted it by way of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, from al-Ṭufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, from his father, who said: A man said, ‘Messenger of God, what do you think if I devote my prayer to you?’—the report. I say: it is known as a report of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, but that does not preclude identifying the man as Ayyūb, if the report is preserved.

## Source unit 419 · printed entry 419

### English candidate

Al-Ābāʾ—on the morphological pattern al-faʿāl—ibn Qays al-Asadī, a poet who lived in both the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods. Al-Marzubānī mentioned him in his Muʿjam and said that he was present during the Ridda. He composed the following in praise of Khālid ibn al-Walīd:

God will not defeat a people whose commander you are;
O son of al-Walīd, nor will those in the rear come to grief through you.

Sufficient for you is a hand of punishment when it strikes
the enemy—and a hand that, one time, forgave.

Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār likewise cited him in the biography of Khālid ibn al-Walīd in Kitāb al-Nasab.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

الآباء بوزن الفعال بن قيس الأسدي شاعر مخضرم ذكره المرزباني في معجمه وقال كان في الردة وله يمدح خالد بن الوليد <br />
 لن يهزم الله قوما أنت قائدهم <br />
 يا بن الوليد ولن يشقى بك الدبر <br />
 كفاك كف عذاب عند سطوتها <br />
 على العدو وكف مرة غفر وهكذا ذكره الزبير بن بكار في ترجمة خالد بن الوليد من كتاب النسب

Al-Ajlaḥ ibn Waqqāṣ. He lived into Islam. Abū ʿUbayda said: ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib and al-Ajlaḥ ibn Waqqāṣ came to ʿUmar and found him with wealth being weighed before him. When the weighing was finished, he set it aside, turned to them, and said, ‘Well?’ ʿAmr said, ‘Commander of the Believers, this al-Ajlaḥ is strong in resolve, not readily caught unawares, and swift to charge. By God, I have never seen his like.’ ʿUmar said to al-Ajlaḥ, with anger visible on his face, ‘Well?’ Al-Ajlaḥ replied, ‘The people are sound; their offspring are numerous, their provisions abundant, their vegetation fertile, and they are bold against their enemy. They are sound through the soundness of their leader.’ ʿUmar asked, ‘What prevented you from saying of your companion what he said of you?’ He answered, ‘What I saw of anger in your face.’ ʿUmar said, ‘You were right. Since I have left you to yourself, I shall leave him to you.’

## Source unit 428 · printed entry 428

### English candidate

Aḥzāb ibn Usayd, with the kunya Abū Rahm, al-Samaʿī—with two fatḥas. He is also called al-Ẓahrī. There is disagreement over his father’s name: it is read Asīd, with fatḥa, and Usayd, with ḍamma. Ibn Yūnus said that he lived in the pre-Islamic period and was counted among the Successors. Al-Bukhārī and Ibn Ḥibbān likewise listed him among the Successors, while Abū Ḥātim said that he had no companionship. Ibn Abī Khaythama and Ibn Saʿd listed an Abū Rahm al-Samāʿī among the Companions who settled in Syria, but did not give his personal name. Ibn Manda transmitted by way of Baqiyya, from Muʿāwiya ibn Saʿīd al-Tujībī, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Marthad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Yazanī, from Abū Rahm al-Samaʿī, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘Among the gravest sins is for someone to appropriate a man’s property without right.’ Muʿāwiya ibn Yaḥyā al-Ṭarābulusī followed him in transmitting it from Muʿāwiya ibn Saʿd. If this Abū Rahm is Aḥzāb, the report does not prove his companionship, because he may have transmitted it in mursal form. If he is someone else, companionship remains possible.

## Source unit 429 · printed entry 429

### English candidate

Al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays ibn Muʿāwiya ibn Ḥuṣayn ibn Ḥafṣ ibn ʿAbbāda ibn al-Nazzāl ibn Murra ibn ʿUbayd ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr ibn Kaʿb ibn Saʿd ibn Zayd Manāt ibn Tamīm, Abū Baḥr al-Tamīmī al-Saʿdī. His mother was Ḥabba bint ʿAmr ibn Qurṭ ibn Thaʿlaba al-Bāhiliyya. His given name, according to the best-known view, was al-Ḍaḥḥāk. It is also said to have been Ṣakhr; this was the opinion of Sulaymān ibn Abī Shaykh as transmitted by Ibn al-Sakan, and Khalīfa likewise gave it in the transmissions of Yaʿqūb ibn Abī Shayba and al-Fallās. It is also said that his name was al-Ḥārith, and also Ḥiṣn; al-Marzubānī reported both. Ibn Ḥibbān stated decisively in al-Thiqāt that it was al-Ḥārith. His epithet was al-Aḥnaf, by which he is famous. He lived during the time of the Prophet ﷺ but did not meet him. It is said that the Prophet prayed for him. Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim said: Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā related to us: Ḥajjāj related to us: Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from al-Ḥasan, from al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays, who said: ‘While I was circumambulating the House during the time of ʿUthmān, a man of Banū Layth took me by the hand and said, “Shall I give you glad tidings?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “Do you remember when the Messenger of God ﷺ sent me to your people and I began presenting Islam to them and calling them to it? You said, ‘You are indeed calling us to good and enjoining it, and he too calls to good.’ That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said, ‘God, forgive al-Aḥnaf.’”’ Al-Aḥnaf used to say, ‘No deed of mine gives me greater hope than that’—meaning the Prophet’s ﷺ supplication. ʿAlī ibn Zayd alone transmitted it, and he is weak. Aḥmad transmitted in Kitāb al-Zuhd, by way of Khayr ibn Ḥabīb, that two men informed al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays that the Prophet ﷺ had prayed for him, whereupon he prostrated. His forbearance became proverbial. ʿUmar said to him, ‘Al-Aḥnaf is the master of the people of Basra.’ In Aḥmad’s al-Zuhd, al-Ḥasan related from al-Aḥnaf that he said, ‘I am not forbearing, but I make myself practice forbearance.’ Ibn al-Sakan transmitted by way of al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl, from al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad, who said: A man asked al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays, ‘How did you gain mastery over your people when you are bow-legged and one-eyed?’ He replied, ‘By leaving alone what does not concern me, just as what did not concern you about my affairs has concerned you.’ Al-Ḥākim mentioned that al-Aḥnaf conquered Marw al-Rūdh. Ibn Saʿd placed him in the first generation of the Successors of Basra and said that he was trustworthy, reliable, and transmitted few reports. He was among those who stood aside from the Battle of the Camel, but he later attended Ṣiffīn. He narrated from ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Dharr, and others. Abū al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Shikhkhīr, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Ṭalq ibn Ḥabīb, and others narrated from him. He had many stories—too lengthy to mention—with ʿUmar, then ʿUthmān, then ʿAlī, then Muʿāwiya, and then those who followed them, until he died in Basra during the governorship of Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr in the year sixty-seven. Muṣʿab walked in his funeral procession and said on the day of his death, ‘Today firmness and sound judgment have departed.’

Arbad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Bajalī. He lived in the Jāhiliyya, and ʿUmar appointed him to judge a case.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq related from Ibn ʿUyayna, from al-Mukhāriq ibn ʿAbd Allāh: “I heard Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb say: We set out for the pilgrimage. A man among us named Arbad ibn ʿAbd Allāh caused a spiny-tailed lizard to be trampled, so we went to ʿUmar to ask him. ʿUmar said to Arbad, ‘Judge concerning it.’ He replied, ‘You are better and more learned than I.’ ʿUmar said, ‘I have ordered you to judge.’ Arbad said, ‘In my judgment, a young goat is due.’ ʿUmar said, ‘It has reached the stage of taking both water and browse.’ Arbad replied, ‘Then that is the due penalty.’”

Its chain is sound. Al-Aʿmash also transmitted it from Sulaymān ibn Maysara, from Ṭāriq, but did not name the man.

## Source unit 433 · printed entry 433

### English candidate

Arṭāh ibn Suhayya—Suhayya was his mother; her name is written with an unpointed sīn and in the diminutive form. He was Arṭāh ibn Zafar ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik ibn Sawād ibn Ḍamra, al-Ghaṭafānī al-Murrī, the famous poet. He lived in the Jāhiliyya and survived into the caliphate of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān.

Hishām ibn al-Kalbī said: Miḥraz ibn Jaʿfar, the client of Abū Hurayra, informed us that Arṭāh ibn Suhayya al-Murrī entered the presence of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān when 130 years had passed over him. He then related a story. On this reckoning, Arṭāh was born about forty years before the beginning of the Prophetic mission.

Al-Marzubānī said in his Muʿjam: “Arṭāh ibn Suhayya had the teknonym Abū al-Walīd and lived in the early Islamic period. ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān encountered him as a very old man.” Arṭāh recited to ʿAbd al-Malik:

“I have seen the nights consume a man,
as the earth consumes fallen iron.
When death comes upon a child of Adam,
it seeks no increment beyond that soul.
I know that it will return again
until it fulfills its vow against Abū al-Walīd.”

ʿAbd al-Malik was alarmed and thought that Arṭāh meant him. Arṭāh said, “Commander of the Faithful, I meant only myself,” and ʿAbd al-Malik fell silent.

It is said that Arṭāh lived to a great age. Shabīb ibn al-Barṣāʾ used to taunt him, saying that Arṭāh had not suffered the blindness that befell his household. Shabīb died before Arṭāh; Arṭāh then went blind and would say, “If only he had lived to see me blind.”

Abū al-Faraj al-Iṣbahānī said: “Suhayya was a slave woman of Ḍirār ibn al-Azwar, then came into Zafar’s possession. She bore Arṭāh in Zafar’s bed. Ḍirār’s household claimed him in the Jāhiliyya, and Zafar gave him to Ḍirār; Zafar’s people then took him back. The attribution to his mother consequently prevailed.”

Al-Marzubānī’s transmitted clause linking al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAwf ibn Abī Ḥāritha al-Murrī to “Ibn Suhayya” is textually corrupt. The account continues that Suhayya, Arṭāh’s mother, had been taken captive from Kalb before she came to Zafar and bore Arṭāh in Zafar’s bed. When Zafar died and Arṭāh grew up, Ḍirār ibn al-Azwar came to al-Ḥārith and said:

‘O Ḥārith, release to me my son from Zafar,
as one whom you release from the captives of Muḍar.
I know him as mine as surely as the moon is known;
his father is an evil old man if he denies it.’

Al-Ḥārith handed him to Ḍirār, who seated him behind himself. Word reached Aqram ibn ʿUqfān, the paternal uncle of Abū Zafar. He said to Ḍirār, ‘Put him down, or I shall draw the sword against you both.’ Ḍirār put him down. Thereafter he was known only as Arṭāh ibn Suhayya.”

 توفي نذرها بأبي الوليد فارتاع عبد الملك وظن أنه أراده فقال يا أمير المؤمنين إنما عنيت نفسي فسكت ويقال إن أرطاة عمر فكان شبيب بن البرصاء يعيره ويقول إنه لم يحصل له ما حصل لآل بيته من العمي فمات شبيب قبل أرطاة ثم عمي أرطاة فكان يقول ليته عاش حتى رآني أعمى وقال أبو الفرج الأصبهاني كانت سهية أمة لضرار بن الأزور ثم صارت إلى زفر فجاءت بأرطاة على فراشه فادعاه فراش ضرار في الجاهلية فأعطاه له زفر ثم انتزعه قومه منه فغلبت عليه النسبة إلى أمة وقال المرزباني كان الحارث بن عوف بن أبي حارثة لابن سهية أم أرطاة وكانت اخيذة من كلب قبل أن تصير إلى زفر فولدت أرطاة على فراش زفر فلما مات زفر وشب أرطاة جاء ضرار بن الأزور إلى الحارث فقال <br />
 يا حار أطلق لي بني من زفر <br />
 كبعض من تطلق من أسري مضر <br />
 أعرفه مني كعرفان القمر <br />
 إن أباه شيخ سوء أن كفر فدفعه الحارث لضرار فاردفه فلحقه فبلغ أقرم بن عقفان عم أبي زفر فقال لضرار ألقه وإلا انتضيتكما بالسيف فألقاه فما صار أرطاة يعرف الا أرطاة بن سهية

</div>

## Source unit 435 · printed entry 435

### English candidate

Arṭabān, a client of the Muzanīs and the grandfather of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwn. He was a mukhaḍram who lived into the Islamic period and embraced Islam during ʿUmar’s rule.

Al-Khaṭīb transmitted through Azhar ibn Saʿd, from Ibn ʿAwn, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: “I brought ʿUmar the alms due on my property. He said, ‘May God bless your property for you.’ I said, ‘And my family.’ He replied, ‘And your family.’” This is the end of the report. A man who had a family during ʿUmar’s rule must have lived into the earlier period.

Abū Khalīfa said: al-Walīd ibn Hishām related to us; my father related to us, from ʿAwn, from his father, from his grandfather Arṭabān, who said: “I was a deacon in a church of Ghassān, and I fell by lot into the share of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Durra al-Muzanī.”

## Source unit 438 · printed entry 438

### English candidate

Armā—also called Arhā and Arīḥā—ibn Aṣḥama ibn Abjar, son of the Negus.

Abū Mūsā said: Imām Abū al-Qāsim Ismāʿīl—meaning his teacher al-Taymī—mentioned in al-Maghāzī that in the seventh year the Prophet ﷺ wrote to the kings and sent messengers to them. He related the story and said: “He sent ʿAmr ibn Umayya to the Negus. The Negus wrote back affirming his faith. His letter said, ‘I have sent you my son Armā ibn Aṣḥama. I possess authority over no one but myself. If you wish, Messenger of God, I shall come to you.’ His son set out with sixty persons from Abyssinia in a ship at sea, and all of them drowned.”

This is how Abū Mūsā transmitted it from his teacher, without a chain. Ibn Isḥāq related it at length in al-Maghāzī. Al-Ṭabarī transmitted it in his Tārīkh, al-Thaʿlabī in his Tafsīr, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Dalāʾil through Ibn Isḥāq, but al-Bayhaqī called him Arīḥā. والله أعلم.

## Source unit 439 · printed entry 439

### English candidate

Azādmard ibn Hurmuz, the Persian. Ibn Manda mentioned him and transmitted through ʿIkrima ibn Ibrāhīm al-Azdī, from Jarīr ibn Yazīd ibn Jarīr, from Azādmard Hurmuz. He had lived into the Islamic period and had been one of Kisrā’s asāwira. He said: “While we were at Kisrā’s gate awaiting permission to enter, permission was delayed, the heat became severe, and we grew restless.” He then related the long story that follows. At its end he said: “I said, ‘There is no power and no strength except through God. What God wills comes to pass, and what He does not will does not come to pass.’ By God, it continued burning until it became ashes.” Ibn Manda said, “It is uncommon.” I say: ʿIkrima is weak.

Ibn Manda also transmitted through Sulaymān ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Jarīr, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: “I was at al-Qādisiyya when a Persian heard me say, ‘There is no power and no strength except through God.’ He said, ‘I once heard these words from heaven,’” and then related the long story.

Ibn Manda also transmitted through Ibrāhīm ibn Fahd, one of the weak transmitters, from Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar: Ḥammād ibn Salama related to us, from Simāk, from Jarīr, who said: “I went out to Persia and said, ‘What God wills! There is no power and no strength except through God.’ A man heard me and said, ‘What are these words? I have not heard them from anyone since I heard them from heaven.’ I asked, ‘What have you to do with news of heaven?’ He said:

‘I was with Kisrā, who sent me on one of his errands. I went out and later returned, only to find that a devil had taken my place among my family in my own form. He appeared to me and said, “Agree that I shall have one day and you one day, or I shall destroy you.” I agreed. He became my companion: he would speak to me and I to him.

‘One day he said, “I am among those who eavesdrop, and tonight is my turn.” I asked, “May I come with you?” He said, “Yes.” He prepared himself, then came to me and said, “Take hold of my mane, and beware of letting it go, lest you perish.” I took hold of his mane, and he ascended until I touched the sky. Then someone said, “What God wills comes to pass. There is no power and no strength except through God.” They fell on their faces, and I fell too. I returned to my family.

‘He came in several days later. I began saying, “What God wills! There is no power and no strength except through God.” At that he began to dissolve until he became like a fly. Then he said to me, “You have memorized it,” and thereafter he ceased visiting us.’”

## Source unit 450 · printed entry 450

### English candidate

Asmāʾ ibn Khārija ibn Ḥiṣn ibn Ḥudhayfa ibn Badr al-Fazārī, Abū Ḥassān al-Kūfī. Abū Ḥassān al-Ziyādī said that he died in the year 60 at the age of eighty. I say: on that reckoning, he was born before the beginning of the prophetic mission. Ibn Ḥibbān said that he died in the year 65, and agreed as to his age. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said in al-Kunā, in the biography of Abū al-ʿUryān: ‘It is not unlikely that he was a Companion, since senior Successors related from him.’ End of quotation. His father and his paternal uncle al-Ḥurr have been listed among the Companions, and Asmāʾ satisfies Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's criterion.

Al-Ṭabarī transmitted by way of Abū al-Aḥwaṣ that Asmāʾ ibn Khārija vied in boasting with a man and said, ‘I am the son of noble shaykhs.’ ʿAbd Allāh said, ‘That is Yūsuf son of Yaʿqūb son of Isḥāq son of Ibrāhīm.’ Ibn al-Mubārak transmitted in al-Zuhd, from al-Masʿūdī, from Mālik ibn Asmāʾ ibn Khārija, from his father, who said: I heard Ibn Masʿūd say, ‘The possessor of two tongues in this world will have two tongues of fire on the Day of Resurrection.’

Al-Marzubānī said that he was noble, generous, munificent, and intelligent, and that many reports are told of him. He came in a delegation to ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān, who honored him. Ibn Abī al-Dunyā said: Abū Ḥudhayfa ʿAbd Allāh ibn Marwān ibn Muʿāwiya ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUthmān ibn Asmāʾ al-Fazārī related to us, from his father, that Asmāʾ ibn Khārija said, ‘I have never insulted anyone.’

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

أسماء بن خارجة بن حصن بن حذيفة بن بدر الفزاري أبو حسان الكوفي قال أبو حسان الزيادي مات سنة ستين وله ثمانون سنة قلت فعلى هذا يكون مولده قبل المبعث وقال بن حبان مات سنة خمس وستين ووافق على مقدار سنه وقال بن عبد البر في الكنى في ترجمة أبي العريان لا يبعد أن يكون صحابيا لرواية كبار التابعين عنه انتهى وقد ذكروا أباه وعمه الحر في الصحابة وهو على شرط بن عبد البر وروى الطبري من طريق أبي الأحوص قال فاخر أسماء بن خارجة رجلا فقال أنا بن الأشياخ الكرام فقال عبد الله ذاك يوسف بن يعقوب بن إسحاق بن إبراهيم وقال بن المبارك في الزهد عن المسعودي عن مالك بن أسماء بن خارجة عن أبيه قال سمعت بن مسعود يقول ذو اللسانين في الدنيا له لسانان من نار يوم القيامة وقال المرزباني كان شريفا جوادا كريما لبيبا وله أخبار كثيرة ووفد على عبد الملك بن مروان فأكرمه وقال بن أبي الدنيا حدثنا أبو حذيفة عبد الله بن مروان بن معاوية بن الحارث بن عثمان بن أسماء الفزاري عن أبيه قال قال أسماء بن خارجة ماشتمت أحدا قط

## Source unit 456 · printed entry 456

### English candidate

Al-Aswad ibn Quṭba, Abū Mufazzir—the fāʾ has fatḥa, the zāy is doubled and has kasra, and it is followed by rāʾ. Al-Dāraquṭnī said in al-Muʾtalif that he witnessed al-Qādisiyya and composed many poems about it. He was Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ's messenger to ʿUmar with the captives of Jalūlāʾ, and he was the Muslims' poet in those days. Sayf mentioned him in al-Futūḥ. He also said that al-Aswad was with Khālid ibn al-Walīd during the caliphate of Abū Bakr. Among his poetry is:

‘We held our ground at al-Yarmūk until there gathered
Rome's levied hosts, in their battalions massed and strong.’

Al-Marzubānī said in his Muʿjam that he witnessed the conquests of Iraq. He is the one who said:

‘Now carry from me to the Arab folk a message:
the non-Arabs' spoils have been divided among us.
The people's tribute flowed in to us as the price
with which we released to them the bracelet-wearing lords.’

Al-Aswad was also the one who replied to Khosrow's envoy when the envoy said to them, ‘Have you not had your fill?’ Al-Aswad said, ‘We will not make peace with you until we eat the honey of Arbidīn with the citron of Kūthā.’ It is related that the expression simply came to his tongue: he neither intended it nor understood its meaning.

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

 جلائب روم في كتائبها العضل وقال المرزباني في معجمه شهد فتوح العراق وهوالقائل <br />
 الا بلغا عني العريب رسالة <br />
 فقد قسمت فينا فيوء الأعاجم <br />
 ودرت علينا جزية القوم بالذي <br />
 فككنا به عنهم ولاة المعاصم والأسود هو الذي قال لرسول كسرى لما قال لهم اما شبعتم لا نصالحكم حتى نأكل عسل اربدين بانرج كوثى وذكر أن ذلك جرى على لسانه ولم يقصده ولاكان يفهم معناه

## Source unit 459 · printed entry 459

### English candidate

Al-Aswad ibn Hilāl al-Muḥāribī, Abū Salām al-Kūfī. He emigrated in the time of ʿUmar; Ibn Saʿd related this. Al-ʿIjlī said that he had lived during the Jāhiliyya and was one of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh. His hadith from the Companions—including Muʿādh ibn Jabal and others—are in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and elsewhere.

Al-Bāwardī transmitted in his work on the Companions, by way of Ashʿath ibn Abī al-Shaʿthāʾ, from al-Aswad ibn Hilāl, who had lived to see the Prophet ﷺ. Al-ʿUthmānī transmitted it likewise, and Ibn Fatḥūn added him to the earlier compilations. Al-Bukhārī transmitted in his Tārīkh, by way of Abū Wāʾil, who said: ‘I went to al-Aswad ibn Hilāl, and he was more intelligent than I.’ Ibn Saʿd said that he died in the time of al-Ḥajjāj. ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī said that he died in the year 84.

## Source unit 460 · printed entry 460

### English candidate

Al-Aswad ibn Yazīd ibn Qays al-Nakhaʿī, Abū ʿAmr; he is also said to have been Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. Ibn Abī Khaythama mentioned that he performed the Hajj with Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān. Ibn Saʿd said that he heard from Muʿādh ibn Jabal in Yemen before he emigrated.

In al-Bukhārī, by way of Ashʿath ibn Sulaym, al-Aswad ibn Yazīd said: ‘Muʿādh ibn Jabal came to us in Yemen as a teacher and governor. We asked him about a man who had died’—and he related the story. Also by way of Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, from his maternal uncle al-Aswad: ‘Muʿādh ibn Jabal rendered judgment among us during the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ.’ Abū Dāwūd transmitted, by way of Abū Ḥassān al-Aʿraj, from al-Aswad ibn Yazīd, that Muʿādh assigned inheritance to a sister and a daughter in Yemen while the Prophet of God was alive.

Al-Bukhārī said that he heard Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. His hadith from senior Companions are in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and elsewhere. Al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba said that he fasted perpetually. Al-ʿIjlī said: ‘A Kūfan who had lived during the Jāhiliyya; trustworthy, righteous, and a jurist.’ He died in the year 74, or it is said 75. Abū Nuʿaym, al-Bukhārī's shaykh, stated the latter categorically.

## Source unit 462 · printed entry 462

### English candidate

Al-Usayfiʿ al-Juhanī. He lived during the time of the Prophet ﷺ and used to outpace the pilgrims. Mālik related in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ, from Ibn Dulāf, from his father, that a man of Juhayna used to buy riding camels and pay high prices for them, then travel swiftly and outpace the pilgrims. He became bankrupt, and his case was brought before ʿUmar. ʿUmar said: ‘To proceed, people: al-Usayfiʿ—Usayfiʿ of Juhayna—was content that all that should be said of his religion and trustworthiness was, “He outpaced the pilgrims.” Take notice: he incurred debt recklessly, and by morning debt had engulfed him. Whoever has a claim against him should come to us tomorrow morning, and we shall divide his property among his creditors. Then beware of debt.’

Al-Dāraquṭnī supplied a connected chain for it by way of Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiya, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAṭiyya ibn Dulāf, from his father, from Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith, from ʿUmar. Ibn Abī Shayba transmitted it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, with that chain. In Gharāʾib Mālik, al-Dāraquṭnī transmitted part of it by way of Ibn Mahdī, from Mālik, from Ibn Dulāf, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿUmar.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq said, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb: one of them related that a man of Juhayna used to purchase riding camels and pay high prices for them. Debt closed in upon him until he became bankrupt. ʿUmar stood on the pulpit, praised and extolled God, and then said: ‘Let neither a man's fasting nor his prayer deceive you. Rather, look at his truthfulness when he speaks, his trustworthiness when he is entrusted, and his scrupulousness when he is free of need.’ He then said, ‘Take notice: al-Usayfiʿ—Usayfiʿ of Juhayna ...,’ and related something similar. Ibn ʿUyayna also transmitted it from Ziyād—namely Ibn Saʿd—from Ibn Dulāf, from his father.

## Source unit 467 · printed entry 467

### English candidate

Al-Ashhab ibn Rumayla was al-Ashhab ibn Thawr ibn Abī Ḥāritha ibn ʿAbd al-Madān ibn Jandal ibn Nahshal ibn Dārim ibn ʿAmr ibn Tamīm. Rumayla was his mother, according to Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī. He said that she had been a slave woman belonging to Jandal ibn Mālik ibn Ribʿī al-Nahshalī and bore Thawr four men in the pre-Islamic period: Rabāb, Ḥajnāʾ, Suwaybiṭ, and al-Ashhab. They were among the strongest sets of brothers among the Arabs in tongue, hand, and defensive strength. They then lived into Islam, accepted it, became wealthy, and grew mighty, to the point that whenever they came to one of the watering places of al-Ṣammān, they barred other people from whatever portion they wanted. In one year they came to a watering place, and a man of Banū Qaṭan ibn Nahshal named Bishr ibn Ṣubayḥ, with the kunya Abū Bidhāl, brought his camel to a trough. Rabāb ibn Rumayla struck him with a staff and split his head. War then broke out between Banū Rumayla and Banū Qaṭan. Banū Qaṭan captured Abū Asmāʾ Ubayy ibn Ashyam al-Nahshalī, chief of Banū Jarwal ibn Nahshal, who was aligned with Banū Rumayla. Nahshal ibn Jarī said, ‘Banū Qaṭan, this man did not take part in your conflict. Bind him to withdraw from you with his people, and release him.’ They did so, and he departed with seventy men of his people. When al-Ashhab ibn Rumayla saw that, he reconciled the parties, handed over his brother Rabāb ibn Rumayla to them, and took custody of the wounded young man. The young man soon died while with him. Al-Ashhab sent to Banū Qaṭan offering blood money. They sought the aid of ʿAbbād ibn Masʿūd ibn Khālid ibn Mālik ibn Ribʿī, and of ʿAwf and Maʿbad, the two sons of al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Maʿbad. They said, ‘We will accept nothing but the killer’s death.’ They intended to kill Rabāb. He said, ‘Let me pray two rakʿas.’ He prayed and then said, ‘By God, I am indeed in need of my Lord. Nothing prevented me from adding to my prayer except that they might think it was fear of death.’ They handed him to the slain man’s father, whose name was Khuzayma, and he struck off Rabāb’s head. This took place during the fitna after ʿUthmān was killed. Al-Ashhab regretted it and elegized his brother:

My two eyes, pour tears for your brother;
stay awake through the whole night and grieve.

A woman weeps for Rabāb, while another says,
‘May God reward him well—how chaste and unyielding he was!’

People have blamed me, and my own soul blames me,
for what my judgment declared concerning Rabāb, lost to us.

Had my heart been iron, this would have melted it;
had it been solid rock, it would have split apart.

Al-Marzubānī mentioned him in Muʿjam al-Shuʿarāʾ under the dotted letter zāʾ and recited what al-Ashhab said when he killed Abū Bidhāl:

I said to him, ‘Be steadfast, Abū Bidhāl!
You shall surely know—by God, I do not care—
that you will never return through all the nights to come.
Be steadfast for it, at the crescent’s first appearance,
the first day of Shawwāl that dawned.’

He said that when Rabāb was killed in retaliation for Abū Bidhāl, al-Ashhab recited:

When I saw the people’s bonds close around
Rabāb amid fierce strife—and he was not weak...

He said that Rabāb was tough and among the strongest of men.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

الأشهب بن رميلة هو بن ثور بن أبي حارثة بن عبد المدان بن جندل بن نهشل بن دارم بن عمرو بن تميم ورميلة أمه قاله أبو عمر الشيباني قال وكانت أمة لجندل بن مالك بن ربعي النهشلي ولدت لثور في الجاهلية أربعة نفر وهم رباب وحجناء سويبط والاشهب فكانوا من أشد إخوة في العرب لسانا ويدا لومعنة ثم أدركوا الإسلام فأسلموا وكثرت أموالهم وعزوا حتى كانوا إذا وردوا ماء من مياه الصمان حظروا على الناس ما يريدونه منه فوردوا في بعض السنين ماء فأورد بعض بني قطن بن نهشل واسمه بشرين صبيح ويكنى أبا بذال بعيره حوضا فضربه رباب بن رميلة بعصا فشجه فكانت بين بني رميلة وبين بني قطن حرب فاسر بنو قطن أبا أسماء أبي بن أشيم النهشلي وكان سيد بني جرول بن نهشل وكان مع بني رميلة فقال نهشل بن جرى يا بني قطن إن هذا لم يشهد شركم فخذوا عليه أن ينصرف عنكم بقومه واطلقوه ففعلوا فذهب من قومه بسعبين رجلا فلما رأى الأشهب بن رميلة ذلك أصلح بينهم ودفع أخاه رباب بن رميلة إليهم وأخذ منهم الفتى المضروب فلم يلبث أن مات عنده فأرسل إلى بني قطن يعرض عليهم الدية واستعانوا بعباد بن مسعود ومالك بن ربعي ومالك بن عوف والقعقاع بن معبد فقالوا لا نرضى الا بقتل قاتله وأرادوا قتل الرباب فقال لهم دعوني أصلى ركعتين فصلى وقال أما والله إني إلى ربي لذو حاجة وما منعني أن ازيد في صلاتي إلا أن يروا أن ذلك فرق من الموت فدفعوه إلى والد المقتول واسمه خزيمة فضرب عنقه وذلك في الفتنة بعد قتل عثمان فندم الأشهب على ذلك فقال يرثي أخاه <br />
 أعيني قلت عبرة من أخيكما <br />
 بأن تسهرا الليل التمام وتجزعا <br />

## Source unit 470 · printed entry 470

Al-Aṣbagh ibn ʿAmr ibn Thaʿlaba ibn Ḥiṣn ibn Ḍamḍam ibn ʿAdī ibn Janāb al-Kalbī al-Quḍāʿī. He had been a Christian and accepted Islam at the hands of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān married his daughter Tamāḍir at the Prophet’s ﷺ instruction. Al-Wāqidī mentioned this from Saʿīd ibn Bānik. Al-Dāraquṭnī transmitted it in al-Afrād by way of Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, the companion of Abū Ḥanīfa ﵀, from Saʿīd ibn Muslim ibn Bānik, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Prophet ﷺ summoned ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and said, ‘Make ready, for I am sending you with an expedition.’ He then related the report. It states that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān went out and joined his companions, then traveled until he reached Dūmat al-Jandal. When he entered it, he called its people to Islam for three days. On the third day, al-Aṣbagh ibn ʿAmr al-Kalbī—who had been a Christian and was their chief—accepted Islam. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān then wrote with a man of Juhayna named Rāfiʿ ibn Makīth to the Prophet ﷺ concerning marriage to al-Aṣbagh’s daughter. He married her; she was Tamāḍir, who later bore him Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. I read the report in full to Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Zaynī: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Khālid al-Bāriqī informed them: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Manāqib informed us: Abū al-Yaman al-Kindī informed us: Abū Manṣūr al-Qazzāz informed us: Abū al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Naqūr informed us: Abū Saʿd al-Ismāʿīlī informed us, from al-Dāraquṭnī’s selection: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Khabbāz related to us: ʿAmr ibn Tamīm related to us: Abū Sulaymān Mūsā ibn Sulaymān al-Jūzajānī related to us: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, the companion of Abū Ḥanīfa, related to us—and he transmitted it at length. Al-Dāraquṭnī said in al-Afrād: ‘Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan alone transmitted it from Saʿīd, and none but Abū Sulaymān transmitted it from him.’ I say: al-Wāqidī’s transmission of it from Saʿīd rebuts that unrestricted statement. والله أعلم.

## Source unit 473 · printed entry 473

### English candidate

Aṣḥama ibn Abḥar, the Negus, king of Abyssinia. His name in Arabic was ʿAṭiyya, while ‘the Negus’ was his title. He accepted Islam during the time of the Prophet ﷺ but did not emigrate to him. He was a useful support to the Muslims. His kindness to the Muslims who emigrated to him at the beginning of Islam is a well-known story in the works on military biography. The authors of the Ṣaḥīḥ collections transmitted the account of the Prophet’s ﷺ absentee funeral prayer for him by several routes. Among them is the transmission of Saʿīd ibn Mīnāʾ from Jābir, and another from ʿAṭāʾ, from Jābir: when the Negus died, the Prophet ﷺ said, ‘A righteous servant named Aṣḥama has died today. Rise and pray over Aṣḥama.’ We formed rows behind him. This is the wording of al-Qaṭṭān from Ibn Jurayj, from him, reporting from the Prophet ﷺ. In Ibn ʿUyayna’s transmission from Ibn Jurayj, the wording is: ‘A righteous servant has died today. Rise and pray over Aṣḥama.’ Al-Ṭabarī and a group said that this occurred in Rajab of the year nine; others said that it was before the Conquest. Ibn Isḥāq related from Yazīd ibn Rūmān, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha: ‘When the Negus died, we used to discuss that a light continued to be seen over his grave.’ Ibn Shāhīn and al-Dāraquṭnī in al-Afrād transmitted by way of Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān, from Ḥumayd, from Anas, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘Rise and pray over your brother, the Negus.’ Some of them said, ‘Do you order us to pray over a non-Arab from Abyssinia?’ God Most High then revealed: ‘Indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God...’ to the end of the sūra. Al-Dāraquṭnī said, ‘We know of none who transmitted it other than Abū Hāniʾ Aḥmad ibn Bakkār from Muʿtamir.’ It also came by way of Zamʿa ibn Ṣāliḥ, from al-Zuhrī and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Hurayra, who said: ‘One morning we were with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he said, “Your brother Aṣḥama, the Negus, has died, so pray over him.”’ The Messenger of God ﷺ sprang up, and we sprang up with him until he came to the prayer ground. He stood, we formed rows behind him, and he pronounced four takbīrs. The best-known pronunciation of al-Najāshī has fatḥa on the nūn; Thaʿlab held that it may have kasra. Its jīm is light, and whoever doubled it was mistaken, according to al-Muṭarrizī. Its final letter is doubled; al-Muṭarrizī also reported a light final and al-Ṣaghānī preferred that. Aṣḥama follows the morphological pattern of arbaʿa. Its ḥāʾ is unpointed, though it is also said to be the pointed khāʾ. It is also said to have bāʾ in place of mīm; to be Ṣaḥma without the initial alif; likewise without alif but with the mīm placed before the ṣād; and to begin with an additional mīm in place of the alif, according to Ibn Isḥāq in al-Ḥākim’s al-Mustadrak. The well-known form from Ibn Isḥāq is the first. These disagreements yield six forms of his name, which I have not seen collected elsewhere.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

أصحمة بن ابحر النجاشي ملك الحبشة واسمه بالعربية عطية والنجاشي لقب له أسلم على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يهاجر إليه وكان ردءا للمسلمين نافعا وقصته مشهورة في المغازي في إحسانه إلى المسلمين الذين هاجروا إليه في صدر الإسلام وأخرج أصحاب الصحيح قصة صلاته صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة الغائب من طرق منها رواية سعيد بن مينا عن جابر ومنها رواية عطاء بن جابر لما مات النجاشي قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد مات اليوم عبد صالح يقال له أصحمة فقوموا فصلوا على أصحمة فصفنا خلفه هذا لفظ القطان عن بن جريج عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي رواية بن عيينة عن بن جريج قد مات اليوم عبد صالح فقوموا فصلوا على أصحمة قال الطبري وجماعة كان ذلك في رجب سنة تسع وقال غيره كان قبل الفتح قال بن إسحاق عن يزيد بن رومان عن عروة عن عائشة لما مات النجاشي كنا نتحدثه أنه لا يزال يرى على قبره نور وعند بن شاهين والدار قطني في الأفراد من طريق معتمر بن سليمان عن حميد عن أنس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قوموا فصلوا على أخيكم النجاشي فقال بعضهم تأمرنا أن نصلي على علج من الحبشة فأنزل الله تعالى @QB@ وإن من أهل الكتاب لمن يؤمن بالله @QE@ إلى آخر السورة قال الدارقطني لا نعلم رواه غير أبي هانئ أحمد بن بكار عن معتمر وجاء من طريق زمعة بن الصالح عن الزهري ويحيى بن سعيد عن سعيد بن المسيب عن أبي هريرة قال أصبحنا ذات يوم عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إن أخاكم أصحمة النجاشي قد توفي فصلوا عليه قال فوثب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ووثبنا معه حتى جاء المصلي فقام فصففنا وراءه فكبر أربع تكبيرات والنجاشي بفتح النون على المشهور وقيل تكسر على ثعلب وتخفيف الجيم وأخطأ من شددها عن المطرزي وبتشديد آخره وحكى المطرزي التخفيف ورجحه الصغاني وأصحمة بوزن أربعة وحاؤه مهملة وقيل معجمة وقيل إنه بموحدة بدل الميم وقيل صحمة بغير ألف وقيل كذلك لكن بتقديم الميم على الصاد وقيل بزيادة ميم في أوله بدل الألف عن بن إسحاق في المستدرك للحاكم والمعروف عن بن إسحاق الأول ويتحصل من هذا الخلاف في اسمه ستة ألفاظ لم أرها مجموعة

## Source unit 477 · printed entry 477

### English candidate

Uṭṭ ibn Abī Uṭṭ, one of the Banū Saʿd ibn Bakr. He accompanied Khālid ibn al-Walīd during Abū Bakr's time. The Nahr Uṭṭ in Iraq is named after him. Khālid appointed him over the land tax of that district, so its river was named for him. Al-Ṭabarī mentioned this from Sayf. Elsewhere it appears as Uṭṭ ibn Suwayd, perhaps his father's name. Ibn Fatḥūn added him in a supplement. I saw the first letter reliably vocalized with ḍamma on the hamza.

## Source unit 485 · printed entry 485

### English candidate

Aktham ibn Ṣayfī ibn Rabāḥ ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Mukhāshin ibn Muʿāwiya ibn Sharīf ibn Jarwa ibn Usayyid ibn ʿAmr ibn Tamīm al-Tamīmī, the famous sage. He was the uncle of Ḥanẓala ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn Ṣayfī, the famous Companion.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: Ibn al-Sakan mentioned him among the Companions, but in doing so accomplished nothing. The report he cited says that when word of the emergence of the Prophet ﷺ reached Aktham ibn Ṣayfī, he wished to go to him, but his people refused to let him. He said, “Then let someone go who will convey from me and convey back to me from him.” Two men volunteered for him. They came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “We are the messengers of Aktham ibn Ṣayfī. He asks you: Who are you? What are you? And with what have you come?” He said, “I am Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and I am God’s servant and His messenger.” Then he recited to them, “Indeed, God commands justice and excellence …” [Qurʾan 16:90]. They came to Aktham and told him this. He said, “My people, he commands the noblest qualities of character and forbids their basest ones. Be leaders in this matter, and do not be tails.” It was not long before death came upon him. He said, “I enjoin upon you fear of God and maintenance of kinship ties”; the remainder of the report gives his testament.

Ibn al-Sakan said: Ibn Ṣāʿid related to us; al-Ḥasan ibn Dāwūd related to us, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir; ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī al-Muqaddamī related to us, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿUmayr, from his father, and he related it. It is a disconnected report. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said, “There is nothing in this report to indicate his acceptance of Islam.”

Ibn Fatḥūn said: Al-Bāwardī mentioned him among the Companions just as Ibn al-Sakan did, and transmitted the report through Ibrāhīm ibn Yūsuf, from al-Munkadir. Al-Umawī, however, mentioned it in his Maghāzī. He said: My uncle related to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ziyād, who said: One of our companions related to me, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, with a similar report, adding that a camel was brought near for Aktham, and he mounted it and set out toward the Prophet ﷺ, but died on the road. He said it is also related that this verse was revealed concerning him: “Whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to God and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has already fallen due from God” [Qurʾan 4:100]. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ziyād is Ibn Samʿān, one of the abandoned transmitters. If this report were sound, it would be evidence against Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr’s position that Aktham accepted Islam, and Aktham would meet Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr’s criterion for including his counterparts in his book—those who did not meet the Prophet ﷺ.

I have found corroboration for him. Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī mentioned it in Kitāb al-Muʿammarīn, from ʿAmr ibn Muḥammad al-Saʿdī, from ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī, who said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about this verse. He said, “It was revealed concerning Aktham ibn Ṣayfī.” I asked, “Then where does that leave al-Laythī?” He said, “This was long before al-Laythī; it is specific and general.” Abū Ḥātim also transmitted in al-Muʿammarīn, from Rushdayn ibn Kurayb, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the cited verse was revealed concerning Aktham.

Al-Aṣmaʿī said: Abū Ḥāḍir al-Asadī related to us, from his father, who said: Among the things Aktham ibn Ṣayfī enjoined upon his son when setting out toward the Prophet ﷺ was—and he then related his story.

Al-ʿAskarī said in al-Ṣaḥāba, in the section on those who lived into the time of the Prophet ﷺ but did not meet him: The authorities on reports related that Aktham set out toward the Prophet ﷺ, but that a nephew of his obstructed their route so that he would turn back. The water was lost; he turned back and died of thirst.

Ibn Manda followed Ibn al-Sakan in including him and transmitted the cited report from him, adding nothing. He then listed “Aktham ibn Ṣayfī,” said that he was Ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, and set out the lineage of Aktham ibn al-Jawn al-Khuzāʿī; then he listed “Aktham ibn al-Jawn” and supplied him a separate entry. This is counted among Ibn Manda’s errors.

I then found the story to which al-ʿAskarī alluded at length in Kitāb al-Ṣaḥāba, and it expressly states that Aktham accepted Islam. Abū Ḥātim said in al-Muʿammarīn: When Aktham heard of the emergence of the Prophet ﷺ, he sent his son Ḥubaysh to bring him news of him. He said, “My son, I admonish you with certain words. Hold to them from the time you leave me until you return.” He then related a long story, in which the Prophet ﷺ wrote back to him: “I praise for you God, other than whom there is no deity. God has commanded me to say: There is no deity but God.” Aktham asked his son, “What did you see?” He replied, “I saw him commanding the noblest qualities of character and forbidding their basest ones.” Aktham gathered his people, called them to follow him, and said to them, “Sufyān ibn Mujāshiʿ named his son Muḥammad out of love for this man, and the bishop of Najrān used to foretell his affair and his mission. Be first in his cause; do not be last.”

Mālik ibn Nuwayra said to them, “Your shaykh has become senile.” Aktham replied, “Woe to the afflicted at the hands of the untroubled! By God, I do not grieve over you, but over the common people.” Then he called out among his people, and one hundred men followed him, among them al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis, Salmā ibn al-Qayn, Abū Tamīma al-Hujaymī, Rabāḥ ibn al-Rabīʿ, al-Hunayd, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Rabīʿ, and Ṣafwān ibn Usayyid.

They traveled until, when they were four nights’ journey short of Medina, his son Ḥubaysh disliked his journey. By night he went to the camels of his father’s companions, slaughtered them, and slit open their waterskins and leather water bags. In the morning they had neither water nor mounts. Thirst exhausted them, and Aktham became certain he would die. He said to his companions, “Proceed to this man and inform him that I bear witness that there is no deity but God and that he is the Messenger of God. See whether he has with him a scripture that makes plain what he says. If so, believe in him, follow him, and support him.” They came to him and accepted Islam.

News of Aktham’s departure reached Ḥājib and Wakīʿ, and they set out after him. When they passed his grave, they stayed beside it and slaughtered a camel there. Then they came to his companions and asked them, “What did Aktham command you?” They replied, “He commanded us to accept Islam.” The two accepted Islam with them.

Abū Ḥātim said: Aktham lived three hundred and thirty years. His father Ṣayfī was also one of the long-lived and lived two hundred and seventy years. It is also said that Aktham lived one hundred and ninety years.

I say: Al-Marzubānī recited these verses of his:

“A man who has lived ninety years,
approaching a hundred, yet has not wearied of life, is ignorant.
Two hundred years came, ten short of their completion;
and that, among the passing nights, is little.”

Al-Khaṭīb mentioned these two verses through his chain to Abū Ḥātim and transmitted from him that Aktham used to say, “A man’s heart is only a morsel of his body, and it wastes away just as the rest of his body wastes away.” Al-Khaṭīb said: He possessed wisdom and eloquence.

ولا ظهر فجهدهم العطش وأيقن أكثم بالموت فقال لأصحابه اقدموا على هذا الرجل وأعلموه بأني أشهد أن لا أله إلا الله وأنه رسول الله انظروا إن كان معه كتاب بإيضاح ما يقول فآمنوا به واتبعوه وآزروه قال فقدموا عليه فأسلموا قال فبلغ حاجبا ووكيعا خروج أكثم فخرجا في أثره فلما مرا بقبره أقاما به ونحرا عليه جزورا ثم قدما على أصحابه فقالا لهم ماذا أمركم به أكثم قالوا أمرنا بالإسلام قال فأسلما معهم قال أبو حاتم عاش أكثم ثلاثمائة وثلاثين سنة وكان أبوه صيفي أيضا من المعمرين عاش مائتين وسبعين سنة ويقال بل عاش أكثم مائة وتسعين سنة قلت وأنشد له المرزباني <br />
 وإن امرئ عاش تسعين حجة <br />
 إلى مائة لم يسأم العيش جاهل <br />
 أتت مائتان غير عشر وفائها <br />
 وذلك من مر الليالي قلائل وذكر الخطيب هذين البيتين بسنده إلى أبي حاتم ونقل عنه أنه كان يقول إنما قلب الرجل مضغة منه وإنه ينحل كما ينحل سائر جسده وقال الخطيب وكانت له حكمة وبلاغة

## Source unit 486 · printed entry 486

### English candidate

Al-Akdar ibn Ḥimām ibn ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿb ibn Kathīr ibn ʿIkārima ibn Hudhayl ibn Saʿīd ibn Razīn ibn Tamīm al-Lakhmī. He lived into the Islamic era.

Saʿīd ibn ʿUfair said: He and his father witnessed the conquest of Egypt. Abū ʿUmar al-Kindī said in Kitāb al-Khandaq: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Muʿāwiya ibn Khalaf ibn Rabīʿa related to me, from his father; al-Walīd ibn Sulaymān related to me, saying: Al-Akdar was a partisan of ʿAlī. He was a man of religion, merit, and understanding in religion. He sat with the Companions and transmitted from them. He is the man associated with the inheritance problem called al-Akdariyya.

He was among those who journeyed to ʿUthmān. Muʿāwiya used him to cultivate his people’s loyalty: he honored him, paid his stipend to him, and elevated his place in the assembly. When Marwān besieged the people of Egypt, al-Akdar rallied his people against him and opposed him in every matter Marwān disliked. When Marwān made peace with the people of Egypt, he knew that al-Akdar would return to his actions. He therefore incited a group of Syrians against him; they alleged that he had killed one of their men. Marwān summoned him, and they gave testimony against him, so Marwān ordered that he be killed.

He said: Mūsā ibn ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ related to me, from his father, who said: I was standing at Marwān’s gate when he summoned al-Akdar. Al-Akdar came, not knowing why he had been summoned, and he was killed almost at once. The troops called out to one another, “Al-Akdar has been killed!” Not one of them failed to put on his weapons and come to Marwān’s gate. They numbered more than eighty thousand people. Marwān, afraid, shut his gate.

They went to Kurayb ibn Abraha and informed him of what had happened. They found him attending the funeral of his wife, Basīsa bint Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd Kulāl. When he had finished, he came in their company to Marwān and entered his presence. Marwān said to him, “Come here, Abū Rashīd.” He said, “Rather, come here to me, Commander of the Faithful.” Marwān rose and came to him; Kurayb cast his cloak over Marwān and said, “He is under my protection.” The army withdrew from Marwān, and al-Akdar’s blood went unavenged.

Abū ʿUmar al-Kindī transmitted through Ibn Lahīʿa that al-Akdar ibn Ḥimām became ill in Medina during the days of ʿUthmān. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib came to visit him and asked, “How do you find yourself?” He replied, “What afflicts me is grave, Commander of the Faithful.” ʿAlī said, “No indeed! You will live for a time; a betrayer will betray you; and you will go to Paradise, إن شاء الله تعالى.”

Al-Bayhaqī transmitted in al-Shuʿab, through ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from Saʿīd ibn Khudayj ibn Ṣawmī, that he heard al-Akdar ibn Ḥimām say: A man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ informed me, saying: One day we were sitting in the mosque. We said to a youth among us, “Go to the Messenger of God ﷺ and ask him what equals the rank of jihad.” He went to him and asked him. He replied, “Nothing.”

Abū ʿUmar al-Kindī transmitted through Abū Bakr ibn Abī Maryam, from Musāfir ibn Ḥanẓala, from al-Akdar ibn Ḥimām, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “Learn trades, for it may soon happen that one of you will need a trade.”

Ibn Abī Shayba said: Wakīʿ related to us, from Sufyān, who said: I asked al-Aʿmash, “Why was the inheritance problem called al-Akdariyya?” He replied, “ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān put it to a man called al-Akdar who studied the inheritance shares, and he erred in it.” Wakīʿ said: Before that, we used to hear that Zayd ibn Thābit’s opinion became muddled in it.

I say: If al-Aʿmash’s statement is accurately preserved, perhaps ʿAbd al-Malik put the problem to al-Akdar at an early date, while ʿAbd al-Malik was pursuing knowledge in Medina. Otherwise, as stated above, this al-Akdar was killed before ʿAbd al-Malik assumed the caliphate.

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted in his Tafsīr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Mubārak, from Zayd ibn al-Mubārak, from Muḥammad ibn Thawr, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning God Most High’s words, “No harm touched them” [Qurʾan 3:174]: A man from among the polytheists came from Badr and told the people of Mecca about Muḥammad’s cavalry. They were terrified and sat down, and he recited poetry about that. They claim that he was al-Akdar ibn Ḥimām.

## Source unit 487 · printed entry 487

### English candidate

Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿAdī ibn Aws ibn Jābir ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿAlīm ibn Hubal ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kināna ibn Bakr ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿUdhra ibn Zayd al-Lāt ibn Rufayda ibn Thawr ibn Kalb al-Kalbī. He lived into the Islamic period. Ibn al-Kalbī mentioned him and said that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb appointed him over those of Quḍāʿa in al-Shām who had embraced Islam. ʿAlī sought a marriage alliance with him, accompanied by his two sons al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, and he married his daughters to the three of them. Concerning his daughter al-Rabāb, by whom al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī had his daughter Sukayna, al-Ḥusayn said:

‘By your life, I truly love a house
where Sukayna and al-Rabāb are found.’

I say: we transmitted his story in the Amālī of Thaʿlab. Ibn Shabīb related to us: al-Zubayr related to us: ʿAlī ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from Abū al-Muthannā Umayya, who informed me: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥasan related to me: my maternal uncle ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Manẓūr related to me: ʿAwf ibn Khārija said: By God, I was with ʿUmar during his caliphate when a man with sparse hair came forward, stepping over people’s necks, until he stood before ʿUmar and greeted him with the salutation due the caliphate. He asked, ‘Who are you?’ The man replied, ‘I am a Christian man—and I am Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿAdī al-Kalbī.’ ʿUmar did not recognize him, but a man told him, ‘This is the adversary of Bakr ibn Wāʾil who raided them in the pre-Islamic period.’ ʿUmar asked, ‘What do you want?’ He replied, ‘I want Islam.’ ʿUmar presented it to him, and he accepted it. He then called for a spear and tied a banner to it for him, appointing him over those of Quḍāʿa who had embraced Islam. The shaykh departed with the banner fluttering above his head. ʿAwf said, ‘Before him, I had never seen a man who had not performed a single prayer appointed over a body of Muslims.’

ʿAlī and his two sons rose and caught up with him. ʿAlī said, ‘I am ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, son of the Prophet’s uncle ﷺ, and these are my two sons by his daughter. We desire a marriage alliance with you, so give us your daughters in marriage.’ He replied, ‘ʿAlī, I have married al-Muḥayyāt daughter of Imruʾ al-Qays to you; Ḥasan, I have married Salmā daughter of Imruʾ al-Qays to you; and Ḥusayn, I have married al-Rabāb daughter of Imruʾ al-Qays to you.’ He said: she was Sukayna’s mother, and concerning her al-Ḥusayn said:

‘By your life, I truly love a house
where Sukayna and al-Rabāb dwell.’

She was the woman who remained at al-Ḥusayn’s grave for a year and then recited:

‘Until the year is complete; then the name of peace be upon you both.
Whoever weeps for a full year has offered sufficient excuse.’

## Source unit 492 · printed entry 492

### English candidate

Unayf ibn Yazīd ibn Fahda al-Kaʿbī, one of the Banū ʿAmr ibn Tamīm. His father was a noted horseman in the pre-Islamic period, and his son Unayf lived into the Islamic period. Unayf had a son named Ghaṭafān, a poet who is mentioned in connection with the caliphate of Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya and the period after it. When Masʿūd ibn ʿAmr al-Azdī rose in support of the cause of ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyād, Ghaṭafān urged the Banū Tamīm on with rajaz verses that included:

‘O Tamīm! This is a deed that will be remembered.
If Masʿūd escapes through it, it will become notorious.
So hold fast to the side of the screened enclosure!’

The Banū Tamīm came to the enclosure while Masʿūd was on the pulpit, pulled him down, and killed him. They besieged Mālik ibn Mismaʿ in his house and burned what lay around it. Ghaṭafān also said concerning that:

‘And Ibn Mismaʿ came to be besieged,
defending palaces and houses before him,
until we kindled the blaze around him.’

Al-Marzubānī mentioned him in his Muʿjam. Concerning this episode, al-Farazdaq al-Tamīmī said, boasting of what his people had done:

‘We deposed and appointed, while Bakr ibn Wāʾil
dragged its testicles, seeking someone with whom to ally.’

## Source unit 498 · printed entry 498

### English candidate

Aws ibn Maghrāʾ al-Qurayʿī, a mukhaḍram whose kunya was Abū al-Maghrāʾ. Al-Marzubānī said that he took part in the conquests, lived into the time of Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān, and had an episode with al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī. He is the one who said:

‘By your life, the shirts of ʿĀmir shall not wear out
from baseness so long as their skins remain upon them.’

He also composed poetry praising the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Sayyid al-Nās included it in his book on the Companions who praised al-Muṣṭafā, and stated that Aws was a mukhaḍram. From it is:

‘Muḥammad is the best of those who walk on foot,
and his two Companions, and ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān.’

Ibn Isḥāq recited from the poem in the Sīra:

‘People shall not leave, so long as they perform pilgrimage, their station at ʿArafāt
until it is said, “Lead forth, O house of Ṣafwān!”’

It is a long ode in which he enumerated their feats in the conquests and elsewhere and boasted of Quraysh. Ibn Abī Ṭāhir said, ‘No one ever composed anything finer than it.’

## Source unit 500 · printed entry 500

### English candidate

Uways ibn ʿĀmir—also said to be ʿAmr. He is also called Uways ibn ʿĀmir ibn Juzʾ ibn Mālik ibn ʿAmr ibn Masʿada ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿd ibn ʿAṣwān ibn Qaran ibn Radmān ibn Nājiya ibn Murād, al-Murādī al-Qaranī, the famous ascetic. He lived into the time of the Prophet ﷺ, transmitted from ʿUmar and ʿAlī, and was transmitted from by Bashīr ibn ʿAmr and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā.

Ibn Saʿd mentioned him in the first generation of the Successors of Kufa and said that he was reliable. Al-Bukhārī mentioned him and said, “There is a problem in his chain.” Ibn ʿAdī said, “He has no transmitted material.” Mālik, however, used to deny that he existed. Yet his fame and the fame of his reports leave no room for anyone to doubt him.

ʿAbd al-Ghanī ibn Saʿīd said: Al-Qaranī—with the qāf and rāʾ pronounced with fatḥa—is Uways. The Prophet ﷺ foretold him before his appearance. He witnessed Ṣiffīn with ʿAlī and was among the best Muslims.

Ḍamra transmitted from Aṣbagh ibn Zayd, who said: Uways accepted Islam during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, but dutifulness toward his mother prevented him from coming.

Muslim transmitted in his Ṣaḥīḥ, in the hadith of Abū Naḍra from Usayr ibn Jābir, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, “The best of the Successors is a man called Uways ibn ʿĀmir.” In another version of Muslim’s: “Whoever among you meets him, command him to ask forgiveness for you.”

Muslim also has it through Qatāda, from Zurāra, from Usayr ibn Jābir. In it ʿUmar says: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, “Uways ibn ʿĀmir will come to you with the reinforcement contingents of Yemen, then from Murād, then from Qaran. He had leprosy and was cured of it except for a spot the size of a dirham. He has a mother to whom he is devoted. Were he to swear an oath by God, God would fulfill it for him. If you are able to have him ask forgiveness for you, do so.” The remainder of the hadith follows.

Al-Bayhaqī and Abū Nuʿaym transmitted it in their Dalāʾil, and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilya, at length through this route. It also has other routes. Among them is what Ibn Manda transmitted through Saʿd ibn al-Ṣalt, from Mubārak ibn Faḍāla, from Marwān al-Aṣghar, from Ṣaʿṣaʿa ibn Muʿāwiya, who said: When delegations from Kufa came to ʿUmar, he would ask them, “Do you know Uways ibn ʿĀmir al-Qaranī?” They would say, “No,” and he related a similar report.

Hudba ibn Khālid transmitted it from Mubārak, but gave Abū al-Aṣghar in place of Marwān al-Aṣghar; Abū Yaʿlā transmitted it. In his Musnad, al-Rūyānī transmitted through Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Abū Hurayra, a hadith describing the God-fearing elect. He said: We asked, “Messenger of God, how can we find a man among them?” He said, “That is Uways,” and then related the hadith in which the Prophet ﷺ instructed ʿAlī and ʿUmar, if they met him, to ask him to seek forgiveness for them. It also contains the story of ʿUmar’s search for him.

Ibn Abī Khaythama said: Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf related to us, from Ḍamra, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from his father, who said: Uways al-Qaranī used to sit with a man among the jurists of Kufa called Yusayr. He then related the report with a disconnected chain.

In al-Bayhaqī’s Dalāʾil, through al-Thaqafī, from Khālid, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Jadʿāʾ, raised to the Prophet, it says: “Through the intercession of one man from my community, more people than the Banū Tamīm will enter Paradise.” Al-Thaqafī said: Hishām ibn Ḥassān said that al-Ḥasan used to say, “It is Uways al-Qaranī.” He will be mentioned again in the entry on Furāt ibn Ḥayyān.

Aḥmad said in his Musnad: Abū Nuʿaym related to us; Sharīk related to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, who said: On the day of Ṣiffīn, a Syrian man called out, “Is Uways al-Qaranī among you?” They said, “Yes.” He said, “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: Among the best of the Successors is Uways al-Qaranī.” A group transmitted it from Sharīk.

Ibn ʿAmmār al-Mawṣilī said: In the presence of al-Muʿāfā ibn ʿImrān, it was mentioned that Uways had been killed among the infantry with ʿAlī at Ṣiffīn. Al-Muʿāfā said, “No one but al-Aʿraj has related this.” ʿAbd Rabbih al-Wāsiṭī said to him, “Sharīk related it to me, from Yazīd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā.” He then fell silent.

Aḥmad transmitted in al-Zuhd from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Mahdī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ashʿath ibn Sawwār, from Muḥārib ibn Dithār, raising it: “Among my community are people unable, for want of clothing, to come to their mosque or place of prayer; their faith restrains them from asking people. Among them are Uways al-Qaranī and Furāt ibn Ḥayyān.” Aḥmad also transmitted it in al-Zuhd from Abū Muʿāwiya, from al-Aʿmash, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, with a disconnected chain.

In al-Mustadrak, through Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, from Abū ʿUbayda al-Ḥaddād, Abū Makīs related to us, saying: I saw a woman in the mosque of Uways al-Qaranī. She said, “He and some companions of his used to gather in this mosque, praying and reciting, until they went on campaign. Uways and a group of his companions were martyred among the infantry before ʿAlī.”

Through al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubāta: I witnessed ʿAlī say on the day of Ṣiffīn, “Who will pledge himself to me unto death?” Ninety-nine men pledged themselves to him. He said, “Where is the one who completes the number?” A man wearing tattered wool garments, with his head shaven, came and pledged himself to be killed. It was said, “This is Uways al-Qaranī.” He continued fighting until he was killed.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad transmitted in the additions to al-Musnad, through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salama, who said: We campaigned in Azerbaijan in the time of ʿUmar, and Uways was with us. When we returned, he fell ill and died. In the chain is al-Haytham ibn ʿAdī, who is abandoned. The first account is the one relied upon.

Al-Ḥākim transmitted through Ibn al-Mubārak: Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān informed us, from al-Jurayrī, from Abū Naḍra al-ʿAbdī, from Usayr ibn Jābir, who said: A companion of mine said to me while I was in Kufa, “Would you like to look at a man?” He then related the story of Uways. In it, Uways withdrew beside a column and prayed two rakʿas. Then he turned his face toward us and said, “What do you want with me, treading on my heels? I am a weak man. I may have a need but be unable to attend to it because of you. Do not do this, may God have mercy on you. Whoever has a need from me, let him meet me in the evening.”

He then said, “Three sorts of men attend this gathering: a learned believer, a believer without understanding, and a hypocrite. In this world that is like rain falling upon a full-grown, fruit-bearing tree, increasing it in beauty, ripeness, and fragrance; falling upon a tree that bears no fruit, increasing the beauty of its leaves and causing it to bear fruit; and falling upon the dry brushwood of a tree and crushing it.”

Then he recited, “We send down of the Qurʾan that which is healing and mercy for the believers, but it increases the wrongdoers only in loss” [Qurʾan 17:82]. He said, “O God, grant me martyrdom that will secure for me life and provision.”

Usayr said: It was only a short time before ʿAlī levied the people for a campaign. The man with the woolen cloak, Uways, went out, and we went out with him until we encamped in the enemy’s presence.

Ibn al-Mubārak said: Ḥammād ibn Salama related to me, from al-Jurayrī, from Abū Naḍra, from Usayr, who said: ʿAlī’s herald called, “Cavalry of God, mount and rejoice!” The people formed ranks against them. Uways drew his sword, broke its sheath, and cast it aside. Then he began saying, “People, fill the ranks! Fill them—let the faces be made complete! Then do not turn back until you see Paradise.” He kept saying that and advancing, when a projectile came and struck his heart. He fell on the spot, as though he had been dead for an age. Its chain is sound.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

أويس بن عامر وقيل عمرو ويقال أويس بن عامر بن جزء بن مالك بن عمرو بن مسعدة بن عمرو بن سعد بن عصوان بن قرن بن ردمان بن ناجية بن مراد المرادي القرني الزاهد المشهور أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وروى عن عمر وعلي وروى عنه بشير بن عمرو وعبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى ذكره بن سعد في الطبقة الأولى من تابعي أهل الكوفة وقال كان ثقة وذكره البخاري فقال في إسناده نظر وقال بن عدي ليس له رواية لكن كان مالك ينكر وجوده إلا أن شهرته وشهرة أخباره لا تسع أحدا أن يشك فيه وقال عبد الغني بن سعيد القرني بفتح القاف والراء هو أويس أخبر به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل وجوده وشهد صفين مع علي وكان من خيار المسلمين وروى ضمرة عن أصبغ بن زيد قال أسلم أويس على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولكن منعه من القدوم بره بأمه وروى مسلم في صحيحه من حديث أبي نضرة عن أسير بن جابر عن عمر بن الخطاب قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول إن خير التابعين رجل يقال له أويس بن عامر وفي رواية له فمن لقيه منكم فمروه فليستغفر لكم وله من طريق قتادة عن زرارة عن أسير بن جابر وفيها قول عمر سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول يأتي عليك أويس بن عامر مع أمداد أهل اليمن ثم من مراد ثم من قرن كان به برص فبرأ منه الا موضع درهم له والدة هر بها بر لو أقسم على الله لأبره فإن استطعت أن يستغفر لك فافعل الحديث ورواه البيهقي وأبو نعيم في الدلائل وفي القرني فيقولون لا فذكر نحوه ورواه هدبة بن خالد عن مبارك عن أبي الأصغر بدل مروان الأصغر أخرجه أبو يعلى وروى الروياني في مسنده من طريق بكر بن عبد الله عن الضحاك عن أبي هريرة فذكر حديثا في وصف الأتقياء الاصفياء قال فقلنا يا رسول الله كيف لنا برجل منهم قال ذاك أويس وساق الحديث في توصية النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عليا وعمر إذا لقيا أن يستغفر لهما وفيه قصة طلب عمر إياه وقال بن أبي خيثمة حدثنا هارون بن ## Source unit 502 · printed entry 502

### English candidate

Iyās ibn Ṣabīḥ ibn al-Muḥarrish ibn ʿAbd ʿAmr al-Ḥanafī, whose kunya was Abū Maryam. Ibn Saʿd said: He was one of the followers of Musaylima; then he repented, and his Islam became sound. He was appointed judge of Basra during the time of ʿUmar. Yazīd ibn Hārūn informed us; Hishām informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, from Abū Maryam al-Ḥanafī: ʿUmar recited after relieving himself. Abū Maryam al-Ḥanafī said to him, “You have just come out of the privy.” ʿUmar replied, “Did Musaylima give you that ruling?” Its chain is sound. Al-Bukhārī transmitted it in his Tārīkh through other routes from Hishām with similar wording. Al-ʿAskarī claimed that this Abū Maryam is not the Abū Maryam al-Ḥanafī who killed Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.

## Source unit 505 · printed entry 505

### English candidate

Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-ʿUdhrī, a Successor. He transmitted a hadith with a disconnected chain, so Ibn Manda and others mentioned him among the Companions.

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿArafa transmitted: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Muʿān ibn Rifāʿa, who said: Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-ʿUdhrī—who was one of the Companions—related to me, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “The upright members of every succeeding generation will carry this knowledge …”

Ibn Manda said: Ibn ʿArafa was not followed in his statement, “who was one of the Companions.”

I say: We transmitted it in Kitāb al-Ghurar min al-Akhbār by Wakīʿ al-Qāḍī. He said: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿArafa related to us, and he related it without saying, “who was one of the Companions.” Ibn Manda then transmitted it through Baqiyya, from Muʿān, from Ibrāhīm, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said—and he cited it. Abū Nuʿaym also included it, then said: Al-Walīd transmitted it in the same way from Muʿān.

Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān ibn Abī Karīma transmitted it from Muʿān, from Abū ʿUthmān, from Usāma. I say: Al-Khaṭīb supplied this route with a connected chain in Sharaf Aṣḥāb al-Ḥadīth. Ibn ʿAdī included this hadith through many routes, all of them weak. In one place he said: Reliable transmitters related it from al-Walīd, from Muʿān, from Ibrāhīm, who said: “A trustworthy man among our companions related to us that the Messenger of God ﷺ …”

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن العذري تابعي أرسل حديثا فذكره بن منده وغيره في الصحابة قال روى الحسن بن عرفة حدثنا إسماعيل بن عياش عن معان بن رفاعة قال حدثني إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن العذري وكان من الصحابة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يحمل هذا العلم من كل خلف عدوله الحديث قال بن منده ولم يتابع بن عرفة على قوله وكان من الصحابة قلت قد رويناه في كتاب الغرر من الأخبار لوكيع القاضي قال حدثنا الحسن بن عرفة فذكره ولم يقل فيه وكان من الصحابة ثم أخرجه بن منده من طريق بقية عن معان عن إبراهيم قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأورده أبو نعيم ثم قال وهكذا رواه الوليد عن معان ورواه محمد بن سليمان بن أبي كريمة عن معان عن أبي عثمان عن أسامة قلت ووصل هذا الطريق الخطيب في شرف أصحاب الحديث وقد أورد بن عدي هذا الحديث من طرق كثيرة كلها ضعيفة وقال في بعض المواضع رواه الثقات عن الوليد عن معان عن إبراهيم قال حدثنا الثقة من أصحابنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكره

## Source unit 506 · printed entry 506

### English candidate

Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUbayd ibn Rifāʿa al-Zuraqī. ʿAbdān included him among the Companions and cited for him, through Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥumayd, from Ibn al-Munkadir, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUbayd ibn Rifāʿa, who said: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī prepared food and invited the Messenger of God ﷺ and his Companions—and the report follows. Abū Mūsā said: This has a disconnected chain. Then he transmitted it by another route from Ibn Abī Ḥumayd, which said: from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUbayd, from Abū Saʿīd. I say: Ibrāhīm also transmitted from his father, from his grandfather Rifāʿa, concerning Rifāʿa’s presence at Badr. Ibrāhīm was a young Successor. His father has no sound claim to Companionship; rather, it is said that he was born during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ.

## Source unit 516 · printed entry 516

### English candidate

Azhar ibn Qays. Al-Baghawī, Ibn Shāhīn, Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, and Abū Mūsā mentioned him among the Companions; Ibn al-Athīr and those after him followed them. This is an error that, to my knowledge, no one noticed. I shall cite their statements and explain the nature of the error. Al-Baghawī said: 'Azhar ibn Qays: Ziyād ibn Ayyūb related to me; Mubashshir ibn Ismāʿīl related to us, from Ḥarīz, from Abū al-Walīd Azhar ibn Qays, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to seek refuge in his prayer from the tribulation of the West. I know no other report from him.' Ibn Shāhīn said: 'Azhar ibn Qays, Abū al-Walīd: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Baghawī related to us,' and then cited it without adding anything. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: 'Azhar ibn Qays. Ḥarīz ibn ʿUthmān narrated from him; to my knowledge no one else narrated from him. His report from the Prophet ﷺ is that he used to seek refuge in his prayer from the tribulation of the West.' Abū Mūsā included him in the Supplement by way of Ibn Shāhīn and added nothing. When Ibn al-Athīr mentioned him, he confined himself to what Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr had included. The error thus overtook all of them. Its cause was that the isnad given by al-Baghawī lost the name of Azhar's father and the Companion's personal name, while the name of the Companion's father remained. The resulting biographical heading joined Azhar's given name to Qays, the surviving name of the Companion's father, and no such person existed in external reality. Ibn Shāhīn followed al-Baghawī, as did the rest who came after him, without scrutiny. To explain: Ḥarīz ibn ʿUthmān narrated the cited report only from Azhar ibn Rāshid—also said to be Ibn ʿAbd Allāh—al-Hawzanī, from ʿIṣma ibn Qays, from the Prophet ﷺ. Abū Zurʿa al-Dimashqī said: 'ʿAlī ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us; Ḥarīz ibn ʿUthmān related to us, from Abū al-Walīd Azhar al-Hawzanī, from ʿIṣma ibn Qays, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to seek refuge in God from the tribulation of the West.' Ibn Saʿd transmitted it from an unnamed informant, from Abū al-Yamān, from Ḥarīz. Al-Bukhārī likewise transmitted it in his Tārīkh from Abū al-Yamān. Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim, al-Ṭabarānī, and Abū Nuʿaym transmitted it by way of Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh, from Ḥarīz ibn ʿUthmān, from Azhar ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿIṣma ibn Qays. This becomes still clearer because, when al-Bukhārī and others gave the biography of Azhar al-Hawzanī, they identified him as one who narrated from ʿIṣma ibn Qays and from whom Ḥarīz ibn ʿUthmān narrated. Al-Bukhārī said: 'Azhar, Abū al-Walīd al-Hawzanī, narrated from ʿIṣma, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ; Ḥarīz narrated from him.' Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: 'Azhar ibn Rāshid, Abū al-Walīd al-Hawzanī, narrated from ʿIṣma ibn Qays, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ; he transmitted mursal reports from Ibn ʿAbbās and heard from Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir. Ḥarīz ibn ʿUthmān and others narrated from him.' Ibn Ḥibbān said in al-Thiqāt among the Successors: 'Azhar, Abū al-Walīd al-Hawzanī, narrates from a man among the Companions; Ḥarīz ibn ʿUthmān narrated from him.' This makes clear that no person named Azhar ibn Qays exists in external reality. What is remarkable is that Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr transmitted the cited report correctly in the biography of ʿIṣma ibn Qays, yet transmitted it here in its erroneous form. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr happened to call attention to an error close to this one among the kunyas, in the biography of Abū Khidāsh al-Sharʿabī, as will come, إن شاء الله تعالى. Here, however, the error overtook him and he did not point out the mistake of those who preceded him in mentioning this entry. God grants success.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

أزهر بن قيس ذكره البغوي وابن شاهين وابن عبد البر وأبو موسى في الصحابة وتبعهم بن الأثير ومن بعده وهو وهم لم يتنبه له أحد فيما علمت وسأذكر كلامهم وأبين وجه الخطأ فيه فقال البغوي أزهر بن قيس حدثني زياد بن أيوب حدثنا مبشر بن إسماعيل عن حريز عن أبي الوليد أزهر بن قيس صاحب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يتعوذ في صلاته من فتنة المغرب لا أعلم له غيره قال بن شاهين أزهر بن قيس أبو الوليد حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد البغوي فذكره ولم يزد شيئا وقال بن عبد البر أزهر بن قيس روى عنه حريز بن عثمان لم يرو عنه غيره فيما علمت حديثه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يتعوذ في صلاته من فتنة المغرب وأورده أبو موسى
