## Source unit 1030 · printed entry 1031

### English candidate

Jābir ibn ʿAtīk ibn Qays ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Haysha—the hāʾ bears fatḥa, followed by a yāʾ with sukūn and then a dotted letter—ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Umayya ibn Zayd ibn Muʿāwiya ibn Mālik ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf ibn Mālik ibn al-Aws al-Anṣārī. Thus Ibn al-Kalbī and Ibn Isḥāq gave his lineage, and they said that he attended Badr and the other campaigns. Mālik narrated in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jābir ibn ʿAtīk, from ʿAtīk ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAtīk—ʿAbd Allāh's maternal grandfather—that Jābir ibn ʿAtīk told him: the Messenger of God ﷺ came to visit ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thābit in his illness and found that he had been overcome. The Messenger of God ﷺ called out to him, but he did not answer. He recited the formula of return and said, 'We have been overcome concerning you, Abū al-Rabīʿ'—the report. Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasāʾī narrated it by way of Mālik. Al-Nasāʾī also narrated by way of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Jabr ibn ʿAtīk, that he entered with the Messenger of God ﷺ upon a deceased person and the women wept—the report. Ibn Mājah and others narrated a similar report by way of Abū Usāma and others, from Abū al-ʿUmays, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabr, from his father, from his grandfather. Al-Nasāʾī narrated it by way of Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn, from Abū al-ʿUmays, without saying 'from his grandfather.' Ibn Mandah narrated it by another route from Abū al-ʿUmays, saying: from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jābir ibn ʿAtīk, from his father, from his grandfather. There is much disagreement concerning it; Mālik's narration is the one relied upon. It is strengthened by what Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasāʾī narrated by way of Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from Ibn Jābir ibn ʿAtīk, from his father, traced to the Prophet: 'Some jealousy is hated by God'—the report. Its chain is sound. In al-Bukhārī's Tārīkh, by way of Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd, Abū Sufyān ibn Jābir ibn ʿAtīk related from his father that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say, 'Whoever appropriates the property of a Muslim man by his oath, God has forbidden him Paradise.' These reports show that his name was Jābir. The last report, however, was mentioned in the biography that follows, which is possible because his grandfather was not named. Al-Dimyāṭī held that his name was Jabr. Others, such as al-Baghawī, stated categorically that Jabr was his brother. Ibn Isḥāq and others stated categorically that Jabr ibn ʿAtīk attended Badr. Among the Companions there are two other men named Jābir ibn ʿAtīk. The first of them is:

## Source unit 1041 · printed entry 1042

### English candidate

Jāḥil, Abū Muslim al-Ṣadafī. Ibn Manda transmitted by way of Ibn Wahb: Abū al-Ashyam, the muezzin of the mosque of Damietta, related to us, from Sharāḥīl ibn Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn Jāḥil, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: ‘Those of my community who have most fully mastered this Qurʾān are its hypocrites.’ He said, ‘This is a strange report; we know it only by this route.’ Abū Nuʿaym mentioned him and said: ‘In my view he did not have Companionship, and none of the earlier or later scholars mentioned him.’ End. ## Source unit 1042 · printed entry 1043

### English candidate

Al-Jārūd ibn al-Muʿallā; he is also said to be Ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Muʿallā, and it is said al-Jārūd ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, as related by al-Tirmidhī. He was al-ʿAbdī, Abū al-Mundhir; he is also called Abū Ghiyāth—with ghayn and thāʾ, according to the sounder view—and Abū ʿAttāb. It is also said that his name was Bishr ibn Ḥanish, the latter name having an unpointed first letter, an open nūn, and a final pointed consonant. Ibn Isḥāq said: ‘Al-Jārūd ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥanish, who was a Christian, came to the Prophet ﷺ’; then he related a story and gave yet another form of his name. He was surnamed al-Jārūd because he raided Bakr ibn Wāʾil and extirpated them. The poet said:

We trampled them with cavalry from every side, / as al-Jārūd stripped Bakr ibn Wāʾil bare.

He was the chief of ʿAbd al-Qays. Ibn al-Sakan related another explanation for the surname: the lands of ʿAbd al-Qays suffered drought, and al-Jārūd still had a remnant of his camels. He took them to Banū Qudayd ibn Shaybān, his maternal uncles, and his maternal uncles’ camels contracted mange. The people said, ‘Bishr stripped them bare,’ so he was surnamed al-Jārūd; the poet then recited the verse just mentioned.

Al-Jārūd came in the year ten with the last delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays, and the Prophet ﷺ was pleased by his acceptance of Islam. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted by way of Zarbī ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Anas, who said: ‘When al-Jārūd came as a delegate to the Messenger of God ﷺ, he rejoiced in him, drew him near, and brought him close.’ Ibn Isḥāq said in al-Maghāzī: ‘His Islam was good, and he was steadfast in his religion.’ Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted by way of Ibn Sīrīn, from al-Jārūd, who said: ‘I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “I have a religion. If I leave my religion and enter yours, do I have a guarantee that God will not punish me?” He said, “Yes.”’ Al-Baghawī gave it at greater length.

Al-Jārūd was related by marriage to Abū Hurayra and was with him in Bahrain when ʿUmar sent him there, as will come in the biography of Qudāma ibn Maẓʿūn. He was killed in the land of Persia at ʿAqabat al-Ṭīn, which thereafter came to be called ʿAqabat al-Jārūd. This occurred in the year twenty-one, during the caliphate of ʿUmar. It is also said that he was killed at Nahāwand with al-Nuʿmān ibn Muqarrin, and it is said that he remained alive until the caliphate of ʿUthmān. Ibn Manda transmitted by way of Abū Bakr ibn Abī al-Aswad: ‘A man descended from al-Jārūd related to me that al-Jārūd was killed in the land of Persia during the caliphate of ʿUmar.’ Abū ʿUmar said that among his fine verses are:

I bear witness that God is true, and the daughters of my heart freely yielded / to the testimony and to rising up.
Convey from me a message to the Messenger of God: / that I am a ḥanīf wherever on earth I may be.
Though my home is not with you in Yathrib, / I am yours in settled residence and ease.
I make myself, before every calamity, / a shield for you; before your honor stands my honor.

His son al-Mundhir ibn al-Jārūd was one of the leaders of ʿAbd al-Qays in Basra. Al-Aʿshā al-Ḥarmāzī and others praised him. His grandson was al-Ḥakam ibn al-Mundhir, concerning whom this same al-Aʿshā said:

O al-Ḥakam ibn al-Mundhir ibn al-Jārūd, / the pavilion of glory is stretched above you.
You are the generous one, son of the praised generous one; / you grew in generosity and in the house of generosity.
A branch may grow from the root of a branch.

Al-Ḥajjāj used to envy al-Ḥakam on account of these verses.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

الجارود بن المعلى ويقال بن عمرو بن المعلى وقيل الجارود بن العلاء حكاه الترمذي العبدي أبو المنذر ويقال أبو غياث بمعجمة ومثلثة على الأصح وقيل بمهملة وموحدة ويقال اسمه بشر بن حنش بمهملة ونون مفتوحتين ثم معجمة وقال بن إسحاق قدم الجارود بن عمرو بن حنش وكان نصرانيا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكر قصة وقال في اسمه غير ذلك ولقب الجارود لأنه غزا بكر بن وائل فاستأصلهم قال الشاعر <br />
 فدسناهم بالخيل من كل جانب <br />
 كما جرد الجارود بكر بن وائل وكان سيد عبد القيس وحكى بن السكن أن سبب تلقيبه بذلك أن بلاد عبد القيس اجدبت وبقي للجارود بقية من إبله فتوجه بها إلى بني قديد بن شيبان وهم أخواله فجربت إبل أخواله فقال الناس جردهم بشر فلقب الجارود فقال الشاعر فذكره وقدم الجارود سنة عشر في وفد عبد القيس الأخير وسر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بإسلامه وروى الطبراني من طريق زربي بن عبد الله عن أنس قال لما قدم الجارود وافدا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فرح به وقربه وادناه وقال بن إسحاق في المغازي كان حسن الإسلام صليبا على دينه وروى الطبراني من طريق بن سيرين عن الجارود قال أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت إن لي دينا فلي إن تركت ديني ودخلت في دينك الا يعذبني الله قال نعم طوله البغوي وكان الجارود صهر أبي هريرة وكان معه بالبحرين لما أرسله عمر كما سيأتي في ترجمة قدامة بن مظعون وقتل بأرض فارس بعقبة الطين فصارت يقال له عقبة الجارود وذلك سنة إحدى وعشرين في خلافة عمر وقيل قتل بنهاوند مع النعمان بن مقرن وقيل بقي إلى خلافة عثمان روى بن منده من طريق أبي بكر بن أبي الأسود حدثني رجل من ولد الجارود قال قتل الجارود بأرض فارس في خلافة عمر قال أبو عمر من محاسن شعره <br />
 شهدت بأن الله حق وسامحت <br />
 بنات فؤادي بالشهادة والنهض <br />
 فأبلغ رسول الله عني رسالة <br />
 بأبي حنيف حيث كنت من الأرض <br />
 فإن لم تكن داري بيثرب فيكم <br />
 فإني لكم عند الإقامة والخفض <br />
 واجعل نفسي دون كل ملمة <br />
 لكم جنة من دون عرضكم عرضي وابنه المنذر بن الجارود كان من رؤساء عبد القيس بالبصرة مدحه الأعشى الحرمازي وغيره وحفيده الحكم بن المنذر وهو الذي يقول فيه الأعشى هذا أيضا <br />
 يا حكم بن المنذر بن الجارود <br />
 سرادق المجد عليك ممدود <br />
 أنت الجواد بن الجواد المحمود <br />
 نبت في الجود وفي بيت الجود <br />
 والعود قد ينبت في أصل العود <br />
 قال فكان الحجاج يحسد الحكم على هذه الأبيات

## Source unit 1043 · printed entry 1044

### English candidate

Al-Jārūd ibn al-Mundhir al-ʿAbdī, another man. Al-Bukhārī distinguished him from the preceding man in Kitāb al-Wuḥdān, according to Ibn Manda. Ibn Manda made this man the one from whom Ibn Sīrīn transmits. Al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān, al-Ṭabarānī, and others, however, transmitted Ibn Sīrīn’s report from al-Jārūd under the preceding biography. The correct view is that they are two men, because al-Jārūd ibn al-Mundhir remained alive long enough for al-Ḥasan and Ibn Sīrīn to receive from him, whereas Ibn al-Muʿallā died before that. Al-Mundhir is his kunyā, which was mistaken for his father’s name. والله أعلم.

Al-Ṭabarānī said that al-Aḥnaf called him his paternal uncle as a form of respect, for the two of them meet in no lineage closer than Saʿd ibn Zayd. Ibn Saʿd listed him among the Companions who settled in Basra. Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from his father that he had Companionship.

Aḥmad transmitted from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd and others, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from al-Aḥnaf, from Jāriya ibn Qudāma, who said: ‘I said, “O Messenger of God, counsel me, and be brief.” He said, “Do not become angry.”’ This report occurs with a short chain in Ibn Manda’s al-Maʿrifa. There is disagreement in the transmission from Hishām. Most of his associates transmitted it from him as just given, and Ibn Ḥibbān authenticated it by this route. Abū Muʿāwiya, Yaḥyā ibn Abī Zakariyyā al-Ghassānī, and Saʿīd ibn Yaḥyā al-Lakhmī transmitted it from Hishām and added: ‘from Jāriya, from his paternal uncle.’ Ibn Abī Shayba transmitted it from ʿAbda ibn Sulaymān, from Hishām, in the reverse form, saying: ‘from al-Aḥnaf, from a paternal uncle of his, from Jāriya.’ In a transmission of Abū Yaʿlā it occurs from Jāriya ibn Qudāma, from a paternal uncle of his father; then he related the report.

The first version is preferable. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it by way of Ibn Abī al-Zinād, from his father, from ʿUrwa, and by way of Muḥammad ibn Kurayb, from his father, who said: ‘I witnessed al-Aḥnaf transmitting from his paternal uncle Jāriya’; and his paternal uncle was Jāriya ibn Qudāma. A separate report from Ibn ʿAbbās has the wording: ‘O Messenger of God, tell me a saying that will benefit me, and be brief’—the report.

Abū ʿUmar said: He was one of ʿAlī’s companions in his wars. He was the man who burned ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥaḍramī in the house of Sunayd in Basra. Muʿāwiya had sent to al-Ḥaḍramī, instructing him to take Basra on his behalf. ʿAlī sent Aʿyan ibn Ḍubayʿa against him, but Aʿyan was killed. He then sent Jāriya ibn Qudāma, who besieged Ibn al-Ḥaḍramī and afterward burned the building over him. It is also said that he is Juwayriya ibn Qudāma, who transmitted from his paternal uncle in al-Bukhārī.

This Jāriya also has a story with Muʿāwiya in which Muʿāwiya said to him, ‘Ask for what you need, O Abū Qundus.’ He replied, ‘Leave the people in their homes and do not summon them to come to you. Only the rich are sent to you, while the poor are left behind.’

## Source unit 1052 · printed entry 1053

### English candidate

Jāhima ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās al-Sulamī. Ibn Mājah gave this lineage in al-Sunan. Ibn al-Sakan said that he was also called the son of al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās. Ibn Saʿd placed him in the generation of those who attended the Trench and said that he accepted Islam and had companionship. Al-Baghawī, Ibn Abī Khaythama, and al-Ṭabarānī narrated by way of Sufyān ibn Ḥabīb, from Ibn Jurayj, from Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa ibn Yazīd ibn Rukāna, from Muʿāwiya ibn Jāhima al-Sulamī, from his father, who said: 'I came to the Prophet ﷺ to consult him about fighting in the path of God. He asked, Do you have a mother? I said, Yes. He said, Stay with her.' The routes from Ibn Jurayj differ. Sufyān ibn Ḥabīb transmitted it well, but dropped Ṭalḥa from the chain, according to al-Baghawī. A similar route is reported from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān, from Ibn Jurayj. Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī narrated from Ibn Jurayj, from Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa ibn Yazīd ibn Rukāna, from his father, from Muʿāwiya ibn Jāhima, who said, 'I came to the Prophet ﷺ.' Al-Baghawī transmitted it from Shurayḥ ibn Yūnus, from al-Umawī. He then narrated by way of Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Jurayj, who differed over Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa's lineage, saying: from Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father Ṭalḥa, from Muʿāwiya ibn Jāhima, that Jāhima came to the Prophet ﷺ; he then mentioned the report. Al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah likewise transmitted it by way of Ḥajjāj. Al-Bayhaqī said that Ḥajjāj's recension is sounder; Abū ʿĀṣim corroborated him, and that route appears in Ibn Shāhīn's biography of Muʿāwiya ibn Jāhima. I say: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal narrated from Rawḥ ibn ʿUbāda in agreement with Ḥajjāj. Ibn Mājah narrated by way of Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who said: from Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr. He agreed with Ḥajjāj but omitted ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭalḥa. Ibn Shāhīn transmitted it in Muʿāwiya ibn Jāhima's biography from Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd, from Ibn Isḥāq, and included him; Muḥammad ibn Salama al-Khuzāʿī corroborated him from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq. This is Ibn Isḥāq's well-known recension. It is also reported from Ibn Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn Ṭalḥa, from Muʿāwiya al-Sulamī. Ibn Luhayʿa narrated from Yūnus ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Isḥāq with this chain, but altered the Companion's name and affiliation to Jahm al-Aslamī. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sulaymān narrated from Ibn Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa, from his father Ṭalḥa ibn Muʿāwiya ibn Jāhima, who said, 'I came to the Prophet ﷺ.' This is an error produced by scribal corruption and reversal. The correct route is Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa, from Muʿāwiya ibn Jāhima, from his father: the word ʿan was corrupted into ibn and 'from his father' was moved forward. This made Ṭalḥa appear to have companionship, although there is no kinship between him and Muʿāwiya ibn Jāhima. Were the chain taken literally, four successive generations would have companionship with the Prophet ﷺ: Ṭalḥa ibn Muʿāwiya ibn Jāhima ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās. Al-Ṭabarānī also narrated by way of Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb, from Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, from Muʿāwiya ibn Dirham, that Dirham came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, 'I have come to consult you about going on campaign.' He asked, 'Do you have a mother?' He replied, 'Yes.' He said, 'Then stay with her.' This is the very story of Jāhima. If Jāhima was corrupted into Dirham and an error occurred in Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa's grandfather's name, it is the same report; otherwise, it is another occurrence involving another man.

## Source unit 1055 · printed entry 1056

### English candidate

Jabbār ibn Sulmā—the sīn bears ḍamma, though fatḥa is also reported—ibn Mālik ibn Jaʿfar ibn Kilāb ibn Rabīʿa ibn ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa al-Kilābī. His father was called Nazzāl al-Maḍīq. Abū Saʿd mentioned that he came to the Prophet ﷺ with ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl while still a polytheist. He was later the man who killed ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra. In Ibn Isḥāq's al-Maghāzī, a descendant of Jabbār ibn Sulmā said that Jabbār was among those present that day with ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl—meaning at Biʾr Maʿūna—and later accepted Islam. Al-Wāqidī said that he accepted Islam at the hands of al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Sufyān al-Kilābī. Al-Wāqidī also narrated from Mūsā ibn Shayba, from Khārija, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik: the delegation of Banū Kilāb arrived, thirteen men including Labīd ibn Rabīʿa, and lodged in the house of Ramla bint al-Ḥārith. Jabbār ibn Sulmā and Kaʿb ibn Mālik were companions. Kaʿb came, welcomed them, honored Jabbār, and accompanied them to the Prophet ﷺ; the source then mentions the story. Ibn Isḥāq, al-Wāqidī, and others narrated that Jabbār ibn Sulmā stabbed ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra that day. ʿĀmir said, 'I have triumphed, by the Lord of the Kaʿba,' rose off Jabbār's spear, and his body was not found. Because of that, Jabbār accepted Islam, and his Islam became excellent. Ibn al-Kalbī related that Jabbār was said to be a better horseman than ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl.

## Source unit 1056 · printed entry 1057

### English candidate

Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr ibn Umayya ibn Khansāʾ ibn Sinān ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿAdī ibn Ghanm ibn Kaʿb ibn Salama al-Anṣārī, then al-Sulamī, known as Abū ʿAbd Allāh. Mūsā ibn ʿUqba, from Ibn Shihāb, mentioned him among the people of al-ʿAqaba; Abū al-Aswad, from ʿUrwa, mentioned him among the people of Badr. Al-Ṭabarānī narrated by way of Ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn Ḥazm: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa assessed their produce for only one year, then was killed at Muʾta; thereafter the Messenger of God ﷺ used to send Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr to assess it for the people of Khaybar. In Ibn Isḥāq's al-Maghāzī, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maknaf, from Ḥāritha: when ʿUmar expelled the Jews of Khaybar, he rode out among the Emigrants and Anṣār; Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr accompanied him and was the assessor and accountant of the people of Medina. Muslim narrated by way of ʿUbāda ibn al-Walīd, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, that he was with the Messenger of God ﷺ on a campaign. In the report he asked, 'Who will go ahead of us, plaster the watering trough for us, drink, and give us water?' Jābir said, 'I will.' He asked, 'Who will accompany Jābir?' Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr stood and said, 'I will, O Messenger of God'—the report. Aḥmad, al-Baghawī, and others narrated a similar report by way of Ibn Abī Uways, from Shuraḥbīl ibn Saʿd, from Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr. Al-Baghawī said: I know of no other report from him. I say: rather, he has another. Ibn Shāhīn, Ibn al-Sakan, and others narrated by way of Zuhayr ibn Muḥammad, from Shuraḥbīl, who heard Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr say: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say, 'We have been forbidden to see one another's private parts.' Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Yaḥyā corroborated it from Sharāḥīl; Ibn Mandah transmitted it. Ibn al-Sakan and others said Jabbār died in 30 during ʿUthmān's caliphate. Abū Nuʿaym added that he was sixty-two years old.

## Source unit 1067 · printed entry 1068

## Source unit 1069 · printed entry 1070

### English candidate

Jabr, a client of Banū ʿAbd al-Dār. Al-Wāqidī mentioned that he was in Mecca and was Jewish. He heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting Sūrat Yūsuf, accepted Islam, and concealed his conversion. His masters then discovered it and tortured him. When the Messenger of God ﷺ conquered Mecca, Jabr complained to him of what he had suffered. He gave Jabr his price, whereupon Jabr purchased himself, became free, attained independence, and married a woman of high standing among Banū ʿĀmir. Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān related in his Tafsīr that Jabr was one of those concerning whom the verse was revealed, 'except one who is compelled while his heart is secure in faith,' and one of those concerning whom 'We have made some of you a trial for others' was revealed. Al-Ṭabarī transmitted, in his commentary on the saying of God Most High, 'Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God or says, Revelation has come to me,' by way of al-Suddī: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ accepted Islam, then apostatized, joined the polytheists, and informed against ʿAmmār and Jabr, a slave of al-Ḥaḍramī or of Banū ʿAbd al-Dār. They seized and tortured the two until they uttered unbelief; then the verse 'except one who is compelled while his heart is secure in faith' was revealed. In the Tafsīrs of Ibn Abī Ḥātim and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, by way of Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim al-Ḥaḍramī, he said: 'We had two slaves, one called Yasār and the other Jabr. They were sword polishers, read their scripture, and practiced their trade. The Messenger of God ﷺ used to pass by them and listen to their reading. People said, He is only learning from the two of them. Then the verse was revealed, We certainly know that they say: It is only a human being who teaches him.' That recension does not mention that they accepted Islam. By way of Qatāda, the verse was revealed concerning a slave of al-Ḥaḍramī called Yuḥannas, who will appear later. Ibn Fatḥūn added Jabr to the biographical corpus.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

جبر مولى بني عبد الدار ذكر الواقدي أنه كان بمكة وكان يهوديا فسمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ سورة يوسف فأسلم وكتم إسلامه ثم اطلع مواليه على ذلك فعذبوه فلما فتح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مكة شكا إليه مالقي فأعطاه ثمنه فاشترى نفسه وعتق واستغنى وتزوج امرأة ذات شرف في بني عامر وحكى مقاتل بن حبان في تفسيره أنه أحد من نزل فيه الا من أكره وقبله مطمئن بالإيمان وأنه أحد من نزل فيه @QB@ وجعلنا بعضكم لبعض فتنة @QE@ وأخرج الطبري في تفسير قوله تعالى @QB@ ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو قال أوحي إلي @QE@ من طريق السدي أن عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح أسلم ثم ارتد فلحق بالمشركين ووشى بعمار وجبر عبد بن الحضرمي أو بن عبد الدار فاخذوهما وعذبوهما حتى كفرا فنزلت الا من الحره وقبله مطمئن بالإيمان وفي تفسير بن أبي حاتم وعبد بن حميد من طريق حصين بن عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن مسلم الحضرمي قال كان لنا عبدان أحدهما يقال له يسار والآخر يقال له جبر وكانا صيقليين فكانا يقرآن كتابهما ويعملان عملهما وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يمر بهما فيسمع قراءتهما فقالوا إنما يتعلم منهما فنزلت ولقد نعلم أنهم يقولون إنما يعلمه بشر ولم يذكر أنهما اسلما ومن طريق قتادة أنها نزلت في عبد بن الحضرمي يقال له يحنس وسيأتي واستدركه بن فتحون

## Source unit 1071 · printed entry 1072

### English candidate

Jabal—with fatḥa on the jīm and the single-dotted letter—ibn Jawwāl ibn Ṣafwān ibn Bilāl ibn Aṣram ibn Iyās ibn ʿAbd Ghanm ibn Jaḥḥāsh ibn Bajāla ibn Māzin ibn Thaʿlaba ibn Saʿd ibn Dhubyān, the Dhubyānī poet, then the Thaʿlabī. Al-Dāraquṭnī said in al-Muʾtalif: “He had Companionship.” Hishām ibn al-Kalbī said: “He was a Jew among the Banū Qurayẓa, then accepted Islam.” He elegized Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab in verses that include:
“By your life, Ibn Akhṭab did not reproach himself; / rather, whomever God forsakes is forsaken.”
Ibn Isḥāq likewise assigned the verses to him in al-Maghāzī, but said: “Some people say that they are by Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab himself.” Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām mentioned that he was descended from al-Fiṭyawn ibn ʿĀmir ibn Thaʿlaba. Al-Marzubānī said in Muʿjam al-Shuʿarāʾ: “He was a Jew and accepted Islam. He is the one who said when the Prophet ﷺ conquered Khaybar:
‘Niṭāh was struck by a battalion from the Prophet, / dust-grey, broad-shouldered and strong-backed.’”
In the recension of the Dīwān of Ḥassān ibn Thābit prepared by Abū Saʿīd al-Sukkarī, from Ibn Ḥabīb, it says: “Ḥassān ibn Thābit said in answer to Jabal ibn Jawwāl al-Thaʿlabī, who had been a Jew and accepted Islam, after his saying:
‘Ah, Saʿd, delight of the Banū Muʿādh, / for what you did to Qurayẓa and al-Naḍīr!
You left your cooking pot with nothing in it, / while the people’s pot is hot and boiling.’
Ḥassān said:
‘Gone is a band that gave Quraysh aid; / in their own town they have no helper.
They were given the Book but squandered it; / blind to the Torah, they are ruined.
You disbelieved in the Qurʾan, though you were brought / confirmation of what the warner said.
A spreading blaze at al-Buwayra would be a light matter / to the nobles of the Banū Luʾayy.’”
And the verses continue. Al-Marzubānī cited for Jabal the verses already mentioned and added:
“But there is no abiding when deaths come: / they snatch away, then the graves enfold them.
As though they were spoils on a feast day, / slaughtered with no one to protest for them.”

## Source unit 1072 · printed entry 1073

## Source unit 1084 · printed entry 1085

### English candidate

Jabala, without a lineage. Al-Bukhārī said: “He had Companionship. Ibn Sīrīn transmitted from him in disconnected form. I think he is the first man”—meaning Jabala ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī. Ibn al-Sakan said: “He is said to have had Companionship, but he has no narration from the Prophet ﷺ.” In a suspended report in al-Bukhārī, Ibn Sīrīn said: “There is no harm in it”—meaning simultaneously marrying a man’s former wife and his daughter by another woman. Al-Baghawī and Ibn al-Sakan connected it, by way of Ḥammād, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: “In one of the provincial cities there was a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ called Jabala. He simultaneously married a man’s former wife and his daughter by another woman.” Ayyūb said: “Al-Ḥasan disliked it.” Ibn Mandah said: “This is how ʿAffān and others transmitted it. Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb transmitted it from Ḥammād but said Jabbār. The first is more correct.” I say: Ibn ʿUlayya likewise transmitted it as Jabala from Ayyūb; Ibn Abī Shayba transmitted it from him. ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Thaqafī also transmitted from Ayyūb: “I was informed that Saʿd ibn Qurḥāʾa, a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ,” and he related a similar report.

## Source unit 1085 · printed entry 1086

### English candidate

Jubayb—with a jīm and two bāʾs, in the diminutive—ibn al-Ḥārith. Ibn al-Sakan mentioned him and said that the chain of his hadith is not sound. He and al-Ṭabarānī transmitted, by way of Nūḥ ibn Dhakwān, from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha: Jubayb ibn al-Ḥārith came and said, “Messenger of God, I am a man much given to committing sins.” He said, “Then repent to الله عز وجل (God, Mighty and Majestic)”; and the report continues. Ibn Mandah said: “It is singular; we know it only through this route.” Al-Ṭabarānī said in al-Awsaṭ: “It is not transmitted from Hishām except through this chain. ʿĪsā alone transmitted it from Ibrāhīm, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Nūḥ, from him.” ʿAbd al-Ghanī ibn Saʿīd mentioned in al-Muʾtalif that Ayyūb ibn Dhakwān transmitted it from Hishām. I say: Ayyūb and Nūḥ are both weak, and it is possible that one of the transmitters altered Nūḥ into Ayyūb. Al-Bayhaqī noted in al-Shuʿab that some transmitted it as Jubayr ibn al-Ḥārith, with an rāʾ, and said that this is an error. Ibn Shāhīn misread it with a dotted khāʾ and placed it there; Abū Mūsā corrected him. Jubayb will also be mentioned in the notice of Abū al-Ghādiya.

## Source unit 1089 · printed entry 1090

### English candidate

Jubayr ibn al-Ḥuwayrith ibn Nuqayd ibn Bujayr ibn ʿAbd ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb al-Qurashī. Al-Zubayr said that his father was killed on the day of the Conquest. ## Source unit 1090 · printed entry 1091

### English candidate

Jubayr ibn Ḥayya—with fatḥa on the undotted ḥāʾ and a doubled yāʾ—ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī, cousin of al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba and nephew of ʿUrwa ibn Masʿūd. I say: It is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī that he witnessed the conquests during ʿUmar’s reign. Al-Bukhārī transmitted the report to that effect through Zāʾida ibn Ziyād ibn Jubayr, from him. I have not seen anyone include Jubayr among the Companions, although he meets their criterion: among the Thaqīf who were alive in the Prophet’s ﷺ time, none remained without accepting Islam and witnessing the Farewell Pilgrimage. Abū Mūsā included him among the Companions and transmitted a hadith for him, yet claimed that it was disconnected and declared him a Follower. In my view his Companionship cannot be dismissed. Anyone who witnessed the conquests in ʿUmar’s reign must have been a man at that time, and the event he witnessed occurred fewer than ten years after the Prophet’s death. At the very least, therefore, he would have seen him. Jubayr lived in al-Ṭāʾif and was a teacher in a kuttāb. He then came to Iraq, settled as a clerk in the register, and was later appointed by Ziyād over Iṣfahān. His standing became great during the caliphate of ʿAbd al-Malik.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

جبير بن حية بفتح المهملة وتشديد التحتانية بن مسعود الثقفي بن عم المغيرة بن شعبة وابن أخي عروة بن مسعود قلت ثبت في صحيح البخاري أنه شهد الفتوح في عهد عمر وأخرج البخاري الحديث بذلك من رواية زائدة بن زياد بن جبير عنه ولم أر من ذكر جبيرا في الصحابة وهو من شرطهم لأن ثقيفا لم يبق منهم في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ممن كان موجودا أحد إلا أسلم وشهد حجة الوداع وقد ذكره أبو موسى في الصحابة وأخرج له حديثا وزعم أنه مرسل وصحح أنه تابعي وليست صحبته عندي بمندفعه فمن يشهد الفتوح في عهد عمر لا بد أن يكون إذ ذلك رجلا والقصة التي شهدها كانت بعد الوفاة النبوية بدون عشر سنين فأقل أحواله أن يكون له رؤية وكان المذكور يسكن الطائف وكان مقم كتاب ثم قدم العراق فاستقر كاتبا في الديوان ثم ولاه زياد أصبهان وعظم شأنه في خلافة عبد الملك

## Source unit 1092 · printed entry 1093

### English candidate

Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim ibn ʿAdī ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manāf al-Qurashī al-Nawfalī. His mother was Umm Ḥabīb bint Saʿīd; it is also said that she was Umm Jamīl bint Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qays, of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy. He was one of the leading men and scholars of genealogy. He came to the Prophet ﷺ concerning the ransom of the captives of Badr and heard him reciting al-Ṭūr. He said: “That was the first moment faith entered my heart.” Al-Bukhārī transmitted this in the Ṣaḥīḥ. The Prophet ﷺ—and peace be upon his family—said to him: “Had your father been alive and spoken to me about them, I would have given them to him.” Jubayr accepted Islam between al-Ḥudaybiya and the Conquest; it is also said that he did so at the Conquest. Al-Baghawī said that he accepted Islam before the conquest of Mecca and died during Muʿāwiya’s caliphate. Ibn Isḥāq said: Yaʿqūb ibn ʿUtba informed me, from an elder of the Anṣār, that when ʿUmar was brought al-Nuʿmān’s genealogy, he summoned Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, who knew the genealogies of Quraysh—and indeed of all the Arabs—better than anyone. He said: Jubayr said, “I learned genealogy from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, and Abū Bakr knew Arab genealogy better than anyone.” Among the Companions, Sulaymān ibn Ṣurad and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar transmitted from him. Ibn al-Musayyib transmitted from him that he and ʿUthmān came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him to grant them shares as he had granted shares to Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib. They said, “Our kinship is one”—meaning that Hāshim, al-Muṭṭalib, Nawfal, Jubayr’s grandfather, and ʿAbd Shams, ʿUthmān’s grandfather, were brothers. He refused and said: “Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib are one.” Jubayr died in the year fifty-seven, fifty-eight, or fifty-nine.

## Source unit 1109 · printed entry 1110

### English candidate

Jidār—with a kasra on the first letter and an ungeminated dāl. Al-Baghawī, Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim, and others transmitted, by way of al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Faḍl ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Anṣārī, from al-Zuhrī, from Yazīd ibn Shajara, from Jidār, who said: We went on campaign with the Messenger of God ﷺ. We met our enemy, and he stood, praised God, and extolled Him. Then he said, “People, you have come to morning while blessings from God surround you, amid green, yellow, and red, and with whatever the houses contain.” He then related the sermon at length. Ibn Mandah said: “It is singular.” Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād transmitted the full report from Mujāhid, from Yazīd ibn Shajara, without mentioning Jidār. Manṣūr likewise transmitted it from Yazīd, but as a stopped report. I say: al-Aʿmash corroborated him in stopping it, from Mujāhid. Al-ʿAbbās is extremely weak. ʿAbbās al-Dūrī related from Ibn Maʿīn concerning Yazīd ibn Shajara: “He had Companionship.” As for the report of Jidār, it is not sound, and we know of no narration by al-Zuhrī from Yazīd ibn Shajara. The report is Manṣūr’s report. Al-Baghawī said something similar and added that al-Zuhrī did not hear from Yazīd. Ibn al-Jawzī related from al-Nasāʾī: “This report is false.” Al-Dāraquṭnī said: “It is not preserved; what is correct is the version of Manṣūr and al-Aʿmash.” He said this in al-ʿIlal.

Judjud—with two jīms bearing ḍamma, separated by an unpointed, quiescent dāl—is al-Jundaʿī. Al-Bayhaqī mentioned him in al-Dalāʾil, in a report of ʿAbd al-Razzāq from a man, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: A man came to some of the Anṣār and said, “The Messenger of God ﷺ has sent me to you and married me to so-and-so.” The Prophet ﷺ sent ʿAlī and al-Miqdād, saying, “Kill him, though I do not think you will catch him.” They found that he had died from a bite. Al-Bayhaqī said: “This man is named, in the report of ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, as Judjud al-Jundaʿī.” I say: In Ibn Mandah’s version, by way of Yaḥyā ibn Bisṭām, from ʿAmr ibn Farqad, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, it reads “Jurayḥ al-Jundaʿī”; he then related the story. ## Source unit 1111 · printed entry 1112

### English candidate

Al-Jadd ibn Qays ibn Ṣakhr ibn Khansāʾ ibn Sinān ibn ʿUbayd ibn Ghanm ibn Kaʿb ibn Salima al-Anṣārī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh. Al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn Mandah transmitted, by way of Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmmār al-Duhnī, from his father, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir, who said: “My maternal uncle al-Jadd ibn Qays carried me—I was not able to throw a stone—among the seventy mounted men of the Anṣār who came as a delegation to the Messenger of God ﷺ.” He then related the report about the pledge at al-ʿAqaba. Its chain is strong. Ibn Mandah said: “It is singular among the reports of Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmmār; Muḥammad ibn ʿImrān ibn Abī Laylā alone transmitted it.” Al-Jadd ibn Qays was chief of the Banū Salima, as will come in the notice of ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ. It is said that al-Jadd ibn Qays was a hypocrite. Abū Nuʿaym and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, by way of al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās, that concerning him was revealed God’s saying, “Among them is one who says, ‘Give me leave, and do not put me to trial’” [Qurʾan 9:49]. Ibn Mardawayh also transmitted it from ʿĀʾisha with a weak chain, from Jābir with a chain containing an unnamed person, and from Jābir that al-Jadd stayed behind at the pledge on the day of al-Ḥudaybiya. Ibn ʿAsākir transmitted this by way of al-Aʿmash, from Abū Sufyān, from him. ʿAbd al-Razzāq related from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, concerning God’s saying, “They mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. Perhaps God will turn to them in mercy” [Qurʾan 9:102]: “It was revealed concerning a group of those who stayed behind from Tabūk, among them Abū Lubāba and al-Jadd ibn Qays; then mercy was turned to them.” Abū ʿUmar said at the end of his notice: “It is said that he repented and that his repentance was good.” He died during the caliphate of ʿUthmān.

## Source unit 1120 · printed entry 1121

Jarād al-ʿUqaylī, father of ʿAbd Allāh. ## Source unit 1124 · printed entry 1125

### English candidate

Jarmūz al-Hujaymī. Abū Ḥātim said: Jarmūz al-Qurayʿī al-Baṣrī; he had Companionship. Ibn Qāniʿ supplied his genealogy, saying: Jarmūz ibn Aws ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jarīr ibn ʿAmr ibn Anmār ibn al-Hujaym ibn ʿAmr ibn Tamīm. Ibn al-Sakan said: “He had Companionship; his report is among the reports of the Baṣrans.” Al-Bukhārī transmitted in his History, by way of Abū ʿĀmir al-ʿAqadī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Hawdha al-Qurayʿī, who said: “A man of the Banū al-Hujaym related to me, from Jarmūz.” Aḥmad and others transmitted it by way of ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAbd al-Wārith, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Hawdha, from a man who heard Jarmūz al-Hujaymī say: “I said, ‘Messenger of God, counsel me.’ He said, ‘I counsel you not to be given to cursing.’” Ibn al-Sakan transmitted it by way of Muslim ibn Qutayba: “ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Hawdha related to us—I saw him in his cradle because of old age—who said, ‘Jarmūz related to me,’” and he related the report. On this account, perhaps ʿUbayd Allāh first heard it from him through an intermediary and later heard it directly from him. Al-Baghawī and Ibn al-Sakan declared that the unnamed man in the first version was Abū Tamīma al-Hujaymī. Ibn Mandah said that his son al-Ḥārith ibn Jarmūz also transmitted from him. Ibn Abī Ḥātim likewise related this from his father.

## Source unit 1132 · printed entry 1133

### English candidate

Jarhad ibn Khuwaylid ibn Bajra ibn ʿAbd Yālīl ibn Zurʿa ibn Razāḥ ibn ʿAdī ibn Sahm ibn Tamīm ibn Māzin ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Salāmān ibn Aslam ibn Afṣā, al-Aslamī. He was one of the People of the Ṣuffa and had the kunya Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. He is also said to have been a nobleman. Hadiths were transmitted from him, among them his well-known report that the thigh is nakedness. There is extensive disagreement over its chain, and Ibn Ḥibbān graded it sound. Ibn Ḥibbān said that he was counted among the people of Basra, while others said among the people of Medina, which is correct. Ibn al-Sakan transmitted by way of Iyās ibn Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ: ‘Muslim ibn Jarhad related to me, from a paternal cousin of mine, from his father, who had witnessed al-Ḥudaybiya,’ and he mentioned a hadith. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted by way of Zurʿa ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jarhad, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Prophet ﷺ sat beside him; he was one of the Companions of the Ṣuffa. He also transmitted by way of Sufyān ibn Farwa, from one of the descendants of Jarhad, from Jarhad, that Jarhad ate with his left hand. The Prophet ﷺ told him, ‘Eat with the right.’ He said, ‘It is injured.’ He spat upon it, and Jarhad never complained of it until he died. Al-Wāqidī said: He had a house in Medina and died there near the end of Yazīd’s caliphate.

## Source unit 1137 · printed entry 1138

### English candidate

Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jābir ibn Mālik ibn Naḍr ibn Thaʿlaba ibn Jusham ibn ʿAwf ibn Ḥuzayma ibn Ḥarb ibn ʿAlī al-Bajalī, the famous Companion. He had the kunya Abū ʿAmr, and it is also said Abū ʿAbd Allāh. There is disagreement about when he embraced Islam. In al-Ṭabarānī’s al-Awsaṭ, through Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿUmar al-Aḥmasī, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, from Jarīr, he said: ‘When the Prophet ﷺ was sent, I came to him. He asked, “What brought you?” I said, “I have come to embrace Islam.” He cast his cloak to me and said, “When a nobleman of a people comes to you, honor him.”’ Ḥuṣayn has weakness. Were this sound, it would be understood figuratively—‘when news of the Prophet’s mission ﷺ reached us’—or as an ellipsis: ‘when the Prophet ﷺ was sent, then called to God, then came to Medina, then fought Quraysh and others, then conquered Mecca, and then the delegations came to him.’ Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr stated decisively on Jarīr’s authority that he embraced Islam forty days before the death of the Prophet ﷺ, which is an error. In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, Jarīr reports that the Prophet ﷺ told him, ‘Ask the people to be silent,’ during the Farewell Pilgrimage. Al-Wāqidī stated decisively that he came in delegation to the Prophet ﷺ in Ramaḍān of the year ten; that the Prophet’s dispatching him to Dhū al-Khalaṣa occurred afterward; and that he joined the Prophet ﷺ for the Farewell Pilgrimage that same year. In my view this is questionable, because Sharīk related from al-Shaybānī, from al-Shaʿbī, from Jarīr, who said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ told us, “Your brother the Negus has died,”’ and the report continues. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it. This indicates that Jarīr embraced Islam before the year ten, because the Negus died before then. Jarīr was handsome. ʿUmar said, ‘He is the Joseph of this community.’ ʿUmar placed him over all Bajīla in the wars of Iraq, and they had a major part in the conquest of al-Qādisiyya. Jarīr then settled in Kufa. ʿAlī sent him as an envoy to Muʿāwiya; he subsequently withdrew from both parties and lived in Qarqīsiyā until he died in the year fifty-one—or, it is said, fifty-four. In an authentic report, the Prophet ﷺ sent him to Dhū al-Khalaṣa and he destroyed it. Also authentically reported from him is his statement: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ never screened me out from the time I embraced Islam, and whenever he saw me he smiled.’ Al-Baghawī transmitted, by way of Qays, from Jarīr: ‘ʿUmar saw me unclothed and said, “I do not think anyone among the people has been formed in this likeness except what has been mentioned of Joseph.”’ By way of Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl al-Kuhaylī, he said that Jarīr was six cubits tall. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted from a marfūʿ report of ʿAlī: ‘Jarīr is one of us, the People of the House.’ Among the Companions, Anas ibn Mālik narrated from him and said, ‘Jarīr used to serve me, though he was older than I.’ The two Shaykhs transmitted it.

جرير بن عبد الله بن جابر بن مالك بن نضر بن ثعلبة بن جشم بن عوف بن حزيمة بن حرب بن علي البجلي الصحابي الشهير يكنى أبا عمرو وقيل يكنى أبا عبد الله اختلف في وقت إسلامه ففي الطبراني الأوسط من طريق حصين بن عمر الأحمسي عن إسماعيل بن أبي خالد عن قيس بن أبي حازم عن جرير قال لما بعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أتيته فقال ما جاء بك قلت جئت لأسلم فألقى إلي كساءه وقال إذا أتاكم كريم قوم فأكرموه حصين فيه ضعف ولو صح لحمل على المجاز أي لما بلغنا خبر بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو على الحذف أي لما بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم دعا إلى الله ثم قدم المدينة ثم حارب قريشا وغيرهم ثم فتح مكة ثم وفدت عليه الوفود وجزم بن عبد البر عنه بأنه أسلم قبل وفاة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأربعين يوما وهو غلط ففي الصحيحين عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له استنصت الناس في حجة الوداع وجزم الواقدي بأنه وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في شهر رمضان سنة عشر وأن بعثه إلى ذي الخلصة كان بعد ذلك وأنه وافي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حجة الوداع من عامه وفيه عندي نظر لأن شريكا حدث عن الشيباني عن الشعبي عن جرير قال قال لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن أخاكم النجاشي قد مات الحديث أخرجه الطبراني فهذا يدل على أن إسلام جرير كان قبل سنة عشر لأن النجاشي مات قبل ذلك وكان جرير جميلا قال عمر هو يوسف هذه الأمة وقدمه عمر في حروب العراق على جميع بجيلة وكان لهم أثر عظيم في فتح القادسية ثم سكن جرير الكوفة وأرسله علي رسولا إلى معاوية ثم اعتزل الفريقين وسكن قرقيسيا حتى مات سنة إحدى وقيل أربع وخمسين وفي الصحيح أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم بعثه إلى ذي الخلصة فهدمها وفيه عنه قال ما حجبني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم منذ أسلمت ولا رآني إلا تبسم وروى البغوي من طريق قيس عن جرير قال رآني عمر متجردا فقال ما أرى أحدا من الناس صور صورة هذا إلا ما ذكر من يوسف ومن طريق إبراهيم بن إسماعيل الكهيلي قال كان طول جرير ستة أذرع وروى الطبراني من حديث علي مرفوعا جرير منا أهل البيت وروى عنه من الصحابة أنس بن مالك قال كان جرير يخدمني وهو أكبر مني أخرجه الشيخان

## Source unit 1144 · printed entry 1145

### English candidate

Juzʾ ibn al-Ḥadirjān ibn Mālik al-Yamānī. Ibn Mandah transmitted by way of Hāshim ibn Muḥammad ibn Hāshim ibn Juzʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Juzʾ ibn al-Ḥadirjān ibn Mālik, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: ‘My father Juzʾ ibn al-Ḥadirjān related to me’—he was one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—‘and said: My brother Qadād ibn al-Ḥadirjān came in delegation to the Messenger of God ﷺ from Yemen with his own faith and the faith of those of his household who obeyed him. At that time they were six hundred households among those who obeyed al-Ḥadirjān and believed in Muḥammad ﷺ. A patrol of the Prophet ﷺ encountered them. Qadād told them, “I am a believer,” but they did not accept this from him and killed him. When that reached me, I went to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and [the verse] was revealed: “O you who believe, when you go forth in the path of God, verify” [Q 4:94]. The Prophet ﷺ gave me my brother’s blood money: one hundred red she-camels. I raided Ṭayyiʾ, obtained spoils from them, and took forty women captive. I brought them to Medina, and the Messenger of God ﷺ married them to his Companions.’ This is an unknown chain. Ibn Mākūlā has ‘Juzʾ ibn al-Ḥudrad; he had Companionship,’ and Ibn al-Amīn likewise added him. Perhaps this is the same man, with disagreement over his father’s name. In Ibn al-Kalbī’s Jamharat al-Nasab, in the genealogy of al-Azd, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Juzʾ ibn al-Ḥadirjān is said to have been a nobleman in Syria and to have held office in the time of al-Ḥajjāj.

## Source unit 1151 · printed entry 1152

### English candidate

Juzʾ, without a lineage. Ibn Mandah said that he was counted among the people of Syria. ## Source unit 1156 · printed entry 1157

### English candidate

Jaʿāl ibn Surāqa al-Ḍamrī—or al-Ghifārī, or al-Thaʿlabī. Abū Mūsā mentioned him and cited, by way of Usāma ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from ʿAwf ibn Surāqa, from his brother, who said: I said to the Messenger of God ﷺ, while he was setting out for Uḥud, ‘I was told that you will be killed tomorrow.’ He replied, ‘Is not all of time tomorrow?’ Abū Mūsā said: They have mentioned Juʿayl ibn Surāqa, and I do not know whether he is this man, whose name was diminutivized, or someone else. I say: he may be his brother. Al-Wāqidī transmitted in al-Maghāzī, by way of al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriya, who said: We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ at Tabūk when Jaʿāl ibn Surāqa and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal appeared, and the three of us used to remain close to him; then he mentioned a story. Mūsā ibn ʿUqba mentioned in al-Maghāzī, concerning the expedition of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq: Among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ was a man called Jaʿāl, whom they claimed was one of Banū Thaʿlaba, and a man of Banū Ghifār called Jahjāh. Their voices rose; then he mentioned a lengthy story. Ibn Isḥāq said in al-Maghāzī: When the Messenger of God ﷺ campaigned against Banū al-Muṣṭaliq in Shaʿbān of the year six, he appointed Jaʿāl al-Ḍamrī over Medina. This differs from Mūsā ibn ʿUqba’s statement that he accompanied them on the expedition against Banū al-Muṣṭaliq. To reconcile the two, it is necessary to say that they were two men.

## Source unit 1157 · printed entry 1158

### English candidate

Jaʿāl the Abyssinian. Ibn Shāhīn transmitted, with a weak chain, by way of al-Aʿmash, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said, ‘Messenger of God, tell me: if I fight before you until I am killed, will my Lord admit me to Paradise and not hold me in contempt?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ The man said, ‘But how, when I am foul-smelling and black in color?’ The report states that he was martyred. Abū Mūsā, after mentioning him without a lineage, said: I do not know whether he is that man—meaning Ibn Surāqa—or someone else. Ibn al-Athīr said: Rather, he is someone else. I say: al-Ṣaffār mentioned him in the Book of Genealogies and called him ‘the Abyssinian’; thus it became clear that he is someone else. والله أعلم.

## Source unit 1158 · printed entry 1159

### English candidate

Al-Jaʿd ibn Qays al-Murādī, the poet, one of Banū Ghuṭayf. Abū Saʿd al-Nīsābūrī transmitted his report in the Book of the Nobility of al-Muṣṭafā. He said: Al-Jaʿd ibn Qays, who had reached one hundred years of age, said: Four of us set out intending the pilgrimage in the Age of Ignorance. We passed through one of Yemen’s valleys. When night approached, we sought the protection of the valley’s mighty one and hobbled our mounts. When the night grew still and my companions slept, a caller from one quarter of the valley said:

‘O encamped riders, convey—
when you stand at the Ḥaṭīm and Zamzam—
our greeting to Muḥammad, the emissary from among us,
which accompanies him wherever he journeys or sets his course.
Tell him that we are followers of your religion;
with that the Messiah, son of Mary, charged us.’

Then he related the report at length, including the story of his conversion.

## Source unit 1161 · printed entry 1162

### English candidate

Jaʿda ibn Hubayra al-Ashjaʿī, a Kufan. Yazīd al-Azdī narrated from him, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: ‘The best people are my generation.’ His hadith is with Idrīs and Dāwūd, the two sons of Yazīd al-Awdī, from their father, from him. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr transmitted it thus, as a separate notice from Jaʿda ibn Hubayra al-Makhzūmī. Ibn al-Athīr said: It is most likely that he is the same man, because ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs narrated this hadith from his father, from his grandfather, from Jaʿda ibn Hubayra al-Makhzūmī. I say: Yet I have not seen any of those who transmitted it call him al-Ashjaʿī. Ibn Abī Shayba, Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ, Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim, al-Baghawī, al-Bāwardī, Ibn Qāniʿ, al-Ṭabarānī, and al-Ḥākim transmitted it under the notice of Jaʿda ibn Hubayra al-Makhzūmī. In Ibn Abī Shayba’s Muṣannaf it reads ‘Jaʿda ibn Hubayra ibn Abī Wahb,’ and this is the Makhzūmī. It is therefore as though Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr erred by making him someone else. Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned that his father related this hadith to them in the notice of Jaʿda al-Makhzūmī among the single-report narrators, and said that Jaʿda was a Successor.

## Source unit 1164 · printed entry 1165

### English candidate

Jaʿsham al-Khayr ibn Khalība ibn Shājī ibn Mawhab al-Ṣadafī. He pledged allegiance beneath the Tree. The Prophet ﷺ clothed him in his shirt and sandals and gave him some of his hair. Jaʿsham married Āmina bint Ṭalīq ibn Sufyān ibn Umayya before al-Sharīd ibn Mālik. Abū ʿUmar’s text instead says that al-Sharīd killed him during the apostasy wars, after the killing of ʿUkkāsha. Ibn Yūnus, however, said in the History of Egypt that Jaʿsham witnessed the conquest of Egypt; he therefore could not have been killed in the apostasy wars, which preceded that conquest. Ibn Mākūlā’s wording—‘he married Āmina bint Ṭalīq before al-Sharīd ibn Mālik’—is nearer to the truth. Thus ‘he killed him’ appears to be a scribal corruption of ‘before him,’ and both the resulting pronoun and the phrase ‘during the apostasy’ are errors.

## Source unit 1166 · printed entry 1167

### English candidate

Jaʿfar ibn Abī Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim. Ibn Saʿd said: The members of his household mentioned that he witnessed Ḥunayn, lived into Muʿāwiya’s time, and died in the middle of his reign. Ibn Shāhīn likewise mentioned it from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, from his authorities, and added that Jaʿfar remained constantly with the Messenger of God ﷺ, together with his father, until the Prophet died. Abū Nuʿaym thought that Ibn Mandah alone had reported this and objected that it was an error, and that the one who witnessed Ḥunayn was Jaʿfar’s father Abū Sufyān. Yet Abū Nuʿaym has no proof for that. Ibn Ḥibbān stated decisively that Jaʿfar embraced Islam with his father and witnessed Ḥunayn. He said that Jaʿfar’s mother was Ḥamāma bint Abī Ṭālib and that he died in Damascus in the year fifty. Al-Juʿābī said in his book on those who narrated from the Prophet ﷺ—both a man and his father: Jaʿfar ibn Abī Sufyān met the Prophet ﷺ together with his father at al-Abwāʾ, and he embraced Islam. In the notice of his father Abū Sufyān it will come that when his father sought permission to enter upon the Prophet ﷺ and was not admitted, he said: ‘If he does not admit me, I shall take this son of mine by the hand and we shall wander through the land.’ Abū al-Yaqẓān said: Jaʿfar left no descendants.

## Source unit 1167 · printed entry 1168

### English candidate

Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, the paternal cousin of the Prophet ﷺ, one of the earliest to embrace Islam, and the full brother of ʿAlī. Ibn Isḥāq said that he embraced Islam after twenty-five men; it is also said, after thirty-one. They said that the Prophet ﷺ established brotherhood between him and Muʿādh ibn Jabal. Abū Hurayra used to say that he was the best of people after the Prophet ﷺ. In al-Bukhārī, Abū Hurayra said: ‘Jaʿfar was the best of people to the poor.’ Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ related from ʿIkrima: I heard Abū Hurayra say, ‘No one who put on sandals, rode mounts, or trod the earth after the Messenger of God ﷺ was better than Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib.’ Al-Tirmidhī and al-Nasāʾī transmitted it, and its chain is sound. Al-Baghawī transmitted, by way of al-Maqburī, from Abū Hurayra, who said: Jaʿfar loved the poor, sat with them, served them, and they served him; thus the Messenger of God ﷺ used to give him the kunya Abū al-Masākīn. The Prophet ﷺ told him, ‘You resemble me in appearance and character.’ Al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmitted this by way of the hadith of al-Barāʾ. In the Musnad, in a marfūʿ report of ʿAlī, is: ‘I have been given noble companions’; Jaʿfar was mentioned among them. He emigrated to Abyssinia, and the Negus and those who followed him embraced Islam at his hands. Jaʿfar remained with him, then emigrated from there to Medina and arrived while the Prophet ﷺ was at Khaybar. All of this is famous in the campaign literature through multiple sound reports. Al-Baghawī and Ibn al-Sakan transmitted, by way of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: When Jaʿfar and his companions arrived, the Messenger of God ﷺ received him and kissed him between the eyes. Ibn al-Sakan transmitted, by way of Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, who said: Whenever I asked ʿAlī for something and he refused, I would adjure him by Jaʿfar’s right, and he would give it to me. Jaʿfar was martyred at Muʾta in the land of Syria, advancing and not retreating, fighting the Byzantines, during the life of the Prophet ﷺ, in the year eight, in Jumādā I. He was ten years older than ʿAlī; he thus completed forty years and, according to the correct view, exceeded them. Ibn Isḥāq said: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr related to me, from his father: My foster father, one of Banū Murra ibn ʿAwf, related to me, saying: ‘By God, it is as though I am looking at Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib on the day of Muʾta. He leapt down from his roan mare and hamstrung it, then advanced and fought until he was killed.’ Abū Dāwūd transmitted it by this route. Ibn Isḥāq said: He was the first to hamstring his mount in Islam. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted from the hadith of Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I was with them on that expedition. We searched for Jaʿfar and found on the front of his body more than ninety wounds, between thrusts and shots. The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘I saw Jaʿfar flying in Paradise with the angels.’ Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted that from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās. Also in al-Ṭabarānī, by way of Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, he said: The Prophet ﷺ was shown Jaʿfar as an angel with two wings stained in blood, because he fought until his hands were severed. In an authentic report, when Ibn ʿUmar greeted ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar he would say, ‘Peace be upon you, son of the one with two wings.’ Al-Dāraquṭnī transmitted in the Gharāʾib of Mālik, with a weak chain, from Mālik, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ when he raised his head to the sky and said, ‘And upon you be peace, the mercy of God, and His blessings.’ The people asked, ‘Messenger of God, what were you doing?’ He replied, ‘Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib passed by me amid a company of angels and greeted me.’ In the fourth part of the Fawāʾid of Abū Sahl ibn Ziyād al-Qaṭṭān, by way of Saʿdān ibn al-Walīd, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: While the Messenger of God ﷺ was sitting and Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays was near him, he said, ‘Asmāʾ, this is Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib. He has passed by with Gabriel and Michael, so return the greeting عليه السلام (“peace be upon him”) to him.’ The report continues, including: God compensated him for his two hands with two wings by which he flies wherever He wills. Ibn Isḥāq said in al-Maghāzī: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim related to me, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: When news of Jaʿfar’s death came, we recognized grief in the face of the Messenger of God ﷺ. When Ḥassān ibn Thābit learned of the killing of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa, he elegized the people of Muʾta in a poem:

‘I saw the best of the believers come in succession
to Death—Shaʿūb—while I was left among those delayed.
May God not cast far away the slain who fell one after another
at Muʾta; among them was Jaʿfar, the one with two wings,
and Zayd and ʿAbd Allāh, when all three followed one another,
while the causes of death flashed about.’

He also says in it:

‘In Jaʿfar we used to see, from Muḥammad,
fidelity and resolute command wherever he was commanded.
May there never cease in Islam, from the house of Hāshim,
pillars of might that do not pass away, and a source of pride.’

## Source unit 1171 · printed entry 1172

### English candidate

Jaʿūna ibn Naḍla al-Anṣārī. He is mentioned in accounts of the conquests. Ibn Jarīr transmitted in the History, and al-Bāwardī in the Companions, by way of Abū Maʿrūf ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿrūf, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Anṣārī, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that when Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ conquered Ḥulwān in Iraq, the Muslims went out. Among them was a man of the Anṣār called Jaʿūna ibn Naḍla. He passed through a mountain defile when the time for prayer had arrived; then he related the report at length, in the story of Zurayb ibn Tharmalī, the trustee of Jesus son of Mary. This chain is weak. We shall give the course of the story by al-Bāwardī’s route in the notice of Zurayb, إن شاء الله تعالى. In Ibn Abī Ḥātim’s al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl it says: “Jaʿūna ibn Naḍla, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ; Qatāda narrated from him. I heard my father say it.” The corruption in this is not hidden. The story has another connected route, also with a weak chain, by way of Nāfiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar, but in it the man is called Naḍla ibn Muʿāwiya al-Anṣārī. Another route, by way of Manṣūr ibn Dīnār from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Hudhayl, says: “Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ dispatched Naḍla ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī,” as will also come later.

## Source unit 1173 · printed entry 1174

### English candidate

Juʿayl ibn Surāqa al-Ḍamrī. Some of what has been related about him preceded in the notice of Juʿāl ibn Surāqa. Ibn Isḥāq transmitted in the Maghāzī from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, who said: It was said, “Messenger of God, you gave ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn and al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis one hundred each, yet left Juʿayl.” He said, “By Him in whose hand is my soul, Juʿayl ibn Surāqa is better than an earth-full of the likes of ʿUyayna and al-Aqraʿ. I am conciliating the two of them, while I entrust Juʿayl to his faith.” This is a fair mursal report, but it has a connected corroboration. Al-Rūyānī transmitted in his Musnad, and Ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam in Futūḥ Miṣr, by way of Bakr ibn Sawāda, from Abū Sālim al-Jayshānī, from Abū Dharr, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said to him, “What do you think of Juʿayl?” I said, “A poor man, like others of his sort.” He said, “And what do you think of so-and-so?” I said, “A chief among chiefs.” He said, “Juʿayl is better than an earth-full of this man.” I said, “Messenger of God, if so-and-so is like that, why do you treat him as you do?” He said, “He is the head of his people, so I conciliate them.” Its chain is sound. Ibn Ḥibbān transmitted it by another route from Abū Dharr but did not name Juʿayl. Al-Bukhārī transmitted it from the report of Sahl ibn Saʿd, leaving both Juʿayl and Abū Dharr unnamed. Ibn Mandah transmitted, by way of Yaʿqūb ibn ʿUtba, from ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn ʿAwf, from Surāqa, from his father, who said: “My brother Juʿayl’s eye was injured during Banū Qurayẓa.”

## Source unit 1174 · printed entry 1175

### English candidate

Juʿayl, without a lineage. Abū Mūsā distinguished him from the preceding man. Ibn Isḥāq transmitted in the Maghāzī from Yazīd ibn Rūmān, from ʿUrwa, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ dug the Trench, he divided the people into groups and worked alongside them. Among them was a man called Juʿayl, whom he renamed ʿAmr. One of them chanted:

“He named him ʿAmr after Juʿayl;
one day he was a support to the wretched.”

Whenever they said “ʿAmr,” the Messenger of God ﷺ said, “ʿAmr”; and whenever they said “support,” he said, “support.”

## Source unit 1175 · printed entry 1176

### English candidate

Jafshīsh ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Kindī. Thus Ibn Mandah named his father. He said that his name is also given as Maʿdān, with the kunya Abū al-Khayr, and as Jarīr ibn Maʿdān. Some recensions have Khafshīsh, with a dotted khāʾ. Abū ʿUmar likewise said it is reported with jīm and the dotted letter; he added that it is also reported with the undotted letter. Its first letter is recorded with both kasra and ḍamma. Ibn al-Kalbī and Ibn Saʿd said his name was Maʿdān ibn al-Aswad ibn Maʿdīkarib ibn Thumāma ibn al-Aswad. Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr mentioned, by way of Mujālid from al-Shaʿbī, that al-Ashʿath ibn Qays said: “There was a land dispute between a man of ours and a man of the Ḥaḍramīs called al-Jafshīsh”—and he related the report. The report’s basis is in Sunan Abī Dāwūd, through Muslim ibn Hayḍam from al-Ashʿath, but it does not name al-Jafshīsh. Abū ʿUmar also transmitted, by way of Ibn ʿAwn from al-Shaʿbī, from Jarīr ibn Maʿdān—who was nicknamed al-Jafshīsh—that he brought a dispute with a man before the Prophet ﷺ; then he related the report. I say: On its face, this makes Jarīr the name of al-Jafshīsh and makes him the Companion, which is strange. It is possible that the pronoun in “who was nicknamed” refers to Maʿdān, Jarīr’s father, so that the report is Jarīr’s narration from his father, sent without a Companion link. This is nearer to the correct view in my judgment. Abū Saʿd al-Naysābūrī mentioned, by way of Maslama ibn Muḥārib from al-Suddī, from Abū Mālik, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The kings of Ḥaḍramawt arrived, and a delegation of Kinda came in which was al-Ashʿath ibn Qays. He related the story, then said that al-Jafshīsh—whose name was Maʿdān ibn al-Aswad al-Kindī—said concerning it:

“The white camels brought us from the Arabs of Yemen,
descending low with us after highland travel,
until we made them kneel beside the hill, coming from Malal,
before the trustworthy, truthful, guiding Messenger.”

Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted by way of Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥayy, from al-Jafshīsh al-Kindī, who said: A group from Kinda came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said, “You are one of us,” claiming him as theirs. He said, “We do not cast aspersions on our mother, nor disown our father.” Al-Ṭabarānī has another route from Ṣāliḥ: “Al-Jafshīsh told us”—which is an error, for he did not meet him. The report’s basis is in the Musnad of Aḥmad, in Muslim ibn Hayḍam’s narration from al-Ashʿath: “I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ in a company from Kinda”; it does not mention al-Jafshīsh. Abū ʿUmar mentioned the like from ʿImrān ibn Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥa, from al-Jafshīsh, and that too is mursal. Ibn al-Kalbī mentioned him without a chain and said that he repeated that claim three times and was answered on the third. Al-Ashʿath then said to him, “May God smash your mouth! Why did you not stop after twice?” He said that al-Jafshīsh is the one who said during the apostasy:

“We obeyed the Messenger of God when he was truthful;
how strange is what befell the rule of Abū Bakr!”

I say: Al-Mubarrad recited this verse in al-Kāmil as al-Ḥuṭayʾa’s, with “present” instead of “truthful” and “alas” instead of “how strange.” ʿUmar ibn Shabba mentioned that al-Jafshīsh apostatized among Kinda, was taken prisoner, and was killed in captivity. If that is sound, he has no Companionship, and every narration from him is mursal, because its transmitters did not live in that period. والله أعلم.

## Source unit 1176 · printed entry 1177

### English candidate

Jufayna al-Juhanī; he is also said to be al-Nahdī, and he is called al-Ghassānī. Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned him from his father. Al-Baghawī and al-Ṭabarānī transmitted, by way of Abū Bakr al-Zāhirī, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿUrayna, from Jufayna, that the Prophet ﷺ wrote him a letter, which he used to patch his bucket. His daughter said to him, “You took the letter of the lord of the Arabs and patched your bucket with it!” He fled, and every possession of his, small and great, was taken. He then came later as a Muslim. The Prophet ﷺ said to him, “Look for any of your property that you find before the shares are divided and take it.” Al-Baghawī said: “It is rejected as a report of al-Thawrī, and Abū Bakr al-Zāhirī is weak in hadith.” I say: The report came to us by his route with a short chain in the second of al-ʿĪsawī’s Fawāʾid. Isrāʾīl—one of the firmest transmitters from Abū Isḥāq—transmitted it from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Shaʿbī, that the Prophet ﷺ wrote to Riʿya al-Suḥaymī; then he gave it at length. Its corroboration is the narration of Ḥammād ibn Salama from Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh, from Abū Isḥāq, except that it says Riʿya al-Juhanī and does not mention al-Shaʿbī. It will come correctly under the letter rāʾ, إن شاء الله تعالى.

## Source unit 1177 · printed entry 1178

### English candidate

Al-Jullās ibn Suwayd ibn al-Ṣāmit al-Anṣārī. He was among the hypocrites, then he repented and his repentance was good. Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī said in his Maghāzī: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq transmitted to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ arrived, my people came to me and said, “You are a poet. If you wish, offer the Messenger of God ﷺ some excuse.” He then related at length the report of Kaʿb ibn Mālik’s repentance, until he said: Among the hypocrites who stayed behind and about whom the Qurʾan was revealed was al-Jullās ibn Suwayd ibn al-Ṣāmit. He was the husband of Umm ʿUmayr ibn Saʿd, and ʿUmayr was in his care. ʿUmayr heard him say, “If Muḥammad is truthful, we are worse than donkeys.” He then related the story that passed between them and the revelation of God’s saying, “They swear by God that they did not say [it]” through His saying, “If they repent, it will be better for them” [Qurʾan 9:74]. They claimed that al-Jullās repented and that his repentance was good. I say: Al-Umawī inserted the story of al-Jullās into the story of Kaʿb’s repentance; Kaʿb’s report ended before it. Ibn Hishām confined himself to Kaʿb’s story and did not mention the story of al-Jullās. Al-Wāqidī gave it at length from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jaʿfar, from his father. At its end it says: Al-Jullās repented, and his repentance was good; he never ceased the good he used to do for ʿUmayr, and by that his repentance was recognized. Al-ʿUdhrī related that al-Jullās was the one who killed al-Mujadhdhar in revenge for his father, Suwayd ibn al-Ṣāmit. He said: The correct view is that the one who killed al-Mujadhdhar was al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd, as will come.

Jullās ibn Ṣulayt al-Yarbūʿī. Ibn al-Sakan and Ibn Shāhīn transmitted, by way of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Jabala, who said: Murrār daughter of Mundhir al-Ṣulaytiyya told us: “My mother, Umm Mundhir daughter of al-Jullās ibn Ṣulayt al-Yarbūʿī, told me, from her father, who said: I said, ‘Messenger of God, I possess much wealth, standing, and a clan. He said: The descendants of al-Jullās attained a great station in Islam. Ibn Mandah cited, by this same route from al-Jullās, that he came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about ablution. He said, “One washing suffices, and two—” He said: “I saw him perform ablution three times for each limb.” Ibn Mandah said: “Singular; it is known only through this route.” End. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān is abandoned in hadith. I say: I saw Murrār vocalized thus in Ibn Shāhīn’s book and in a reliable copy of Ibn al-Sakan’s book, with ḍamma, without gemination, and ending in dāl; in other copies it ends in rāʾ. والله أعلم.

## Source unit 1180 · printed entry 1181

### English candidate

Julaybīb, without a lineage; the name is a diminutive of jilbāb. Muslim transmitted, in a report of Ḥammād from Thābit, from Kināna ibn Nuʿaym, from Abū Barza al-Aslamī, that the Prophet ﷺ was on one of his campaigns and God granted him spoils. He said, “Are you missing anyone?” They said, “We are missing so-and-so and so-and-so.” He said, “But I am missing Julaybīb.” He then related the report. Al-Nasāʾī also transmitted it. Julaybīb is mentioned in Anas’s report about the Prophet marrying him to an Anṣārī woman, including his saying ﷺ, “Yet in God’s sight you are not without worth.” It is also in al-Barqānī’s Mustakhraj within the report of Abū Barza. Aḥmad transmitted it at length. Al-Bazzār transmitted the report of Anas at length by way of ʿAbd al-Razzāq from Maʿmar, from Thābit, from him; Aḥmad also transmitted it from ʿAbd al-Razzāq. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr related in Julaybīb’s notice that concerning his story was revealed: “It is not for a believing man or woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in their affair” [Qurʾan 33:36]. I have not seen that claim in any connected route, whether from Anas or from Abū Barza.

جليبيب غير منسوب وهو تصغير جلباب روى مسلم من حديث حماد عن ثابت عن كنانة بن نعيم عن أبي برزة الأسلمي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان في مغزى له فأفاء الله فقال هل تفقدون من أحد قالوا فقدنا فلانا وفلانا قال ولكني أفقد جليبيبا فذكر الحديث وأخرجه النسائي وله ذكر في حديث أنس في تزوجيه بالأنصارية وفيه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لكنك عند الله لست بكاسد وهو عند البرقاني في مستخرجه في حديث أبي برزة أيضا وقد أخرجه أحمد مطولا وحديث أنس أخرجه البزار من طريق عبد الرزاق عن معمر عن ثابت عنه مطولا وأخرجه أحمد عن عبد الرزاق وحكى بن عبد البر في ترجمته أنه نزل في قصته وما كان لمؤمن ولا مؤمنة إذا قضى الله ورسوله أمرا أن يكون لهم الخيرة من أمرهم الآية ولم أر ذلك في شيء من طرقه الموصولة من حديث أنس ومن حديث أبي برزة

Jamra ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Hawdha ibn Mālik ibn Samʿān al-ʿUdhrī. Ibn al-Kalbī said that he was the first person to bring the alms of Banū ʿUdhra to the Prophet ﷺ. Abū Ḥātim said that he came with the delegation of ʿUdhra. Al-Ṭabarī said that he was chief of Banū ʿUdhra and came as a delegate to the Prophet ﷺ, bringing him their alms. Ibn al-Kalbī said that he was the first of the people of the Ḥijāz to come to the Messenger of God ﷺ with his people’s alms. The Prophet ﷺ granted him from Wādī al-Qurā as much land as his horse could cover at a gallop and as far as he could cast his whip. He settled there until he died. Ibn Shāhīn mentioned him, but entered him under the undotted ḥāʾ. Al-Wāqidī said: Shuʿayb ibn Maymūn told us, from Abū Marāya al-Balawī, who heard Ḥamza ibn al-Nuʿmān al-ʿUdhrī—who had Companionship—say: “The Messenger of God ﷺ ordered that hair and blood be buried.” Al-Dāraquṭnī transmitted it in al-Muʾtalif by al-Wāqidī’s route. “Praise be to God, the Majestic, Lord of favors!

## Source unit 1192 · printed entry 1193

### English candidate

Jamīl ibn Usayd al-Fihrī, whose kunya was Abū Maʿmar and whose epithet was Dhū al-Qalbayn, ‘the Man with Two Hearts.’ Al-Farrāʾ named him in Maʿānī al-Qurʾān. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said: ʿUmar ibn Abī Bakr al-Mawṣilī related to us, from Zakariyyā ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: Dhū al-Qalbayn was of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Fihr. He was Abū Maʿmar, the man who informed Quraysh of ʿUmar’s acceptance of Islam. Muqātil said in his commentary, concerning the Most High’s words, ‘God has not placed two hearts within any man,’ that they were revealed concerning Abū Maʿmar al-Fihrī. Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād al-Shāmī said the same. He was among the most intelligent and retentive of the Arabs. Abū Zakariyyā al-Farrāʾ said in Maʿānī al-Qurʾān: They were revealed concerning Abū Maʿmar, Jamīl ibn Usayd. The people of Mecca used to say that Abū Maʿmar had two hearts and two minds in his breast because of the strength of his memory. Al-Wāḥidī also mentioned him in Asbāb al-Nuzūl. Ibn Durayd, however, said that his name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb. Al-Suhaylī attributed the epithet instead to the Jamīl ibn Maʿmar who will appear later. The well-known and preferred view is that Jamīl ibn Usayd was a different man from Jamīl ibn Maʿmar. والله أعلم.

## Source unit 1195 · printed entry 1196

### English candidate

Jamīl ibn Maʿmar ibn Ḥabīb ibn Wahb ibn Ḥudhāfa ibn Jumaḥ al-Jumaḥī. Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Mubarrad said in al-Kāmil that he had Companionship and was especially close to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. There was no genealogical relationship between him and the famous poet Jamīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿmar al-ʿUdhrī, the companion of Buthayna. He was the man who informed Quraysh of ʿUmar’s acceptance of Islam, as related in Ibn Isḥāq’s Sīra from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: When my father embraced Islam, he asked, ‘Which Qurashī carries news most quickly?’ He was told, ‘Jamīl ibn Maʿmar al-Jumaḥī.’ He informed Jamīl of his conversion and asked him to keep it secret, but Jamīl called out at the top of his voice, ‘ʿUmar has become a Ṣābiʾ!’—and the story continues. Jamīl later embraced Islam, witnessed Ḥunayn, and killed Zuhayr ibn al-Abjar in a famous episode. Abū Khirāsh al-Hudhalī elegized Zuhayr in well-known verses. Al-Mubarrad said in al-Kāmil that Jamīl ibn Maʿmar witnessed the Conquest—the conquest of Mecca—and killed there a brother of Abū Khirāsh al-Hudhalī. Ibn Yūnus said that Jamīl witnessed the conquest of Egypt and died during ʿUmar’s time; ʿUmar grieved intensely for him. I think that when he died he was nearly one hundred, for he witnessed the Sacrilegious War as an adult. His father was one of the senior Companions, as will come later. Al-Zubayr said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb came to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and heard him singing in the naṣb style:

‘How can I remain in Medina after
Jamīl ibn Maʿmar has fulfilled his term there?’

He asked, ‘What is this, Abū Muḥammad?’ ʿAbd al-Raḥmān replied, ‘When we are alone, we say what people say.’ Al-Mubarrad mentioned this story but made ʿUmar the one who was singing. والله أعلم.

## Source unit 1197 · printed entry 1198

### English candidate

Janāb ibn Ḥāritha ibn Ṣakhr ibn Mālik ibn ʿAbd Manāt al-ʿUdhrī. Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī mentioned him in al-Muʿammarīn, saying: Ḥāritha lived into Islam but did not embrace it. His son Janāb embraced Islam and emigrated to Medina, and his father was deeply distressed by that. Abū Ḥātim mentioned poetry by him on the matter, including:

‘When the doves call upon the branches,
streams of my tears pour forth.
The doves remind me of the pure delight of my life—
Janāb; who will excuse me against Janāb?
You sought your Lord’s reward in parting from me,
yet kinship would have been nearer to reward.’

These verses resemble the verses of Umayya ibn al-Askar about his son Kilāb. Their language may suggest that Ḥāritha embraced Islam, despite the prose report to the contrary.

## Source unit 1202 · printed entry 1203

### English candidate

Junāda ibn Abī Umayya al-Azdī. Aḥmad, al-Nasāʾī, and al-Baghawī transmitted, by way of Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Abū al-Khayr, from Ḥudhayfa al-Bāriqī, from Junāda ibn Abī Umayya al-Azdī, that eight men entered upon the Messenger of God ﷺ, Junāda being the eighth. He brought food near to them on Friday—and the hadith concerns the prohibition of fasting on Friday. Some narrators said ‘Junāda al-Azdī’ and did not say ‘ibn Abī Umayya.’ Aḥmad also transmitted, by way of Yazīd, from Abū al-Khayr, that Junāda ibn Abī Umayya related to him that some men among the Companions said, ‘Migration has ceased.’ They disagreed about it, so I went to the Prophet ﷺ, who said, ‘Migration does not cease so long as jihad continues.’ Ibn Yūnus mentioned him in the History of Egypt, saying that he witnessed the conquest of Egypt and that its people narrated from him. Among the reports indicating his Companionship, there is no narration from him by anyone other than the Egyptians. Al-Ṭabarānī did, however, transmit with a weak chain from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ṣanʿānī, that Junāda al-Azdī led a group in prayer. The report includes: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, ‘Whoever leads a people while they dislike him, his prayer does not rise beyond his collarbone.’ Al-Ṭabarānī placed it in the notice of this Junāda. The first two reports are sound and demonstrate the validity of his Companionship. In my view, his father’s name has not been established soundly. Ibn al-Sakan, in the notice of Junāda ibn Mālik al-Azdī, transmitted the hadith given at the beginning of the notice of Junāda ibn Abī Umayya; Ibn Mandah and Abū Nuʿaym followed him. What appears correct is that this was an error. والله أعلم. Ibn Saʿd, Abū Ḥātim, Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, and others distinguished Junāda ibn Abī Umayya al-Azdī from Junāda ibn Mālik al-Azdī. ʿAbd al-Ghanī ibn Surūr al-Maqdisī objected to Abū Nuʿaym’s combining them, and I have mentioned his predecessor in that view. There was also another Junāda ibn Abī Umayya whose father’s name was Kabīr, with bāʾ. He was a mukhaḍram who lived through both eras and encountered the Prophet ﷺ. The Two Shaykhs and others transmitted for him from his narration from ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit. He settled in Syria and died there in the year sixty-seven. Al-ʿIjlī said of him: ‘A trustworthy Successor, one of the senior Successors.’ Ibn Ḥibbān said in the Successors: ‘Companionship is not soundly established for him.’ Ibn Saʿd, Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān, and Ibn Jarīr mentioned him in their books on the Successors. Ibn Abī Ḥātim reported from his father: ‘Junāda al-Azdī had Companionship. Al-Layth narrated from Yazīd, from Ḥudhayfa al-Azdī, from him.’ I say: This is the subject of the notice; he did not mention his father’s name.

### Arabic authority

<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">

## Source unit 1204 · printed entry 1205

### English candidate

Junāda ibn Jarād al-ʿAylānī al-Bāhilī. Al-Dāraquṭnī transmitted in al-Muʾtalif, as did Ibn al-Sakan and Ibn Shāhīn, by way of Ziyād ibn Qurayʿ, one of Banū ʿAylān ibn Jaʾwa, from his father Qurayʿ, from Junāda—reported in this chain as Junāda ibn Junāda ibn Jarād—one of Banū ʿAylān ibn Jaʾwa ibn Maʿn, who said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ with my camels after branding them on their noses. He said, ‘Could you find no limb on them to brand except the face?’—and the hadith continues. Ibn al-Sakan said: I know of no other narration from him, and his chain is not known. I say: al-Rashāṭī vocalized al-ʿAylānī with the unpointed consonant and said that he was of ʿAylān of Bāhila. Ibn Mākūlā and Ibn Nuqṭa omitted this nisba in their works on confusable nisbas. Ibn Mākūlā did, however, mention ʿAylān and Ghaylān. He said that the form with the pointed consonant is common, while the form with the unpointed consonant is Qays ʿAylān; he mentioned the disagreement over why Qays was annexed to ʿAylān.
